verified_symbols.name: Skill
verified_symbols.doc:
One job, and the tools it needs.

Attributes:
    name: snake_case identifier, matching :data:`SKILL_NAME_PATTERN`.
    description: One sentence, what the skill ACCOMPLISHES -- not what its
        tools are named. Goes in front of a model choosing between skills.
    when_to_use: Prose guidance for that choice. The reason a skill beats a
        bare tool list: it can say "use this before simulating anything" in
        a way a function signature cannot.
    tools: Registry tool names, e.g. ``sim_simulate_structure``. Validated
        against the live tool registry at registration.
    profiles: The agent profiles whose system prompt describes this skill
        (:data:`KNOWN_PROFILES`). A skill's prompt text names tools, and a
        prompt must never name a tool its profile does not bind -- so a
        skill whose tools are served only in Calibration mode is rendered
        only there.

verified_symbols.doc:

Delegates to the module-level :func:`render_prompt_section`, which

verified_symbols.name: AgentState
verified_symbols.doc:
State threaded through the supervisor graph.

Attributes:
    messages: The full conversation, including tool calls, tool results,
        and model responses. Uses LangGraph's ``add_messages`` reducer,
        so nodes return only the NEW messages to append, not the whole
        accumulated list -- or, to REPLACE one in place, the same message
        under its original ``id``, which is how the supervisor node's
        attachment trim persists (see
        :mod:`forge.agents.message_trimming`). This channel is a full
        snapshot per graph step, so anything left in it is re-serialised
        on every step; that is why raw image/PDF blocks do not survive
        past the turn they arrived on.
    run_id: Unique identifier for this agent run (for tracing).
    user_id: Optional user identifier (for tracing context).
    start_time: Timestamp when the run started (for duration calculation).
    tool_times: Dictionary mapping tool names to their execution times.

verified_symbols.name: _supervisor_node
verified_symbols.doc: Call the model with bound tools on the current conversation.

verified_symbols.name: _should_continue
verified_symbols.doc: Route to sub-agents if the last message requested tool calls, else end.

verified_symbols.name: _call_key
verified_symbols.doc: A stable identity for one tool call, for repeat detection.

verified_symbols.name: _already_called
verified_symbols.doc:
Map every tool call already made THIS RUN to what it returned.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Measured 2026-09-14 on vllm:qwen3.8-27b, the question
"reduce the measured GISAXS frame from sample 12" -- naming a sample the
catalog does not hold -- produced 29 tool calls in 204 s and no answer. The
agent read "No datasets match your search criteria." as "try a different
spelling" and worked through `sample 12`, `12`, `sample12`, `S12`, recent
datasets and distinct values, re-calling the same tools with the same
arguments along the way. It ran until LangGraph's recursion limit stopped
it. Nothing else would have.

The loop is read back out of the message history rather than carried in
state, so it costs no new state field and works for a resumed thread too.

TURN-SCOPED, not thread-scoped. The thrash above happened inside one run.
Across turns the SAME call can legitimately mean something new: the
Scattering workbench binds a tool's frame and ring arguments from what the
user has selected, so ``index_crystal_peaks({})`` on frame B in turn two is
a different measurement from the identical-looking call on frame A in turn
one. Refusing it with turn one's answer would report frame A as frame B.

verified_symbols.name: _discovery_calls
verified_symbols.doc: How many data-catalog lookups this run has already made.

verified_symbols.name: _over_discovery_budget
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether this call is one search too many.

Measured: 71% of benchmark runs opened with a catalog call whatever the
question was, and the tools that do the real work were reached 6% (analysis)
and 22% (sim) of the time because the budget was gone first.

verified_symbols.name: _execute_tools_node
verified_symbols.doc:
Execute tools through their respective sub-agents or directly.

For each tool call in the last message, either:
1. Call the tool directly if it was passed to build_supervisor_graph
2. Route to the appropriate sub-agent if it's a registry tool with a domain prefix

Supports both registry-prefixed tool names (domain_verb_object) and
legacy tool names (verb_object).

Args:
    state: The agent state containing messages and run context.
    tool_map: Mapping of tool names to tool objects.
    tracer: Optional Langfuse tracer for observability.

Returns:
    Dictionary with "messages" (tool results) and optionally "tool_times".
verified_symbols.signature: state: AgentState, tool_map: dict[str, Any], tracer: LangfuseTracer | None=None

verified_symbols.name: build_supervisor_graph
verified_symbols.doc:
Build a compiled supervisor graph coordinating sub-agents.

Args:
    model: A chat model. Must support ``.bind_tools()`` (all
        LangChain-integrated chat models do); this function binds
        ``tools`` to it internally.
    tools: The tools available to the agent. The supervisor uses these
        to bind to the model, but actual tool execution is delegated to
        sub-agents based on tool domain or executed directly if they're
        legacy tools.
    system_prompt: Prepended to the conversation if the incoming
        messages don't already start with a SystemMessage.
    checkpointer: Optional LangGraph checkpoint saver (e.g.
        ``AsyncSqliteSaver``). When given, the compiled graph persists
        ``AgentState`` across separate invoke/astream calls that share
        the same ``config={"configurable": {"thread_id": ...}}``.
        When ``None`` (the default), each call starts from exactly the
        messages it is given, with no memory of any prior call.
    tracer: Optional Langfuse tracer for observability. When provided,
        all agent runs, tool calls, and errors are traced.

Returns:
    A compiled LangGraph graph with an ``invoke({"messages": [...]})``
    interface, looping between the supervisor model and tool execution
    through sub-agents until the model responds without requesting
    further tool calls.
verified_symbols.signature: model: BaseChatModel, tools: list[BaseTool], system_prompt: str=DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT, checkpointer: BaseCheckpointSaver | None=None, tracer: LangfuseTracer | None=None

verified_symbols.name: media_placeholder
verified_symbols.doc:
Render one dropped media block as text that names it and how to restore it.

Args:
    block: A LangChain standard data content block -- ``{"type": "image"
        | "file", "base64": ..., "mime_type": ...}`` or the ``url``
        variant.

Returns:
    A single line of text. It carries the block's kind, mime type and
    size so a reader (human or model) can tell WHICH attachment is gone,
    followed by :data:`_RESTORE_HINT`.

verified_symbols.name: strip_media_from_content
verified_symbols.doc:
Replace media blocks in one message's content with named placeholders.

Args:
    content: A message's ``content``: a plain string (returned unchanged
        -- there is nothing to strip) or a list of content blocks.

Returns:
    ``content`` itself when it holds no media block, so callers can use
    identity to detect "nothing changed". Otherwise a plain STRING: once
    the media is gone every remaining block is text, and a plain string is
    the one content shape every provider accepts. That matters here
    beyond tidiness -- a block built for whichever provider handled the
    original turn is not guaranteed valid for whichever model handles a
    later one, and replaying it was its own reported bug.

verified_symbols.name: current_turn_start
verified_symbols.doc:
Index of the message that opens the current turn.

The current turn starts at the LAST human message: everything after it
(the model's replies and its tool results) belongs to the same turn, and
everything before it is settled history.

Args:
    messages: The conversation, oldest first.

Returns:
    The index of the last human message, or ``0`` when there is none (in
    which case nothing is stale and nothing is trimmed).

verified_symbols.name: trim_stale_media
verified_symbols.doc:
Drop media from every message older than the current turn.

Args:
    messages: The conversation as held in ``AgentState["messages"]``,
        oldest first.

Returns:
    ``(for_model, replacements)``.

    ``for_model`` is the full conversation with stale media replaced --
    send this to the model instead of ``messages``.

    ``replacements`` holds ONLY the messages that actually changed, each
    keeping its original ``id`` so LangGraph's ``add_messages`` reducer
    replaces it in place rather than appending a copy. Return it from a
    node to persist the trim into the checkpoint. It is empty whenever
    there is nothing to do, so a node can return it unconditionally and a
    conversation with no attachments is untouched.

    A message with no ``id`` cannot be replaced in place (``add_messages``
    matches on id), so it is trimmed for the model but left out of
    ``replacements`` -- better a slightly larger checkpoint than a
    duplicated message, which is the exact bug this module exists to kill.

verified_symbols.name: trim_stale_tool_results
verified_symbols.doc:
Bound the tool output a long conversation carries, newest kept first.

The text counterpart to :func:`trim_stale_media`, and it exists for the same
reason at a different scale: media blew the CHECKPOINT, accumulated tool
output blows the CONTEXT WINDOW.

NEWEST-FIRST, NOT OLDEST-FIRST. Walking backwards and spending the budget on
the most recent results keeps what the model is actually reasoning about and
drops what it has already used. Trimming from the front would keep the
opening of a conversation and discard the answer it just received.

THE CURRENT TURN IS NEVER TOUCHED, whatever it costs. A turn trimmed while
it is still running would drop the result of the call the model made two
steps ago and is about to act on -- which is not a smaller answer, it is a
wrong one. Only settled history is eligible.

Args:
    messages: The conversation as held in ``AgentState["messages"]``,
        oldest first.
    budget_chars: Total characters of STALE tool output to keep.

Returns:
    ``(for_model, replacements)``, with the same contract as
    :func:`trim_stale_media` -- ``replacements`` carries each rewritten
    message under its ORIGINAL id so ``add_messages`` replaces it in place,
    and omits any message with no id rather than risk a duplicate.

verified_symbols.name: repair_orphaned_tool_calls
verified_symbols.doc:
Rewrite every tool call that never got a result, so the model can be called.

WHY. A turn's stream can end while a tool is running -- the user presses
Stop, closes the tab, or a proxy drops the SSE connection. The supervisor
step that ASKED for the tool has already been checkpointed by then, and the
step that would have answered it never commits, so the thread is left
holding ``AIMessage(tool_calls=[...])`` with no ``ToolMessage`` after it.
Every later turn on that thread resends it, and Anthropic and
OpenAI-compatible endpoints refuse a ``tool_use`` with no ``tool_result``
(HTTP 400): the conversation is dead until "Clear Memory" destroys it.
Reproduced in ``src/forge/api/tests/test_cancelled_turn_leaves_no_orphan.py``:
cancel the stream during a tool, send one more turn, and without this the
model receives ``[System, Human, AI(tool_calls), Human]``.

It cannot be cleaned up after the cancelled turn for the reason recorded in
this module's docstring: a cancelled async generator cannot run an
``await`` in its ``finally``. So, like the media trim, the repair runs
inside the next model-calling node and is committed by the same checkpoint
write as the reply.

The repaired message keeps its ``id`` (so ``add_messages`` replaces it in
place), keeps every call that DID get a result (dropping those would orphan
their results instead), and keeps its text. The unanswered calls are
removed and named in a note, so the model knows the work was asked for and
never finished -- rather than reading a conversation in which it promised a
simulation and then silently changed the subject. It is built fresh rather
than copied: ``additional_kwargs`` carries the provider's raw tool calls,
and ``langchain_openai`` resends those when ``tool_calls`` is empty.

Args:
    messages: The conversation as held in ``AgentState["messages"]``,
        oldest first.

Returns:
    ``(for_model, replacements)``, with the same contract as
    :func:`trim_stale_media`. Both are unchanged copies -- ``replacements``
    empty -- for a conversation with no orphan, which is every one whose
    turns ran to completion.

verified_symbols.doc: Count raw media blocks across a conversation. Used by tests and probes.

verified_symbols.name: CheckpointerConfig
verified_symbols.doc:
Configuration for the centralized checkpointer.

Attributes:
    db_path: Path to the SQLite checkpoint database. If None, uses the
        default path relative to this module directory.
    enable_async: Whether to use AsyncSqliteSaver (True) or synchronous
        SqliteSaver (False). Defaults to True for async support.

verified_symbols.name: compact_checkpoint_db
verified_symbols.doc:
Reclaim a bloated checkpoint database. MAINTENANCE, never automatic.

Deliberately not called on startup: ``VACUUM`` rewrites the whole file and
takes an exclusive lock, so on the 553 MB database that motivated this it
would turn every agent start into a multi-second stall -- and would do it
while another process might hold the file open.

Three steps, in this order: checkpoint the WAL into the database and
truncate it; enable incremental auto-vacuum; ``VACUUM`` to rewrite the file
without its freelist (which is also what makes the auto-vacuum setting
take effect for everything after this).

Args:
    db_path: The database to compact. Defaults to
        :func:`get_checkpoint_db_path`.

Returns:
    ``{"before_mb", "after_mb", "reclaimed_mb"}``. Sizes include the WAL.

Raises:
    FileNotFoundError: If the database does not exist.
    sqlite3.OperationalError: If another process still holds the file
        after ``COMPACTION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S`` -- a RAISE, not a log, because
        a compaction that silently did nothing would leave the caller
        believing the space was reclaimed.

verified_symbols.name: get_checkpoint_db_path
verified_symbols.doc:
Return the path for the checkpoint SQLite file.

Reads ``FORGE_CHECKPOINT_DB`` from the environment; falls back to the
default path ``.checkpoint.db`` in the module directory.

Returns:
    Path to the checkpoint database file. Parent directories are not
    created; callers must call ``.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)``.

verified_symbols.name: get_checkpointer
verified_symbols.doc:
Return the singleton AsyncSqliteSaver checkpointer.

Constructs the checkpointer on first call and caches it for all subsequent
calls, enforcing the ADR-6 single-construction-site requirement.

Args:
    config: Configuration for the checkpointer. If None, uses defaults
        (async SQLite, default database path). Ignored on subsequent calls
        (the singleton is already constructed).

Returns:
    A BaseCheckpointSaver instance (AsyncSqliteSaver by default).

Raises:
    ImportError: If ``langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite`` is not installed.

verified_symbols.name: get_async_checkpointer
verified_symbols.doc:
Return the singleton ``AsyncSqliteSaver``, creating it on first call.

Async graphs need this rather than :func:`get_checkpointer`: the synchronous
``SqliteSaver``'s async methods raise ``NotImplementedError`` by design, so
an async ``astream``/``ainvoke`` fails at the first checkpoint write.

This cannot be folded into :func:`get_checkpointer`, because
``aiosqlite`` binds its connection to the running event loop at
construction time -- there has to be one, which means an async caller.

Returns:
    The process-wide AsyncSqliteSaver.

Raises:
    ImportError: If ``langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite`` or ``aiosqlite`` is
        not installed.

verified_symbols.name: _open_async_checkpointer
verified_symbols.doc: Open, configure and cache this loop's saver. Called under its lock.

verified_symbols.name: _close_async_checkpointers
verified_symbols.doc:
Exit every entered async context manager, so its connection closes.

THE ASYNC ONES WERE BEING DROPPED, NOT CLOSED. `reset_checkpointer` used to
`.clear()` this dict and exit only the SYNC context manager below -- while
this module's own docstring claimed the manager is kept "so
reset_checkpointer() can close the connection rather than leaking it".
True of the sync saver; false of these.

What leaks is not a file handle. `AsyncSqliteSaver.__aenter__` opens an
aiosqlite connection, which starts a worker thread that is NON-DAEMON and
parks on an untimed `Queue.get()`. It exits only on the sentinel that
`close()` enqueues. Drop the manager and that sentinel is never sent, so
the thread lives until the interpreter joins it -- forever. Two autouse
fixtures call `reset_checkpointer` around EVERY test, so a suite that
touches the async path leaks one such thread per test.

Best-effort by contract: teardown must not fail a test run. Each manager is
exited on its own loop when that loop is still alive, because aiosqlite's
close is a coroutine and the connection belongs to the loop that made it;
a dead loop leaves nothing safe to do but say so.

verified_symbols.name: reset_checkpointer
verified_symbols.doc:
Reset the singleton checkpointer to None.

**For testing only.** This allows tests to construct fresh checkpointers
with different configurations or to verify the singleton pattern.

Closes what it clears -- see :func:`_close_async_checkpointers` for why
dropping an entered async manager is a thread leak rather than a tidy-up
nicety.

verified_symbols.name: tracer_from_settings
verified_symbols.doc:
Build a tracer from ``Settings``, or None when tracing is off.

THE MISSING PIECE, not a convenience. ``build_supervisor_graph`` has taken a
``tracer=`` argument since it was written and **no caller ever passed one**
-- `simulation/run.py`, `sweep.py`, `evals/runner.py` and
`api/agent_helpers.py` all omitted it -- so every ``if tracer:`` in
``graph.py`` was dead in production. Config existed, the plumbing existed,
and nothing connected them.

Returns None (rather than a disabled tracer) when Langfuse is off or
unconfigured, so callers pass the result straight through and `graph.py`'s
existing ``if tracer is not None`` guards do the rest.

Credentials come through :mod:`forge.core.secrets`, so an unknown field
name is a startup error rather than a silently empty key.

Returns:
    A configured tracer, or None.

verified_symbols.name: LangfuseTracer
verified_symbols.doc:
Wrapper around Langfuse client for agent-level observability.

This class manages tracing of:
- Agent run lifecycle (start, end, status)
- Tool invocations and results
- Token usage
- Errors and failures

Attributes:
    enabled: Whether tracing is enabled (if False, all operations are no-ops).
    _client: The underlying Langfuse client (lazy-initialized).
    _trace_urls: Cache of resolved deep-link URLs, keyed by run id.

NO SPAN OBJECTS ARE RETAINED, unlike the version this replaces, which kept
a ``_run_traces: dict[run_id, trace]`` and required
:meth:`trace_agent_run` to be called FIRST -- a tool call arriving before
it logged "creating implicit trace" and started a second, competing trace.
Trace ids are now derived from the run id by a pure hash
(``Langfuse.create_trace_id(seed=...)``, verified deterministic), so any
method can be called in any order and every span lands in the same trace.
That also makes :meth:`trace_id_for` usable with no client and no network,
which is what lets the knowledge graph record a ``langfuse_trace_id``
alongside a run.

The tool set the CLI binds: the console's, plus knowledge-graph reads.

Assembled from the four ``forge.agents`` builders rather than from
``forge.api.agent_helpers.build_agent_tools``, which is the console's own
entry point but reaches the donor's flat module layout (``import
thumbnails``) and therefore only imports under
``PYTHONPATH=src/forge/api``. A CLI must not require that.

Knowledge-graph tools ARE included here, unlike in the console where they
are added per-request behind a UI toggle: this command is the knowledge
graph agent, so a question about what the system already knows is its
central case rather than an opt-in.

NOT FREE. Roughly seventy tool schemas is a large prompt for a local model
-- ADR-3 records that thirty-two already push a 40,960-token context to
65,536 via YaRN. That is the cost ADR-003 accepted for one chat instead of
three; it is stated here so a future narrowing is a decision rather than a
surprise.

Returns:
    Physics, catalog, literature and knowledge-graph tools.

entries.integration_instructions: CLI integration pattern only: the donor CLI still constructs simulation tools. Preserve F2W entrypoints and inject a literature-only tool set.
entries.evidence: AST-verified source symbols; selected implementations statically reviewed; runtime behavior not certified

verified_symbols.name: lit_search_papers
verified_symbols.doc:
Search the published literature by topic, technique and material.

Full-text search over OpenAlex (250M+ works). Use it to find what has been
published about a material or a measurement — "GISAXS studies of PS-b-PMMA
lamellar films", "block copolymer cylinder spacing".

Results carry an abstract and a DOI, so a promising hit can be followed up
with ``lit_read_paper`` for the full text.

Args:
    query: Free text, e.g. ``"PS-b-PMMA lamellar period"``.
    technique: Appended to the search, e.g. ``"GISAXS"``, ``"SAXS"``.
    material: Appended to the search, e.g. ``"block copolymer"``.
    year_from: Earliest publication year; 0 for no bound.
    year_to: Latest publication year; 0 for no bound.
    max_results: Cap, clamped to 25.

Returns:
    JSON ``{"count", "papers": [{openalex_id, doi, title, authors, year,
    journal, abstract, concepts, citation_count, is_oa}]}`` — or
    ``{"error": ...}``. An empty list means nothing matched, which is an
    answer, not a failure.
verified_symbols.signature: query: str, technique: str='', material: str='', year_from: int=0, year_to: int=0, max_results: int=10

verified_symbols.name: lit_get_papers_by_doi
verified_symbols.doc:
Look up specific papers by DOI.

Use when a DOI is already known — from a citation, a user, or a graph
entity — rather than searching for it.

Args:
    dois: One DOI, or several separated by commas. Up to 10 are resolved.

Returns:
    JSON ``{"count", "papers": [...]}`` with longer abstracts than search
    returns, plus ``referenced_works`` (the paper's own citations) — or
    ``{"error": ...}``. A DOI OpenAlex does not know is omitted rather than
    failing the whole call.

verified_symbols.name: lit_find_citing_papers
verified_symbols.doc:
Find later papers that cite a given work.

Follows the citation graph FORWARD in time — what did this paper lead to,
who built on it, was it contradicted. Pair with ``lit_find_related_papers``,
which finds work on the same problem that never cited it.

Args:
    openalex_id: An OpenAlex work id (``"W2741809807"``) or its full URL,
        as returned by ``lit_search_papers``.
    max_results: Cap, clamped to 25.

Returns:
    JSON ``{"count", "papers": [...]}``, most-cited first — or
    ``{"error": ...}``.

verified_symbols.name: lit_find_related_papers
verified_symbols.doc:
Find semantically related papers, whether or not they cite each other.

Semantic Scholar recommendations. Surfaces work on the same problem that a
citation search misses — parallel groups, later independent work, different
vocabulary for the same structure.

Args:
    paper_id: A DOI or a Semantic Scholar paper id.
    max_results: Cap, clamped to 20 by the upstream API.

Returns:
    JSON ``{"count", "papers": [...]}`` — or ``{"error": ...}``.

verified_symbols.name: lit_read_paper
verified_symbols.doc:
Fetch an open-access paper's full text and list its sections.

Downloads the PDF (Unpaywall / Semantic Scholar / arXiv), converts it to
markdown and splits it into named sections. **Returns the section NAMES,
not the text** — a paper is far larger than a usable tool response. Read a
section with ``lit_read_paper_section``.

Only open-access papers can be read. A paywalled DOI returns an error; that
is a fact about the paper, not a malfunction, and search results carry
``is_oa`` so it can be predicted.

Args:
    doi: The paper's DOI.

Returns:
    JSON ``{"doi", "section_names", "num_pages", "num_images"}`` — or
    ``{"error": ...}``.

verified_symbols.name: lit_read_paper_section
verified_symbols.doc:
Read one section of an open-access paper.

The section that usually matters for structure is "results" or
"experimental"; ``lit_read_paper`` lists what a given paper actually has.

Args:
    doi: The paper's DOI.
    section: Section name, matched case-insensitively as a substring, so
        ``"results"`` finds "Results and Discussion".

Returns:
    JSON ``{"doi", "section", "text", "truncated"}`` — or ``{"error",
    "available_sections"}``, which names the sections that DO exist so the
    next call can use a real one instead of guessing again.

verified_symbols.name: build_lit_tools
verified_symbols.doc:
The literature tools to hand the agent.

Returns:
    Six tools: three search/citation, one DOI lookup, two full-text.

entries.integration_instructions: Six verified donor tool IDs; retain FORGE-facing behavior through adapters while replacing direct provider/cache globals with F2W services.
entries.evidence: AST-verified source symbols; selected implementations statically reviewed; runtime behavior not certified

verified_symbols.name: OpenAlexNoData
verified_symbols.doc:
An EMPTY dict that says WHY it is empty.

`fetch_openalex` has always answered ``{}`` for every failure, and callers
written against that contract -- ``payload = fetch(...) or {}``, ``if not
data:`` -- must keep working unchanged, including ones this change cannot
touch. An empty ``dict`` subclass is exactly ``{}`` to all of them (falsy,
``== {}``, ``.get`` answers the default), while a caller that cares can ask
:func:`is_quota_paused` / :func:`is_not_found` and tell "the allowance is
spent until 00:00 UTC" from "no such DOI" from "the network blinked". Those
three need opposite handling: park the job, give up on the DOI, retry soon.

Never cached: one is built fresh for every miss.

verified_symbols.name: OpenAlexQuotaPaused
verified_symbols.doc:
Raised by the list-returning helpers while the breaker is open.

They return ``[]`` for "nothing matched", which is an answer. Returning
``[]`` for "the allowance is spent" would tell a chat model there is no
literature on the topic; raising lets the tool layer say which it was.

verified_symbols.name: is_quota_paused
verified_symbols.doc: True when *value* is the breaker's "allowance spent" answer.

verified_symbols.name: is_not_found
verified_symbols.doc: True when OpenAlex ANSWERED that the record does not exist.

verified_symbols.name: pause_openalex
verified_symbols.doc:
Open the breaker for *seconds* (at least 60); returns the resume time.

Only ever EXTENDS a pause. Two threads tripping it with different waits
must not let the shorter one reopen the gate early and spend a request
rediscovering the quota.

verified_symbols.name: openalex_pause_state
verified_symbols.doc:
The open breaker, or None when OpenAlex may be called.

Returns:
    ``{"resume_at": epoch_s, "resume_at_iso": "...+00:00", "seconds_left":
    s, "reason": "HTTP 429"}`` while paused. This is what a job runner
    records as ``resume_at`` when it parks a queue rather than draining it.

verified_symbols.name: reset_openalex_pause
verified_symbols.doc: Close the breaker -- for tests, and for an operator who topped up the key.

verified_symbols.name: openalex_auth_params
verified_symbols.doc:
``api_key`` and ``mailto`` query parameters, each only when real.

Kept OUT of the cache key (see :func:`fetch_openalex`): a key rotation must
not orphan 30 days of cached answers, and the cache file must never hold a
credential.

verified_symbols.name: openalex_headers
verified_symbols.doc: Polite-pool header. OpenAlex gives identified callers better limits.

verified_symbols.name: fetch_openalex
verified_symbols.doc:
GET from OpenAlex, cached, with credentials, backoff and a breaker.

Args:
    path: API path (``"works"``, ``"works/https://doi.org/10.1021/x"``) or
        a full URL.
    params: Query parameters. ``api_key``/``mailto`` are added here; do not
        pass them.
    ttl: Cache lifetime in seconds; ``None`` uses ``OPENALEX_CACHE_TTL``.
    use_cache: ``False`` bypasses the read (positive and negative), but
        still writes on success.
    timeout: Per-request timeout.
    max_attempts: Retry budget for 429/5xx, backing off 1s, 2s, 4s.

Returns:
    Parsed JSON on success. Otherwise an EMPTY :class:`OpenAlexNoData` --
    ``== {}`` and falsy, so every caller written against the old "``{}`` on
    failure" contract behaves exactly as before -- whose ``reason`` says
    which failure it was: :data:`NOT_FOUND` (a singleton 404, cached for
    ``OPENALEX_NEGATIVE_TTL``), :data:`QUOTA_PAUSED` (the breaker is open;
    ``resume_at`` says until when), :data:`UNREACHABLE` or
    :data:`REJECTED`. Never raises: a literature outage must degrade a
    search, not fail an agent turn or abort a build.
verified_symbols.signature: path: str, params: dict[str, Any] | None=None, *, ttl: float | None=None, use_cache: bool=True, timeout: float=15.0, max_attempts: int=3

verified_symbols.name: abstract_from_inverted_index
verified_symbols.doc:
Rebuild a readable abstract from OpenAlex's inverted index.

OpenAlex ships abstracts as ``{word: [positions]}`` for copyright reasons.

Returns:
    The reconstructed text, or ``""`` when absent or malformed.

verified_symbols.name: search_papers
verified_symbols.doc:
Full-text search OpenAlex.

*technique* and *material* are appended to the search text rather than
applied as filters: OpenAlex's concept filters need concept IDs, and the
words themselves are what actually appear in a scattering paper's title and
abstract.

Args:
    query: Free text, e.g. ``"PS-b-PMMA lamellar period"``.
    technique: Appended, e.g. ``"GISAXS"``.
    material: Appended, e.g. ``"block copolymer"``.
    year_from: Inclusive lower bound on publication year; 0 disables.
    year_to: Inclusive upper bound; 0 disables.
    max_results: Cap, clamped to 50.

Returns:
    Paper records, most relevant first. Empty on failure or no match.

Raises:
    OpenAlexQuotaPaused: The allowance is spent. NOT an empty list, which
        would read as "nothing has been published on this".
verified_symbols.signature: query: str, *, technique: str='', material: str='', year_from: int=0, year_to: int=0, max_results: int=10

verified_symbols.name: get_papers_by_doi
verified_symbols.doc:
Look up specific papers by DOI.

Args:
    dois: DOIs, with or without the ``https://doi.org/`` prefix. Capped at 10.

Returns:
    Records for the DOIs that resolved. A DOI OpenAlex does not know is
    omitted rather than raising -- one bad DOI in a list must not lose the
    others.

Raises:
    OpenAlexQuotaPaused: The allowance is spent, so "omitted" would be a
        lie about the DOIs not yet asked.

verified_symbols.name: fetch_works_by_doi
verified_symbols.doc:
Resolve many DOIs in OR-filtered batches, priming the per-DOI cache.

Args:
    dois: Bare or URL-form DOIs. Case and prefix are normalised; duplicates
        are asked once. Order is preserved so a run is reproducible.
    batch: DOIs per request. Clamped to ``BULK_DOI_BATCH``.
    prime_cache: Whether to also write each work under the cache key a later
        single-DOI resolve will look for. Leave on for a corpus pass; turn
        off when only the return value is wanted.

Returns:
    ``{bare_doi: work}`` for the DOIs OpenAlex knows. A DOI it does not know
    is ABSENT rather than mapped to ``{}``, so a caller can tell "no such
    work" from "never asked". Stops early and returns what it has if a batch
    fails. When the failure is the spent allowance the breaker is open, and
    :func:`openalex_pause_state` says until when -- the caller should report
    THAT rather than spin through 500 more failures.

Example:
    >>> works = fetch_works_by_doi(["10.1063/1.4973996"])  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> works["10.1063/1.4973996"]["title"]                # doctest: +SKIP
    'Ab initio ...'
verified_symbols.signature: dois: Sequence[str], *, batch: int=BULK_DOI_BATCH, prime_cache: bool=True

verified_symbols.name: find_citing_papers
verified_symbols.doc:
Papers that cite a given work, most-cited first.

Args:
    openalex_id: ``"W2741809807"`` or the full OpenAlex URL.
    max_results: Cap, clamped to 50.

Returns:
    Citing paper records; empty on failure.

Raises:
    OpenAlexQuotaPaused: The allowance is spent.

verified_symbols.name: find_related_papers
verified_symbols.doc:
Semantically related papers, via Semantic Scholar recommendations.

A different axis from citation: it surfaces work on the same problem that
never cited the seed.

Args:
    paper_id: A DOI or a Semantic Scholar paper id.
    max_results: Cap, clamped to 20 (the API's own limit).

Returns:
    Recommended paper records; empty on failure. Not cached -- the
    recommendations endpoint is a POST and the cache is GET-shaped.

verified_symbols.name: normalise_doi
verified_symbols.doc: A DOI as ``10.x/y``, lowercased; ``""`` when *value* is not one.

verified_symbols.name: TokenBucket
verified_symbols.doc:
A thread-safe token bucket: *rate_per_s* sustained, *burst* at once.

The clock and the sleep are injectable so a test can drive it without
waiting.

verified_symbols.name: Resolved
verified_symbols.doc:
One identifier's resolution.

Attributes:
    key: ``"doi:10.1021/..."`` | ``"title:<fold>:<year>"`` | ``"arxiv:..."``.
    source: ``openalex`` | ``semantic_scholar`` | ``crossref`` |
        ``s2_title`` | ``crossref_title`` | ``none``.
    record: The provider's record, or ``None`` for a verified negative.
    fetched_at: ISO-8601 UTC.
    cost_usd: What this answer cost under OpenAlex usage pricing.

verified_symbols.name: ResolverCache
verified_symbols.doc: One row per identifier key. A row with no record says "asked; nobody has it".

verified_symbols.name: ReferenceLike
verified_symbols.doc:
What :meth:`BatchResolver.resolve_references` reads from a reference.

``als_knowledge_agent.graph.reference_parsing.ParsedReference`` satisfies
it; forge cannot import that type (dependency direction is als -> forge).

verified_symbols.name: title_similarity
verified_symbols.doc:
Shared 6-character shingles of the folded titles, over the shorter's.

Folding first makes it blind to case, punctuation, and GROBID's habit of
dropping a ligature or a hyphen at a line break.

verified_symbols.name: BatchResolver
verified_symbols.doc:
Resolve DOIs and parsed references across OpenAlex, S2 and Crossref.

Args:
    cache: Where answers are kept. Defaults to :func:`default_cache_path`.
    s2_key: Semantic Scholar key; defaults to ``SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY``.
    mailto: Polite-pool contact; defaults to ``OPENALEX_EMAIL`` when real.
    http: An ``httpx.Client`` -- injected in tests with ``MockTransport``.
    sleep: Backoff sleep, injectable for tests.
    buckets: Override the ``(openalex, s2, crossref)`` token buckets.

The OpenAlex ``api_key`` is not a parameter: it comes from the one place
:mod:`~forge.agents.literature.openalex` reads it, and is never logged.

entries.integration_instructions: Preserve batching, throttling, cache and provider fallbacks. Distinguish bibliographic candidate resolution from authoritative Work identity.
entries.evidence: AST-verified source symbols; selected implementations statically reviewed; runtime behavior not certified

verified_symbols.name: ResolverError
verified_symbols.doc: Raised when an identifier cannot be resolved to a publication.

verified_symbols.name: resolve
verified_symbols.doc:
Resolve a DOI, OpenAlex work ID, arXiv ID, or URL to an OpenAlex works record.

Accepted forms:
  - Bare DOI:            10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2
  - DOI URL:             https://doi.org/10.1038/...
  - OpenAlex work ID:    W2912345678
  - OpenAlex work URL:   https://openalex.org/W2912345678
  - arXiv ID:            arXiv:2103.00020  or  arxiv:2103.00020  or  2103.00020
  - arXiv URL:           https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020

Args:
    identifier: Any recognised publication identifier string.

Returns:
    The raw OpenAlex works dict (same shape as ``fetch_openalex("works/W...")``).

Raises:
    ResolverError: If the identifier format is unrecognised or the record
        is not found on OpenAlex.

verified_symbols.name: _normalise_abstract
verified_symbols.doc:
Reconstruct the abstract from the inverted index if it is missing.

Mutates *record* in place.

Args:
    record: OpenAlex works dict to normalise.

verified_symbols.name: _normalise_bibliographic
verified_symbols.doc:
Lift `authors`, `journal` and `abstract_snippet` to the top level.

THE RESOLVER RETURNS THE RAW OPENALEX RECORD AND THE WRITER EXPECTS A
NORMALISED ONE, and for three fields nothing bridged the two.
`upsert_publication_full` reads `work["authors"]`, `work["journal"]` and
`work["abstract_snippet"]`; OpenAlex sends `authorships`,
`primary_location.source.display_name`, and no snippet at all. So every
paper ingested through `add_publication` stored `authors: []`, `journal: ""`
and `abstract_snippet: ""`.

Measured on the live graph before this fix: **0 of 494 publications** had
any of the three, and the author loop in `kg_writer` -- which mints
`author` entities and `schema:author` edges -- iterated an empty list every
time. That is why the graph holds zero authors.

IT IS IRREVERSIBLE PER PAPER, which is why this is worth fixing before any
backfill. Entity properties are CREATE-ONLY, so a publication written
without a journal can never be given one; only delete-and-recreate would,
and that cascades to its sections, figures and panels. Every paper ingested
while this was broken lost those three fields permanently.

`enrichment_agent` has had the correct mapping twice over (:447, :2224).
This is the shared boundary both ingest paths cross, so it belongs here --
the same "one implementation for what was three" the citation pass needed.

Mutates *record* in place, and never overwrites a value a caller already
supplied.

verified_symbols.name: _ensure_oa_fields
verified_symbols.doc:
Ensure ``is_oa``, ``oa_url``, and ``pdf_url`` keys are present.

Sets them from nested OpenAlex fields if they are not already present at
the top level of *record*.  Mutates *record* in place.

Args:
    record: OpenAlex works dict to patch.

entries.integration_instructions: Retain DOI/arXiv/OpenAlex normalization; resolve metadata without treating every identifier as a new scholarly Work.
entries.evidence: AST-verified source symbols; selected implementations statically reviewed; runtime behavior not certified

verified_symbols.name: IntakeReport
pdf_first_pages_text
verified_symbols.doc:
Text of the first *pages* pages, plus the document's own metadata.

Uses PyMuPDF directly. That is a new dependency direction for this file but
not for the tree: ``pymupdf4llm`` is already required
(``pyproject.toml``) and pulls PyMuPDF, which is what it is built on. Going
through ``pymupdf4llm.to_markdown`` instead would render the WHOLE document
to markdown -- seconds per file and megabytes of string -- to read a header.

The metadata block is included because publishers frequently write the DOI
into ``/Subject`` or ``/Keywords`` even when the rendered page shows it only
as part of a logo image, which extracts as nothing.

Returns "" on any failure, including an encrypted document: a file whose
text cannot be read is a file with no recoverable DOI, which is a reportable
outcome rather than an error.

verified_symbols.name: extract_doi_candidates
verified_symbols.doc:
Distinct DOIs in *text*, in first-occurrence order.

EVERY CANDIDATE IS TRIED, not just the first, and the ordering is the
heuristic: a paper's own DOI is almost always the first on page one, in the
header or the footer block, while a cited work's DOI appears later. But
"almost always" is not a guarantee, so the caller title-checks each in turn
and takes the first that verifies -- ordering narrows the search, the title
check is what makes the answer safe.

Trailing sentence punctuation is stripped, and the UN-stripped form is kept
as a lower-priority candidate: SICI-style DOIs legitimately end in ')'.

verified_symbols.name: filename_doi_candidates
verified_symbols.doc:
DOIs a FILENAME implies, for papers whose text does not carry one.

NOT AN EXCEPTION TO THE NO-INVENTED-KEYS RULE, because these are candidates,
not answers: they go through `resolve_verified` like any other, so a guess
only survives if OpenAlex has that DOI *and* its title matches this PDF's own
first pages. A wrong guess resolves to a different paper and is rejected on
the title, and a guess for a paper that does not exist is rejected outright.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING. Publisher-named downloads encode the citation, and
older scans are exactly the ones whose text has no DOI because the DOI
postdates the paper. Measured on one real folder of 24 PDFs: 8 had no
recoverable DOI, and 5 of those 8 verified from their filename alone --
including Moharam & Gaylord's two RCWA papers (JOSA 1981, JOSA A 1995),
which are foundational for grating analysis and were simply unreachable
before.

Two patterns, both formulaic:

* OSA/Optica journals -- ``ao-49-31-6102`` is Applied Optics volume 49,
  issue 31, page 6102, whose DOI is ``10.1364/AO.49.006102``. The page is
  zero-padded to six digits; the issue does not appear in the DOI.
* arXiv -- ``CyRSoXS2209.13121`` carries the arXiv id, whose registered DOI
  is ``10.48550/arXiv.2209.13121``.

Both spellings of case are offered because OpenAlex normalises DOIs to
lowercase and publishers do not agree.

Args:
    filename: Base name of the PDF; directories are ignored.
    limit: Maximum candidates to return.

Returns:
    Candidate DOIs, most specific first. Empty when nothing is implied.

verified_symbols.name: extract_doi_from_pdf
verified_symbols.doc:
The first DOI candidate in *path*, or "". Convenience for callers that
do not verify (tests, diagnostics); `prepare_local_pdf` uses
:func:`extract_doi_candidates` and checks every one.

verified_symbols.name: title_matches_pdf
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether *title* plausibly names the document *text* came from.

THE GUARD AGAINST FILING A PAPER UNDER ANOTHER PAPER'S DOI. Compares
content words only: tokens of four characters or more, case-folded. Short
words are dropped because "of", "the" and "and" match everything, and
because their absence from a hyphenation-mangled extraction says nothing.

A word counts as present if it appears anywhere in the text, not as a whole
token -- PDF extraction routinely welds words to punctuation and splits them
across line breaks, and a stricter test fails on correct pairs.

``threshold`` of 0.6 tolerates a subtitle or a mangled word while still
rejecting an unrelated paper. A title with no long words at all cannot be
checked, and returns False: unverifiable is not the same as verified.
verified_symbols.signature: title: str, text: str, *, threshold: float=0.6

verified_symbols.name: cache_path_for
verified_symbols.doc:
Where a PDF for *doi* must live for the cache to find it.

``_safe_stem(_doi_only(doi))``, and the nesting matters: ``_safe_stem`` on a
raw ``https://doi.org/10.1039/x`` yields ``https___doi_org_10_1039_x``,
which ``_cached_pdf_for`` never probes for. That exact trap is documented
inside ``_download_by_doi``, which writes the un-normalised form.

verified_symbols.name: resolve_by_filename
verified_symbols.doc:
The candidate DOI the FILENAME confirms, with no network call at all.

THIS IS A VERIFICATION, NOT A GUESS, and the distinction is the whole reason
it is allowed to stand in for the OpenAlex title check. Two INDEPENDENT
sources have to agree: the DOI must appear in the document's own text, and
it must fold to the filename. Neither alone would be enough -- a reference
list is full of other papers' DOIs, and a filename cannot say where its
eaten separators belonged -- but a candidate satisfying both is the paper.

Folding is what makes the filename usable: this corpus stores
`10.1093/nar/gkw961` as `10.1093nargkw961`, every slash gone, and the
registrant prefix is 4-9 digits so no mechanical split is reliable. The
filename says WHICH characters; the document says WHERE the separators go.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO: confirm the DOI belongs to a real, findable publication,
or supply a title, authors or a year. Those come from OpenAlex, and a
publication resolved this way carries `metadata_source: "pdf_only"` so the
graph says so rather than implying bibliographic data it does not have.

Returns:
    ``(work, status, tried)`` in `resolve_verified`'s shape. *work* is a
    MINIMAL record -- the DOI and nothing invented.

verified_symbols.name: resolve_asserted
verified_symbols.doc:
Resolve a CALLER-ASSERTED DOI, without requiring its title in the PDF.

WHY THE TITLE CHECK CANNOT APPLY HERE, measured on the file that motivated
this function -- the Supporting Information for ``10.1021/nl2020526``:

* The SI carries no DOI in its text, its metadata, or its filename, so
  every recovery path in :func:`prepare_local_pdf` reports
  ``skipped:no_doi``. An SI is not a registered work; its identity lives
  only in its parent, which only the caller knows.
* Its title line reads "Defining the **Nanostrucutred** Morphology..." --
  the SI misspells the paper's own title, so even a hand-written title
  check against OpenAlex's spelling would fail. This is not an edge case
  to code around; it is why the corroboration has to come from the caller
  instead.

OpenAlex is still consulted, and a DOI it does not know is still refused.
That keeps the two things this module exists to guarantee: the cache stem
is derived from OpenAlex's own (lowercased) spelling of the DOI -- see the
two-stem note in :func:`prepare_local_pdf` -- and a typo in an asserted DOI
cannot mint a publication that no registry has ever heard of.

What is given up is the protection against a WRONG-but-real DOI. Nothing
downstream can detect that, and create-only properties make it unfixable in
place, so :attr:`IntakeReport.identity_asserted` records that this path was
taken.

Returns:
    ``(work, status, tried)`` in :func:`resolve_verified`'s shape, so
    callers branch on one contract.

verified_symbols.name: resolve_verified
verified_symbols.doc:
The first candidate DOI whose OpenAlex title matches *pdf_text*.

QUERIES `fetch_openalex` DIRECTLY RATHER THAN `paper_resolver.resolve`, and
that is the whole reason this function exists. `resolve` raises one
`ResolverError` for two different situations (paper_resolver.py:108-109),
and they need opposite handling:

* `fetch_openalex` returns ``{}`` when it could not get an answer at all --
  a network failure or a 5xx after retries. **Retryable**, and NOT cached
  (only 200s reach `_cache_put`), so trying again later genuinely can work.
* A response with an empty ``results`` list means OpenAlex answered and has
  no such record. **Permanent** for this DOI, and cached for 30 days.

Reporting "unknown DOI" for an outage would send someone chasing a
non-existent data problem; reporting "unreachable" for a genuinely unknown
DOI would promise a retry that can never succeed.

Returns:
    ``(work, status, tried)``. ``work`` is non-None only on success, and
    then ``status`` is "". Otherwise ``status`` is the closed-set reason,
    chosen so the RETRYABLE outcome wins if any candidate saw an outage.
verified_symbols.signature: candidates: list[str], pdf_text: str, *, fetch: Any=None

verified_symbols.name: prepare_local_pdf
verified_symbols.doc:
Vet one local PDF and, with *apply*, seed it into the paper cache.

Does NOT call ``add_publication`` -- the caller does, so that the CLI can
talk HTTP to a running service while the upload route calls the handler
in-process, without two copies of this vetting.

Order is chosen so the cheap, offline refusals happen before any network
call: magic bytes, then content hash against the manifest, then DOI
extraction, and only then OpenAlex.

Args:
    path: The local file.
    apply: Copy into the cache and record it. False reports what would
        happen and writes nothing.
    force: Proceed even when the manifest already holds these bytes.
    fetch: Injected ``fetch_openalex``-alike for tests. Defaults to the
        real client.
    verify: How a candidate DOI is confirmed. ``"openalex"`` (default) looks
        each one up and requires its title to appear in the PDF.
        ``"filename"`` requires it to fold to the filename instead, which
        makes the whole intake OFFLINE -- see :func:`resolve_by_filename`
        for what that buys and what it gives up. Any other value raises,
        rather than silently falling back to a check the caller did not
        ask for.
    doi: A DOI the CALLER asserts this file belongs to. Bypasses recovery
        from the text and the filename, and waives the title check --
        :func:`resolve_asserted` explains why an SI cannot pass either.
        Still refused if OpenAlex has no such record, and *verify* is
        ignored (the caller has already supplied the corroboration that
        *verify* selects between).

Returns:
    An :class:`IntakeReport`. Never raises for a bad input file.
verified_symbols.signature: path: Path, *, apply: bool=False, force: bool=False, fetch: Any=None, verify: str='openalex', doi: str=''

        then not appended again -- re-running the back-fill is a no-op
        rather than one more edge per paper per run.
    client: Injectable graph client.

Returns:
    A :class:`BackfillResult`.

verified_symbols.name: sha256_of
verified_symbols.doc:
Content hash of a file's bytes, or "" if it cannot be read.

THE FIRST CONTENT HASH IN THIS PIPELINE. Every other `hashlib` call here
and in the graph writers hashes TEXT -- a section heading, a figure
filename, a query payload -- never the bytes of the document. So two DOIs
pointing at the same paper produced two cache entries and two publication
nodes, and a truncated download over 1 kB was accepted as "cached" forever
(the only size check is `> 1000`).

Returns "" rather than raising: a hash is metadata, and failing to compute
one must not fail an ingest that would otherwise succeed.

verified_symbols.name: read_manifest
verified_symbols.doc:
The manifest, or an empty mapping if absent or unreadable.

Never raises. A corrupt manifest must degrade to "we know nothing about
the cache", which is exactly the state before it existed -- not to a failed
ingest.

verified_symbols.name: record_in_manifest
verified_symbols.doc:
Record *pdf_path*'s hash and size, and warn if we already have it.

Args:
    pdf_path: The cached PDF.
    source_url: Where it came from, when known.
    digest: Precomputed sha256, to avoid a second read.

Returns:
    The file's sha256, or "" if it could not be hashed.

WRITTEN NON-ATOMICALLY ON PURPOSE, with the risk stated rather than hidden:
a temp-file-and-replace protects a reader from seeing a half-written
manifest, but two ingest processes finishing at once still lose one of the
two records. That is acceptable because the manifest is derived data -- the
audit script rebuilds it from the PDFs -- and unacceptable to fix with a
lock file that could be left behind by a crash.
verified_symbols.signature: pdf_path: Path, *, source_url: str | None=None, digest: str | None=None

verified_symbols.name: duplicate_stems
verified_symbols.doc:
Cached filenames whose content hashes to *digest*, newest last.

Used to answer "do we already have this paper under another name" without
re-reading every PDF.

verified_symbols.name: _cached_pdf_for
verified_symbols.doc:
An already-downloaded PDF for *doi*, under any spelling this cache uses.

THREE MISMATCHES ARE TOLERATED HERE:

1. **The DOI shape** -- the one that was actually breaking. The graph
   stores ``https://doi.org/10.1039/...`` while every filename was built
   from the bare DOI, so the stem came out
   ``https___doi_org_10_1039_c5ta01004g`` and matched nothing ever
   written. Found by running the corpus refresh: both pilot papers
   reported "no PDF" with their PDFs sitting in the cache.
2. **The stem convention.** ``_safe_stem`` versus :func:`_legacy_stem` --
   they differ on hyphens, which 30 of the 155 cached papers have.
3. **CASE**, which matters less here than it first appeared and is worth
   recording accurately. 26 cached files keep the publisher's mixed case
   (``10_1039_C5TA01004G.pdf``) while DOIs are compared lowercased -- but
   macOS's filesystem is case-INSENSITIVE, so the plain probe already
   finds them and this was never the live failure. It becomes a real one
   on Linux, which this tree ran on until recently and may again, so the
   fallback scan below handles it rather than leaving a trap for the move.

Reading is permissive so nothing on disk is stranded; writing uses
:func:`_safe_stem` on the bare DOI alone, so new files converge on one
convention.

verified_symbols.name: _download_by_doi
verified_symbols.doc:
Attempt to download a paper PDF via open access routes.

Tries in order:

0. ``pdf_url`` from a pre-fetched OpenAlex work record (fastest, no API call).
1. Unpaywall REST API.
2. Semantic Scholar graph API.
3. arXiv direct download (for DOIs of the form ``10.48550/arXiv.*``).

Args:
    doi: The paper's DOI.
    work: Optional pre-fetched OpenAlex works dict.  When provided, the
        ``primary_location.pdf_url`` field is tried before any external
        API calls.

Returns:
    Path to the downloaded PDF, or None if unavailable.

verified_symbols.name: _fetch_pdf
verified_symbols.doc:
Download a PDF from a URL.

Args:
    url: URL to the PDF file.
    dest: Destination path to save the file.

Returns:
    Path to the saved file, or None on failure.

verified_symbols.name: is_pdf
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether a cached file really is a PDF, by magic bytes.

NOT PEDANTRY -- IT WAS COSTING FIGURES. ``_fetch_pdf`` accepted any 200
with a body over 1 kB, so an OSTI.GOV landing page (HTML, 133 kB, HTTP 200)
was saved as ``10_1021_acs_macromol_0c01782.pdf``. PyMuPDF **also** reads
HTML, so it opened that page, reported 21 pages, and produced ten blank
figures that were ingested into the graph as this paper's figures. Nothing
in the pipeline disagreed at any point.

Docling refuses it outright (``PdfiumError: Data format error``), which is
how the file was found. A sweep of the 155 cached papers found exactly this
one, so the check is cheap insurance rather than a widespread repair.

verified_symbols.name: _parse_pdf_with_pymupdf
verified_symbols.doc:
The previous parser, kept as the fallback when docling is absent.

Its shortcomings are documented on :func:`_parse_pdf_with_docling`; it is
retained because docling is an optional extra and an ingest that refuses to
run without it would be a worse failure than one that runs with fewer
captions.

verified_symbols.name: PublicationParser
verified_symbols.doc:
Turn a PDF into a :class:`ParsedDocument`.

Implementations must not raise for a merely disappointing document -- an
empty section list is a legitimate answer. Raise only when the file cannot
be parsed at all, so :func:`parse_pdf` can fall through to the next parser.

verified_symbols.name: DoclingParser
verified_symbols.doc:
docling: real figures with captions, typed headings, and tables.

MEASURED AGAINST THE ALTERNATIVE on 10.1039/c5ta01004g, same machine:
13 images vs pymupdf4llm's 109 (101 of them slivers), 10 captions vs 0,
3 tables vs 0, 22 typed headings vs 0. The 109-vs-13 is one fact, not two:
pymupdf4llm extracts every embedded XObject, so one figure arrives as a
dozen strips and `_is_usable_figure` discards most of them.

Captions are why it matters beyond tidiness -- the figure classifier was
measured confidently wrong on experimental-vs-simulated from pixels alone,
and a caption naming the technique is the signal it was missing. They can
only be attached at CREATION, since entity properties are create-only.

verified_symbols.name: PyMuPDFParser
verified_symbols.doc:
pymupdf4llm: the fallback, and honest about what it cannot give.

No captions, no typed headings, no tables, and no per-figure page -- the
old dict claimed ``page: 0`` for every figure, which is a value, not an
absence. Sections come from the markdown regex, and their ``page`` is None
rather than 0.

verified_symbols.name: parse_pdf
verified_symbols.doc:
Parse *pdf_path* with the first parser that succeeds.

Args:
    pdf_path: The PDF to parse.
    parsers: Ordered candidates. Defaults to :data:`DEFAULT_PARSERS`.

Returns:
    A :class:`ParsedDocument` stamped with the parser and version that
    produced it, and the content hash of the bytes read.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the file is not a PDF (see :func:`is_pdf`), or if every
        parser failed. A missing optional parser is not a failure.

verified_symbols.name: _parse_pdf_to_markdown
verified_symbols.doc:
Parse a PDF into structured markdown, figures and captions.

THE LEGACY DICT CONTRACT, now a thin adapter over :func:`parse_pdf`. It
used to carry its own copy of the docling/pymupdf dispatch, which meant two
implementations of "which parser ran and what did it find" that could
disagree. Callers that want bounding boxes, tables, section pages or the
parser version should use :func:`parse_pdf` and read the typed object.

Args:
    pdf_path: Path to the PDF file.

Returns:
    ``{markdown, num_pages, num_images, image_paths, figures, tables,
    pdf_path, parser, parser_version, file_sha256}``. The first eight keys
    are exactly what this returned before; the last two are additive.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the file is not a PDF, or if every parser failed.

verified_symbols.name: _extract_sections
verified_symbols.doc:
Split markdown into named sections based on headers.

Args:
    markdown: Full markdown text of the paper.

Returns:
    Dictionary mapping section names to their content.

verified_symbols.name: without_embedded_images
verified_symbols.doc:
Remove encoded image bytes from prose, retaining captions and markup.

Figure pixels are stored as separate artifacts. Sending their data URIs to
a text model creates hundreds of meaningless chunks and can truncate real
prose from the graph. Also handles a URI cut off by an older storage cap.

verified_symbols.name: BoundingBox
verified_symbols.doc:
Where an element sits on its page, in the parser's own coordinates.

Stored as given rather than normalised: docling reports ``coord_origin``
(BOTTOMLEFT for PDF-native, TOPLEFT for rendered), and silently converting
would make a wrong overlay impossible to diagnose. Callers that draw must
read ``coord_origin``.

verified_symbols.name: ParsedFigure
verified_symbols.doc:
One usable figure, its caption, and where it came from.

``path`` is deterministic (``{stem}-p{page:03d}-{index:02d}.png``) and that
is LOAD-BEARING: figure entity ids hash the filename, so a path that moved
between runs would mint a new node on every re-parse and orphan the old one.

verified_symbols.name: figure_geometry_props
verified_symbols.doc:
The geometry keys a `paper_figure` entity should carry, from a legacy dict.

ONE HELPER FOR THREE WRITERS. `paper_figure` nodes are minted in three
places -- `server.py`'s `_do_pdf`, `enrichment_agent.run_pdf_parse` and
`corpus_refresh` -- and they have already drifted once: two stamped
`parser_version` and the third stamped only `parser`, which put 0 versions
on 11,667 rows. Entity properties are CREATE-ONLY, so a writer that omits a
key omits it permanently for every row it makes; there is no later pass
that can add it. A shared helper is the only shape where adding a key
reaches all three by construction.

Args:
    figure: One entry of `ParsedDocument.as_legacy_dict()["figures"]`.

Returns:
    Only the keys actually present. An absent bbox writes NO key rather
    than a null -- the `parser_version` lesson: `""` and `None` look like
    answers and sort with the others, where a missing key is honestly
    missing. `bbox` is JSON-encoded because entity properties are scalars.

verified_symbols.name: ParsedSection
verified_symbols.doc:
One section of the paper.

``level`` is the heading depth where the parser reports one (docling's typed
headings), else 0. ``page`` is None on the pymupdf fallback, which recovers
sections from markdown and has no page to give -- None says "unknown"
rather than claiming page 0, which is what the old dict did for figures.

verified_symbols.name: ParsedTable
verified_symbols.doc:
One table, exported to CSV beside the figures.

EXTRACTED BUT NEVER STORED until now: docling parses tables and the old
dict had no key for them, so they survived only as markdown inside a
section's truncated text.

verified_symbols.name: ParsedDocument
verified_symbols.doc:
Everything one parse of one PDF produced.

Attributes:
    pdf_path: The file parsed.
    markdown: Full text as markdown.
    num_pages: Page count.
    parser: Which parser ran (``PARSER_DOCLING`` / ``PARSER_PYMUPDF``).
    parser_version: The installed version of that parser. NEW -- nothing
        recorded it before, so two docling releases were indistinguishable
        in the graph.
    file_sha256: Content hash of the PDF bytes, or "" when not computed.
    sections / figures / tables: What was found.

verified_symbols.name: ParsedDocument.as_legacy_dict
verified_symbols.doc:
The old ``dict[str, Any]`` contract, for callers not yet migrated.

EXISTS SO THIS CHANGE IS NOT A REWRITE OF THE INGEST PATH. Three write
sites and five test modules read these keys; they keep working
unchanged, and each can move to the typed object when it has a reason
to. The keys are exactly what ``_parse_pdf_to_markdown`` returned
before, plus ``parser_version``, ``file_sha256`` and ``tables`` -- new
keys are additive and cannot break a caller that ignores them.

Every ``<listBibl>/<biblStruct>`` in a GROBID TEI document, in order.

verified_symbols.name: grobid_references
verified_symbols.doc:

Args:

Raises:

        whether that costs the paper its citations; it is not silently an
        empty list.

verified_symbols.doc:
The figure number a caption announces, or "" when it announces none.

Args:
    caption: The figure's caption.

Returns:

Returned as a STRING rather than an int because it is only ever used to
build a search pattern, and an int would invite arithmetic on a label.

verified_symbols.name: citing_sentence
verified_symbols.doc:
The first sentence in the paper that cites figure *number*.

Args:
    number: A figure number, from :func:`caption_figure_number`.
    sections: The paper's section texts, in document order.

Returns:
    One sentence, truncated to :data:`CITING_CHARS`, or "" if the figure is
    never cited in prose.

THE NUMBER MUST BE WORD-BOUNDED OR "Fig. 1" MATCHES "Fig. 12". That is not
hypothetical on a corpus whose largest paper has 86 figures, and the failure
is silent -- a plausible sentence about the wrong figure, handed to the model
as fact about this one.

ONE sentence, and the FIRST. A paper discusses a figure across a paragraph
and the later sentences are the argument built on it; the first is normally
what the figure shows. Sending the argument would invite the model to
restate the authors' conclusion instead of reading the image.

verified_symbols.name: render_paper_context
verified_symbols.doc:
The block describing the paper a figure came from.

Args:
    title: The publication's title -- its entity ``name``.
    abstract: Its abstract, truncated here.
    domain: The taxonomy domain the paper resolved to, for the model's
        orientation rather than for the class menu (the menu is chosen by
        the caller).
    techniques: Technique slugs the paper names, most-mentioned first.
    citing: The sentence citing this figure, from :func:`citing_sentence`.

Returns:
    A labelled block, or "" when nothing is known -- an empty context must
    be no context, not a heading with blanks under it, because a model shown
    "Paper: " reads it as a paper with no title.

EVERY LINE IS LABELLED WITH WHAT IT IS. The whole risk of supplying context
is that the model describes the paper instead of the image, and an unlabelled
wall of text is an invitation to do exactly that. The closing line says so in
words; it is not decoration.

verified_symbols.name: figure_publications
verified_symbols.doc:
``{figure entity id: publication entity id}`` for the whole graph.

Args:
    predicate: The edge to walk. ``schema:image`` for figures;
        ``forge:hasPanel`` gives panel -> figure, which a caller chains.

Returns:
    The mapping, empty when the graph is unreachable -- a missing context is
    a worse description, and raising would take a whole sweep down.

ONE PAGED READ, NOT ONE LOOKUP PER FIGURE. `store.get_node` costs 13.9 s
against this graph because it has no server-side id filter; 4,038 of them is
fifteen hours to answer a question one query answers. This repo has recorded
that clamp family six times and this is the same shape.

AND IT PAGES TO EXHAUSTION. `Query.links` DEFAULTS TO limit 100, which is
how a publication's figures became invisible behind its 330 author edges.

    characters on the paper this was measured against, and a sentence search
    over blanks costs the same as one over prose.

verified_symbols.name: redistribution_terms
verified_symbols.doc:
Licence, attribution and source for a work, for stamping onto figures.

**``is_oa`` IS NOT A LICENCE, and conflating the two is the mistake this
guards against.** ``is_oa`` says a human may READ the paper without paying;
it says nothing about whether its figures may be re-published. "Bronze" open
access -- free on the publisher's own site under no licence at all -- is the
common case where the two diverge, and it is a large share of OpenAlex's
``is_oa: true`` records.

Stamped at figure CREATION and never revised, because entity properties are
create-only in tiled 0.2.15. A figure ingested before this shipped therefore
has no terms at all, which ``figure_redistributable`` reports as ``False``:
unknown provenance is treated as not-redistributable, not as permission.

Args:
    work: The OpenAlex work record. An empty dict yields the unknown terms.

Returns:
    Property keys to merge into a ``paper_figure`` node's properties.

verified_symbols.name: unknown_redistribution_terms
verified_symbols.doc:
Terms for a figure whose licence could not be established.

FAILS CLOSED, and says which kind of nothing it is. ``figure_license_source
= "unavailable"`` distinguishes "we asked and could not find out" from a
figure written before terms were captured at all, which carries no keys
whatsoever. Both render as not-redistributable; only one of them is worth
re-asking about later.

verified_symbols.name: is_public_host
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether *hostname* resolves to at least one public, routable IP address.

Resolves via DNS (``socket.getaddrinfo``) rather than trusting the
hostname string alone -- a hostname can look innocuous and still resolve
to a private/loopback/link-local address (the standard SSRF-via-DNS
bypass). ANY resolved address being non-public is enough to refuse: a
multi-homed name that resolves to both a public and a private address is
exactly the kind of DNS-rebinding trick this guard exists to stop.

Args:
    hostname: The URL's hostname (already parsed out by the caller).

Returns:
    True if the hostname resolved to at least one address and every
    resolved address is public; False otherwise (including on a DNS
    failure -- an unresolvable host is refused, not assumed safe).

        host, or the host resolves to a private/loopback/link-local/
        reserved/multicast address (or doesn't resolve at all).

verified_symbols.name: require_allowed_folder
verified_symbols.doc:
Return *path* resolved, or raise ``ValueError`` if it escapes the allowlist.

Compared by resolved identity and ``parents`` membership rather than by
string prefix: a bare ``startswith`` also admits a SIBLING directory that
happens to share the prefix (``data/paper_cache_evil``). The same reasoning,
and the same shape, as ``rsoxs_helpers.require_spectra_path`` and
``browse_server._require_scratch_path``.

Resolving first is what makes it hold: ``..`` segments and symlinks are
collapsed before the comparison, so neither can walk out of a root.

verified_symbols.name: ingest_folder
verified_symbols.doc:
Vet, and with *apply* ingest, every PDF under *folder*.

Yields the report after each file so a caller can stream progress; the last
yield is the complete report. A generator rather than a callback because
the route needs to publish progress AND return a final answer, and a
callback would make the final state the caller's job to accumulate.

DRY RUN BY DEFAULT. Without *apply* nothing is copied, nothing is posted,
and the verdict list is the preflight for the run that does.

Args:
    folder: Directory to walk. Containment is the CALLER's responsibility
        via :func:`require_allowed_folder` -- this function is also used by
        the CLI, where the operator's own filesystem is the boundary.
    apply: Actually seed the cache and ingest.
    glob: Filename pattern, matched recursively.
    limit: Stop after this many files; 0 means all.
    force: Ingest even when the manifest already holds these bytes.
    offline: Verify a candidate DOI against the FILENAME rather than
        OpenAlex, which makes the whole intake offline.
    files: An explicit, ORDERED file list, replacing the glob. The order is
        the caller's priority and is preserved exactly -- a queue ranked by
        how likely each paper is to be worth the ~40 s it costs can be
        stopped at any point and will have done the most valuable work
        first. Entries outside *folder* are ignored, so a ranked list from
        elsewhere cannot widen what a contained caller reads.
    ingest_on_cache_conflict: Ingest the DOI anyway when the cache already
        holds DIFFERENT bytes at its stem. Off by default: the refusal
        exists for a real reason -- figure entities may already point into
        the `<stem>_images/` directory beside the cached PDF, and those
        paths are create-only, so replacing the bytes would silently
        re-point every figure at another document's content.

        Turning it on does NOT overwrite; that is the point. The cached
        copy stays exactly where it is and the paper is ingested from it.
        Measured on the rebuild: the re-fetched cache and the `ALS_all`
        archive hold different copies of the same papers -- a preprint and
        the published version, typically -- and refusing lost the paper
        from the GRAPH over a disagreement about which PDF to keep on DISK.
        Either copy answers the question the graph is asking.
    dois: Path -> a DOI the caller has ALREADY verified against the
        document, bypassing this function's own recovery for those files.
        A path absent from the mapping recovers as before. This is how a
        corpus scan's verified identifiers reach the intake: without it,
        every file is re-derived from its own text and a paper whose DOI the
        scan read but the intake cannot is lost as `skipped:no_doi`.
    ingest_one: Called with a verified DOI for each ingestable file.
        Required when *apply* is set. Returning a dict with `n_sections` /
        `n_figures` populates the verdict.
    concurrency: Bounded number of papers in flight. Intake/cache updates
        and writes for the same DOI are serialized; results finish independently.
    on_active: Optional callback with currently scheduled file paths.
    already_ingested: Asked, once a file's DOI is verified, whether that paper
        is already ingested (see `ingested_papers`); a paper it names is
        `skipped:already_ingested` in a dry run AND an applied one, and every
        paper this run ingests is recorded so a second file of the same
        paper is skipped too. Ignored with *force*. None means no check --
        the CLI's behaviour, which talks to the service over HTTP and has no
        graph of its own to ask.

Raises:
    ValueError: If *apply* is set with no *ingest_one*.

A RUNNING JOB'S OWN MODEL WINS over the server default, because they differ
in practice: `.env` sets `OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen3.8:27b-mlx` while every batch
script passes `vllm:qwen3.8-27b` per request. Reporting the default would
tell someone they are on Ollama while the run in front of them is on vLLM

verified_symbols.name: annotate_stall

Only a RUNNING job can stall. A finished job's counter stopped moving
because it finished, and flagging that would train a reader to ignore the
flag -- which is the failure mode of every alert that cries wolf.

verified_symbols.name: read_graph_snapshot
verified_symbols.doc:
Totals and the newest publication, read straight back from the catalog.

READ BACK, NOT REMEMBERED. The point of showing the last entry is to prove
that writes are LANDING; a value cached from the write path would have
reported success throughout the tiled outage that wrote nothing.

Degrades field by field: an unreadable catalog yields zeros and a null
entry, never an exception, because this is the view someone opens when the
stack is already broken.

**ZEROS ARE A WRONG ANSWER WHEN THE FILE IS MERELY ABSENT.** In production
the graph is reachable only over the Tiled API -- there is no catalog.db to
open -- and this function would then report `0 entities, 0 links` for a
perfectly healthy graph, on the one panel whose stated job is to prove that
writes are LANDING. An empty graph and an unopenable file are not the same
fact and must not render the same.

So a missing file falls through to the API. That costs more (measured:
~1,099 ms for 28,081 entities and ~1,198 ms for 53,892 links, paging ids at
5,000 a request, against ~5 ms for the SQL COUNT), which is why the SQL path
is still preferred when the file is there. Only when BOTH are unavailable
does this report zeros, and then it says so via `DEGRADED_KEY` rather than
letting the numbers speak for themselves.

verified_symbols.name: RefreshOutcome
verified_symbols.doc:
What happened to one paper, in terms a report can print.

Statuses are deliberately specific rather than a bool. "No PDF" and "the
parse produced nothing" and "the writes did not attach" are three different
facts about a corpus, and only the third is a bug.

verified_symbols.name: already_parsed_by
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether this paper's content already came from *parser*.

RESUME SUPPORT, and it is worth having because the alternative is
measurable: re-running the refresh over a corpus where 120 papers are
already done re-parses every one of them at ~20 s a paper, which is 40
minutes spent to write nothing. The parse is deterministic -- same PDF,
same parser, same filenames, same ids.

"CANNOT BE CHANGED BY PARSING IT AGAIN" IS ONLY TRUE WHILE THE WRITE PATH
HOLDS STILL, and this docstring used to state it unconditionally. The
2026-08-24 section-cap raise (20k -> `SECTION_TEXT_MAX_CHARS`) falsified it:
same PDF, same parser, LONGER stored text -- and the default `--resume
docling` would have skipped exactly the papers whose reference lists the
re-parse existed to restore. When anything about what gets STORED changes,
run with `--resume ''`; the parser name only records who parsed, not how
much was kept.

Requires at least one child: a paper with no figures and no sections has
not been refreshed, it has been skipped, and must not be mistaken for done.

verified_symbols.name: publications_with_dois
verified_symbols.doc:
Every publication carrying a DOI, with its real entity id.

Paged through :func:`forge.kg.views.iter_entities` rather than
``find_entities``, which clamps at 200 -- this graph holds 232
publications, so the clamp alone would hide a seventh of the corpus.

verified_symbols.name: child_entity_ids
verified_symbols.doc:
Entity ids of the figures and sections attached to a publication.

Found through the EDGES, not by matching a ``publication_id`` property: a
publication entity's id is a Tiled UUID while a figure's stored
``publication_id`` is an als-style id, and comparing the two is false for
every row -- the bug that left the Figures panel empty for every paper.

verified_symbols.name: link_child
verified_symbols.doc:
Attach a child to its publication by the publication's real entity id.

Idempotent, like ``upsert_edge``: re-running must not add a second
identical edge. Returns False when the child cannot be resolved, which the
caller must treat as "this row did not land".
verified_symbols.signature: store: Any, publication_entity_id: str, child_node_id: str, predicate: str, evidence: str=''

verified_symbols.name: refresh_publication
verified_symbols.doc:
Re-parse one paper and replace its sections and figures.

Dependencies are injected rather than imported so this is testable without
a PDF, a parser or a graph -- the parts that have actually gone wrong here
are the ORDERING and the verification, and those deserve tests that run in
milliseconds.

Args:
    store: A ``TiledKGStore``-shaped object.
    publication: A row from :func:`publications_with_dois`.
    parse: ``(Path) -> parse result dict``.
    extract_sections: ``(markdown) -> {name: text}``.
    find_pdf: ``(doi) -> Path | None``.
    stable_id: ``(text) -> str``, the id hash used at ingest.
    figure_terms: ``(doi) -> dict`` of redistribution terms.
    apply: When False, report what would happen and write nothing.
    skip_if_parser: Skip papers whose rows already come from this parser.
        Requires *entities_by_id*. The parse is deterministic, so a paper
        already parsed by it cannot be changed by parsing it again.
    entities_by_id: A snapshot of the graph's entities, for the skip check.

Returns:
    ``{status, doi, sections, figures, captions, deleted}``.
