verified_symbols.name: Hit
verified_symbols.doc:
A single keyword match found inside a section.

Attributes:
    taxon: Ontology category of the hit.
    slug: Normalized identifier, e.g. "giwaxs", "rietveld_refinement".
    name: Canonical display name.
    span: (start, end) character offsets in the section text.
    snippet: Up to 80-character context window centered on the match.

verified_symbols.name: RefinedExtraction
verified_symbols.doc:
LLM-refined extraction result for a single section.

`ok` DISTINGUISHES "the model said nothing" FROM "the model was never
reached", and the two must not look alike. When vLLM is unreachable
`llm_refine` logs a warning and returns an empty result, extraction silently
falls back to the keyword scanner, and the ingest reports success -- the same
shape as the project notes' 27 papers that landed with sections, figures and NO
entities while the run looked clean. Measured again this session: 10 of 25
papers in one re-extraction pass were keyword-only because the tunnel
dropped mid-run, and nothing in the graph recorded it.

Attributes:
    techniques: List of technique slugs.
    analyses: List of dicts with keys: method, software (optional),
        target_material (optional).
    instruments: List of instrument slugs.
    materials: List of canonical material names.
    confidence: Model-reported confidence in [0, 1].

verified_symbols.name: ResolvedTerm
verified_symbols.doc:
One extracted term, after the vocabulary has had its say.

`canonical` is the whole point of this type. A term the vocabulary
recognises becomes a real technique/analysis/instrument/material node; a term
it does not becomes a `candidate_term` node with a `mentions` edge, which is
an honest claim ("this section named this string") rather than a typed one.
Before this split, the unrecognised terms WERE the typed nodes -- which is how
`crystallization_regulation` came to be an experimental technique.

`surface` is kept even when canonical, because it is the evidence: it is what
the paper actually said, and the cleanup pass and any reviewer need it.

verified_symbols.name: SectionEntities
verified_symbols.doc: What one section yielded. The unit `link_section_entities` writes.

verified_symbols.name: PaperExtraction
verified_symbols.doc:
Aggregated extraction across all sections of a paper.

Attributes:
    techniques: Deduplicated technique slugs across all sections.
    analyses: Aggregated analysis dicts across all sections.
    instruments: Deduplicated instrument slugs.
    materials: Deduplicated canonical material names.
    per_section: Mapping of section_name -> list[Hit] from keyword pass.

verified_symbols.name: extract_keywords
verified_symbols.doc:
Run all KEYWORD_TAXONOMY patterns against section_text.

Returns one Hit per unique slug per taxon (deduped by slug within the
section).  The span and snippet are taken from the *first* match of each
slug.

Args:
    section_text: Raw text of a single paper section.

Returns:
    List of Hit objects found in the section, deduplicated by slug.

verified_symbols.name: llm_refine
verified_symbols.doc:
Refine keyword hits using a local LLM, Ollama or vLLM.

Uses a strict JSON-only system prompt.  Falls back to an empty
``RefinedExtraction`` on any failure (import error, timeout, JSON parse
failure).

ROUTES ON THE ``vllm:`` PREFIX, and it did not. The model pickers offer ONE
combined list -- ``server.py`` tags every vLLM entry ``vllm:<id>`` so callers
can route -- and this function fed whatever it was given straight to
``ChatOllama``. Selecting a vLLM model therefore asked OLLAMA for a model
called ``vllm:qwen3.8-27b``, which it does not have.

Measured against the running servers: ``vllm:qwen3.8-27b`` -> Ollama 404,
while the same id without the tag -> vLLM 200. The prefix is a routing tag,
never part of the model id, and `tiled_agentic.vision_tools` already treats it
that way.

WHAT THAT COST, and why it went unnoticed for 27 papers: the failure was
logged at DEBUG and swallowed into an empty ``RefinedExtraction``, so every
paper ingested with sections and figures and NO extracted entities, while the
ingest reported "8 sections, 11 figures" and looked like a success. The
entities are the part that makes a paper answerable in chat, so the graph grew
while getting no more useful. The log is now a WARNING naming the model and
the provider it was tried against.

Args:
    section_text: One bounded text chunk; sent in full.
    candidate_hits: Hits produced by :func:`extract_keywords`.
    model: Model name, optionally ``vllm:``-prefixed to route to vLLM
        instead of Ollama.  Defaults to the shared resolution in
        :func:`~als_knowledge_agent.graph.llm_defaults.default_ollama_model`
        (``OLLAMA_MODEL``, else the project default). This module used to
        carry its own ``"llama3.2"`` fallback, which meant a deployment that
        never set the variable ran THIS extractor on a different model from
        every other stage, with nothing reporting the difference.

Returns:
    A :class:`RefinedExtraction` populated from the LLM response, or an
    empty one on any exception.
verified_symbols.signature: section_text: str, candidate_hits: list[Hit], model: str | None=None, *, thinking_budget: int | None=None

verified_symbols.name: _resolve
verified_symbols.doc:
One free-text term -> a canonical or candidate `ResolvedTerm`.

DETERMINISTIC ON PURPOSE: exact slug/alias equality only. Ingest already runs
six concurrent `llm_refine` calls against a shared GPU box; asking a model to
canonicalise every term would roughly double that traffic and make ingest
nondeterministic run to run. Judging the leftovers is a bounded batch job
(~600 terms once), which is what the cleanup pass is for.

Returns None for a term that slugs to nothing -- an empty slug would become
`candidate_term:` with no identity.
verified_symbols.signature: vocab: Vocabulary, surface: str, category: str, *, software: str | None=None, definitions: dict | None=None

verified_symbols.name: extract_paper
verified_symbols.doc:
Extract techniques, analyses, instruments, and materials from all sections.

For each section:

1. Run :func:`extract_keywords` to get candidate ``Hit`` objects.
2. Refine overlapping chunks, including sections without keyword hits.
3. Use validated LLM output on success, otherwise local keyword fallback.
   Preserve the extraction method and coverage for every chunk.

Deduplicates techniques, analyses, instruments, and materials across
sections.  Stores the raw per-section Hit list in
``PaperExtraction.per_section``.

Args:
    sections: Mapping of section_name → section_text.
    model: Ollama model name passed through to :func:`llm_refine`.
    promote_vocabulary: Run global promotion inline; disable for JSON staging,
        which records observations for independent resolution.

Returns:
    A :class:`PaperExtraction` with aggregated, deduplicated results.
verified_symbols.signature: sections: dict[str, str], model: str | None=None, cache_dir: str | None=None, publication_id: str | None=None, thinking_budget: int | None=None, promote_vocabulary: bool=True

verified_symbols.name: QuoteLocation.is_verbatim
verified_symbols.doc:
True only for an EXACT hit.

A normalized match found the sentence after folding whitespace and
glyph variants, which means the stored text and the quote differ in
ways a reader would call cosmetic -- but "verbatim" is a claim about
bytes, and overstating it is how a quote that was subtly altered stops
being checkable.

verified_symbols.name: locate_quote
verified_symbols.doc:
Where *quote* sits in *section_text*.

Args:
    quote: The sentence the extractor reported, verbatim as it gave it.
    section_text: The section text AS STORED -- already truncated, so the
        returned offsets index the same string a reader can fetch back.

Returns:
    A :class:`QuoteLocation`. `match_kind` is `exact` when the quote is
    present byte-for-byte, `normalized` when it is present after folding
    whitespace and glyph variants, and `not_found` otherwise -- with no
    offsets, because a span nobody can dereference is worse than none.

verified_symbols.doc:
Require a located quote and a locally paired as-reported number/unit.

Missing or ambiguous evidence remains a candidate. A pass establishes text
support only: it cannot establish that an LLM assigned the correct scientific
meaning, or that the publication's measurement itself is correct.

verified_symbols.name: canonical_unit
verified_symbols.doc:
A unit string as the PAPER prints it, reduced to one spelling.

Papers print the ANGSTROM GLYPH -- extracted live from this corpus:
``'Å -1'`` (glyph, space, -1) and ``'Å'`` -- and the model copies
units verbatim because the prompt tells it to. An ASCII-only match refused
every one of a real paper's six extracted peaks. Spaces go, case folds,
the glyph becomes ``a``, and the superscript minus-one becomes ``^-1``;
what the string MEANS is still decided by the caller's closed sets, so an
unrecognised unit still refuses rather than guesses.

verified_symbols.name: to_nm
verified_symbols.doc: *value* in nanometres, or raise. Strict: the unit must be a table key.
verified_symbols.signature: value: float, unit: str, where: str=''

verified_symbols.name: to_ev
verified_symbols.doc: *value* in electronvolts, or raise.
verified_symbols.signature: value: float, unit: str, where: str=''

verified_symbols.name: to_deg
verified_symbols.doc: *value* in degrees, or raise.
verified_symbols.signature: value: float, unit: str, where: str=''

verified_symbols.name: length_in_nm
verified_symbols.doc:
A length in nm from a unit spelled however the paper spelled it.

The tolerant front door: folds the spelling, then converts strictly.

Returns:
    ``(nm, "")`` or ``(None, reason)``.
verified_symbols.signature: value: float, unit: str, where: str=''

verified_symbols.name: q_in_nm_inv
verified_symbols.doc:
One scattering vector magnitude in nm^-1, or the reason it cannot be.

The single place an inverse unit is interpreted. :func:`q_to_d_nm` is the
d-spacing view of the same conversion and delegates here, so the two cannot
disagree about which spellings are legal.

Args:
    q_value: The magnitude as printed.
    q_unit: The unit as printed, in any spelling `canonical_unit` folds.

Returns:
    ``(q_nm_inv, "")`` or ``(None, reason)``.

verified_symbols.name: q_to_d_nm
verified_symbols.doc:
A scattering vector magnitude as a real-space d-spacing in nm.

``d = 2*pi/q``, for the reciprocal units this corpus actually prints. An
unrecognised unit refuses with the reason rather than assuming nm^-1.

verified_symbols.name: unit_dimension
verified_symbols.doc:
What a unit string measures, or ``unknown``.

Returns ``length``, ``reciprocal``, ``angle``, ``energy`` or ``unknown``.

ANGLE AND ENERGY ARE HERE FOR THE GUARD, not for conversion. A stored
`first_peak_q = 8.3 deg` is a 2-theta filed as a q -- a real row in this
graph -- and it is only catchable if `deg` is RECOGNISED. Left out, it
reads as an unknown unit, and unknown units pass the guard by design (see
`dimension_mismatch`). So the set of units this function knows has to be
wider than the set it can convert.

Order matters: ``a-1`` is reciprocal and a sloppy length match would also
claim it, so reciprocal is tested first.

verified_symbols.name: dimension_mismatch
verified_symbols.doc:
Why *unit* cannot belong to *quantity_name*, or ``""`` when it can.

AN EMPTY STRING IS THE PASS, matching `unreachable_reason` and the rest of
this repo's refusal helpers, so a caller writes ``if reason: refuse`` and
cannot mistake a message for success.

Unknown quantity names and unknown units both PASS. This guard exists to
catch a contradiction it can prove, not to become a second, weaker copy of
the unit tables' own refusal -- an unrecognised unit already fails at
conversion with a better message, and refusing it twice in different words
would make the same paper unparseable for two different stated reasons.

Args:
    quantity_name: A name from `extraction.QuantityName`.
    unit: The unit as printed in the paper.

Returns:
    ``""`` when the pairing is possible, else a sentence naming both.

verified_symbols.name: ExtractedQuantity
verified_symbols.doc:
One number extracted from a publication, with its unit and provenance.

Attributes:
    value: The number exactly as reported (in ``unit``, not converted).
    unit: The unit it was reported in (e.g. ``"nm"``, ``"angstrom"``,
        ``"keV"``, ``"deg"``, or ``""`` for dimensionless quantities like
        a relative disorder). Recording the AS-REPORTED unit and
        converting explicitly, rather than converting in one's head while
        reading, is the point of this class.
    location: Where in the paper the value came from, as specifically as
        possible (e.g. ``"Table S1, 8nm-C18 row"`` or ``"Fig. 2f,
        first-order peak"``), so it can be re-checked against the source.
    caveat: Optional free-text qualification (e.g. "out-of-plane value;
        in-plane assumed equal per reported cubic symmetry").
    quote: The sentence the value was read out of, VERBATIM. Distinct from
        ``location``, which only names a region of the paper -- and the
        distinction matters because evidence entities were being created
        with ``location`` as their text, i.e. holding the word "results"
        where a checkable quotation was intended.

verified_symbols.name: PublicationRecord
verified_symbols.doc:
Everything extracted from one publication, with global identification.

Attributes:
    title: The paper's title.
    identifier: A persistent identifier -- DOI or arXiv id (e.g.
        ``"arXiv:2509.10849"``).
    quantities: Named extracted values (e.g. ``"superlattice_period"``,
        ``"edge_length"``, ``"beam_energy"``), each with unit and
        provenance.
    sample_label: Which of the paper's samples these values describe, when
        a paper reports several (e.g. ``"8nm-C18"``); empty if singular.
    access_note: How the full text was obtained and what was/wasn't
        available (e.g. "arXiv full text; SI figures not captured"), so a
        later reader knows which checks were possible at extraction time.
    readings: Every extracted value in source order, including repeated
        names. ``quantities`` holds at most one per name; this holds all
        of them. See the field comment for why both exist.

verified_symbols.name: ObservationContext
verified_symbols.doc: Qualifications for one occurrence, not a paper-wide sample guess.

verified_symbols.name: ExtractedValue
verified_symbols.doc: One number the paper reports, with where it came from.

verified_symbols.name: ReportedPeak
verified_symbols.doc:
One scattering peak as the paper reports it.

THE UNIT OF EXTRACTION FOR PAPERS THAT NAME NO PHASE. Most OPV GIWAXS
papers -- measured on this corpus, where every one of the ten most relevant
papers for a PM6:Y6 sample was refused `morphology_not_simulatable` -- never
claim a simulatable mesophase. What they DO report is peak positions: a
lamellar (100) at ~2 nm and a pi-pi (010) at ~0.36 nm, each with an
orientation. Those positions are directly renderable as Bragg reflections
without asserting any structure the paper did not claim, which is what makes
a peaks-only simulation honest where a guessed morphology would be a
fabrication.

Either a d-spacing or a q-position identifies the peak; the paper's own
unit is kept verbatim (conversion refuses rather than guesses, downstream).

verified_symbols.name: PaperStructureExtraction
verified_symbols.doc: What a paper reports about a structure.

verified_symbols.name: attributed_phase_mentions
verified_symbols.doc:
Phase mentions that sit in a sentence attributing them to other work.

Reported separately rather than merely dropped so the skip is auditable:
this is the one place the deterministic guard chooses NOT to refuse, and a
silent skip would be indistinguishable from the term never appearing.

Returns:
    ``(matched_term, sentence)`` pairs, in the order they appear.

verified_symbols.name: names_unsimulatable_phase
verified_symbols.doc:
The first non-simulatable phase *text* names, if any.

Args:
    text: The paper's title, abstract and/or body -- whatever the caller
        gave the extractor. Checking the SAME text the model saw is the
        point: a guard reading different input than the classifier could
        disagree with it for uninteresting reasons.

Returns:
    ``(matched_term, rejection_reason)`` where the reason is one of
    :class:`GateRejection`'s closed set, or None when nothing matched. No
    new reason is introduced -- the decision entities and the per-run
    counters both key on that set, and widening it would silently
    invalidate the histories that already use it.

Example:
    >>> names_unsimulatable_phase("a well-ordered gyroid network")
    ('gyroid', 'gyroid_needs_mesh')
    >>> names_unsimulatable_phase("hexagonally packed cylinders") is None
    True
    >>> names_unsimulatable_phase(
    ...     "Other groups reported a gyroid here. We observe cylinders."
    ... ) is None
    True

verified_symbols.name: extract_structure_from_text
verified_symbols.doc:
Ask a model what structure a paper reports.

Args:
    text: Paper text -- an abstract, or the results section.
    title: Paper title, given to the model as context.
    model: A LangChain chat model, e.g. from
        ``forge.agents.simulation.run.build_model``. Injected rather than
        constructed here so the caller picks the provider and so tests can
        pass a scripted stand-in.
    max_chars: Maximum characters per model call. Longer documents use
        overlapping chunks and retain every distinct observation.
    max_retries: Extra attempts after a reply that will not parse or
        validate. The validation error is fed back, which is what usually
        fixes a near-miss.

Returns:
    The extraction, or ``None`` when the model never returns something
    valid. ``None`` means "we do not know", never "there is no structure":
    the caller must not treat it as a negative result.
verified_symbols.signature: text: str, *, title: str='', model: Any, max_chars: int=8000, max_retries: int=2

verified_symbols.name: _record_reported_quantities
verified_symbols.doc:
Record what the PAPER reported, before the gate decides what can run.

THE GATE DECIDES WHAT CAN BE SIMULATED. It should not decide what the paper
is recorded as having said, and until this existed it did exactly that:
`_record_quantities` and `_record_evidence` were reachable only from
`_link`, on the post-render success path, so every rejection `continue`d
past them and the paper's numbers were discarded.

Measured on the two-paper rebuild of 2026-09-03. Both papers extracted
correctly -- Freychet at 87.6 / 35.84 / 49.8 nm with verbatim quotes
(confidence 0.90), and the IS2VP SI at the published d = 39 nm annealed
(confidence 0.95) -- both were gate-refused, and the graph kept ZERO
quantity and ZERO evidence rows for either. The refusals were not even
wrong: one paper is a line grating this engine has no morphology for, and
the other tripped a false veto since fixed. A correct refusal to SIMULATE
is not a reason to forget what the paper measured.

IDEMPOTENT WITH `_link`, BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck.
`_quantity_node_id` hashes ``pub_path|name|value|unit`` and nothing about
the run, so the node this writes and the node `_link` later writes for the
same reading are THE SAME NODE. A simulated paper therefore ends up with
one quantity row carrying an extra `prov:used` edge, not two rival rows --
which matters because entity properties are create-only and a second row
could not be merged away afterwards.

ONLY THE PAPER'S OWN NUMBERS. `_publication_record` is the same builder
`gate_and_map` uses, so the dimensional-contradiction drop applies here
too; the mapper's ASSUMED defaults are not in scope, because they do not
exist until a candidate is built and they are not claims about the paper.

BEST-EFFORT. A paper that extracted is worth gating even if this fails, so
nothing here is allowed to abort the stage.

Returns:
    How many quantity nodes were written.
verified_symbols.signature: store: Any, pub_path: str, extraction: Any, *, identifier: str, title: str, aliases: tuple[str, ...]=(), model_name: str='', source_text: str=''

verified_symbols.name: _record_evidence
verified_symbols.doc:
Write the sentences a simulation's numbers were read out of.

THE DISTINCTION THIS MAKES. The provenance edge already carries the
quantities, which says WHAT was extracted. This says what the paper
actually SAID -- ``location`` is the extractor's own record of the text a
value came from, and until now it was buried in a JSON blob on an edge,
where nothing could search it, link to it, or disagree with it.

Separating the two is what makes a claim checkable without re-reading the
paper, and it is the thing that keeps an uncertain inference from
hardening into a definitive parameter: the quote stays visible beside the
number for as long as the number exists.

An EVIDENCE entity is safe to create even though properties are
create-only, because a quotation is immutable. A different reading of the
same sentence is a new assertion edge pointing at the same evidence, not an
edit.

BEST-EFFORT BY CONTRACT. The simulation and its provenance edge are already
durable when this runs; losing the evidence must not undo them.

Args:
    store: The KG store.
    sim_node: Node id of the simulation making the claim, or None when
        the quotation is being recorded at EXTRACTION time and no run
        exists. The quantity's own ``forge:supportedBy`` edge is written
        either way; only the simulation-side edge is conditional.
    pub_path: Path of the publication quoted.
    candidate: The simulation candidate (for the extractor's identity).
    quantities: Extracted quantities, each possibly carrying a ``location``.
    aliases: Other identifiers this publication is stored under, passed to
        :func:`_section_node_for` so the ``forge:extractedFrom`` edge can be
        found when the sections were written under the paper's DOI and this
        stage resolved it by OpenAlex id.

Returns:
    How many evidence nodes were written.
verified_symbols.signature: store: Any, sim_node: str | None, pub_path: str, candidate: Any, quantities: list[dict[str, Any]], *, aliases: tuple[str, ...]=()

verified_symbols.name: _locate_in_any_section
verified_symbols.doc:
Find the section a quote is ACTUALLY in, when the label does not lead there.

THE LABEL IS THE EXTRACTOR'S OPINION; THE TEXT IS EVIDENCE. `location` comes
back as "results", and a great many papers in this corpus have no section
called anything like that -- docling's heading detection fails on them and
the entire body lands in one `preamble` blob, 20,000 characters at the
truncation cap. The sentence is right there in the stored text; only the
name over it disagrees.

Measured over all 656 evidence rows in the live graph:

    located in the labelled section    289   44.0%
    located ONLY by this fallback      253   38.5%
    not in any section of that paper   112   17.0%
    publication has no sections          3    0.5%

So 44% -> 82.5%.

THIS IS NOT A LOOSER GUESS THAN THE LABEL MATCH -- IT IS A STRICTER ONE.
`_section_node_for` matches on the section's NAME and refuses when several
match, because a wrong `extractedFrom` edge asserts a sentence came from
somewhere it does not appear. This function never matches on a name at all:
it only accepts a section whose stored text CONTAINS the quote, which is the
very thing the edge claims. An exact hit is preferred over a normalised one,
and among equals the shortest section wins -- `preamble` frequently holds
the whole paper, so the shorter of two containing sections is the more
specific answer.

Returns `(section_node, QuoteLocation)`, or `(None, None)` when the quote is
in no section of this paper -- which is the honest answer for a sentence the
extractor paraphrased rather than copied.
verified_symbols.signature: store: Any, pub_path: str, quote: str, *, aliases: tuple[str, ...]=(), sections: list[dict[str, Any]] | None=None

verified_symbols.name: _section_text_for
verified_symbols.doc:
The section's text AS STORED, or "".

THE STORED STRING, not the parsed one: `run_pdf_parse` truncates at
`SECTION_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` before writing, so an offset computed against the
full text would dereference to the wrong characters -- or past the end --
for any section that was cut. This is the only string a reader can fetch
back, so it is the only one the offsets may index.

verified_symbols.name: _section_page_for
verified_symbols.doc:
The page the section starts on, when the parser reported one.

None rather than 0 for a section whose parser could not say: "unknown" and
"page zero" are different claims.

verified_symbols.name: _stable_evidence_id
verified_symbols.doc:
Deterministic id for one quotation from one paper.

Keyed on the TEXT, so the same sentence extracted twice is one evidence
node with two assertions pointing at it, rather than two copies.

verified_symbols.name: entity_slug
verified_symbols.doc:
THE slug function for entity identity and lookup keys.

`forge.kg.paths.slug` with hyphens mapped to underscores: inherits its
Greek-letter and NFKD folding, keeps the underscore convention every live
node id already uses. Returns "" for text that slugs to nothing rather than
the sentinel "unknown" `paths.slug` uses -- an empty string is falsy, which
is what callers actually branch on.

verified_symbols.name: VocabEntry
verified_symbols.doc: One canonical term.

verified_symbols.name: Vocabulary
verified_symbols.doc: The loaded vocabulary: lookup by slug or alias, taxonomy export.

verified_symbols.name: Vocabulary.match
verified_symbols.doc:
The canonical entry *term* denotes, or None.

Deterministic only -- exact slug/alias equality after `entity_slug`
normalisation. No fuzzy matching: a wrong merge in a provenance graph is
effectively unrecoverable (see `forge/kg/aliases.py`'s docstring), so
anything cleverer belongs in the reviewed cleanup pass, not here.
verified_symbols.signature: self, term: str, category: str | None=None

verified_symbols.name: Vocabulary.match_smiles
verified_symbols.doc: Resolve a typed SMILES input to its named molecular entity.

verified_symbols.name: Vocabulary.match_within
verified_symbols.doc:
The entry whose own PATTERN fires inside *term*, or None.

Args:
    term: A free-text surface, e.g. ``"RSoXS chamber (high vacuum)"``.
    category: Restrict to one category, or None for any.

Returns:
    The single entry whose pattern matches, or None when none or SEVERAL
    do -- an ambiguous surface is refused rather than assigned, on the
    same reasoning `match` gives for refusing fuzzy equality.

WHY THIS IS NOT FUZZY MATCHING. The patterns here are the ones
`extract_keywords` already runs against raw section text to decide that a
section is about a technique at all; they are word-boundary anchored and
hand-written per entry. Applying them to a model's ANSWER is the same
test on a shorter string, not a new and looser one.

WHY IT WAS NEEDED. `match` is exact-equality on slug or alias, so a
surface any richer than the bare alias falls through to
`candidate_term`. Measured on one RSoXS methods paper, every one of
these was extracted correctly and placed nowhere:

    "polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering"
    "RSoXS chamber (high vacuum)"
    "liquid environment RSoXS instrument at NSLS-II"
    "NEXAFS spectroscopy (calibrated spectra)"

The first contains the `rsoxs` alias verbatim; the rest contain
`\bRSoXS\b` or `\bNEXAFS\b`, which are that entry's own patterns.
Live, before this: 138 RSoXS papers in the graph and ZERO
`describesTechnique` edges to the rsoxs node.
verified_symbols.signature: self, term: str, category: str | None=None

verified_symbols.name: Vocabulary.technique_profile
verified_symbols.doc:
Describe mentioned families without claiming methods were combined in a study.

Families overlap. A multimodal candidate requires distinct techniques
spanning measurement families; preparation steps and a single hybrid
technique cannot establish multimodal experimentation.

verified_symbols.name: Vocabulary.taxonomy
verified_symbols.doc:
The `KEYWORD_TAXONOMY` shape, for `extract_keywords`.

Only entries with patterns participate in keyword scanning; alias-only
entries still resolve through `match`.

verified_symbols.name: canonical_smiles
verified_symbols.doc:
Normalize atom order while retaining isotopes, stereochemistry and salts.

Wildcard/polymer structures and extended SMILES are unresolved. Missing
RDKit is also unresolved, never a punctuation-stripped pseudo-identity.

verified_symbols.name: structure_slug
verified_symbols.doc: A molecular graph key, not a name or fingerprint-similarity key.

verified_symbols.name: pubchem_structure
verified_symbols.doc:
Resolve a unique exact-name PubChem result; ambiguous/outage means unknown.

Called only for a supported new material at promotion, not for every token.
The caller persists successful results, including the database identifier.

verified_symbols.name: molecular_name_candidate
verified_symbols.doc:
Reject explicit bulk-material and FORM descriptors from molecular name matching.

See `_FORM_DESCRIPTORS` for the measured cases the form words were added for.

verified_symbols.name: formula_ambiguous
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether a structure states a FORMULA but not a material.

True for:

* a single neutral atom with no hydrogens -- ``[C]``, ``[Au]``, ``[Fe]``,
  ``[Si]``: the bulk element, whose allotropes and forms (graphite, diamond,
  carbon black, nanotubes; foil, powder, nanorods) all share it;
* a structure containing a metal or metalloid and no C-H bond -- ``O=[Si]=O``,
  ``O=C([O-])[O-].[Ca+2]``, ``[O]=[Ti]=[O]``, ``B#N``: a formula unit of an
  extended solid, whose polymorphs (quartz, coesite, fused silica; calcite,
  aragonite; anatase, rutile; h-BN) all share it.

False for molecules (ethanol, O2, PC71BM, Pd(PPh3)4) and for ions of a
single element (``[Ca+2]``), which name a species rather than a solid. An
unparseable structure is not ambiguous here -- it is not an identity at all,
and `canonical_smiles` refuses it already.

verified_symbols.name: plain_inorganic_name
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether *label* names the bare substance of *smiles*, not a form of it.

Plain: the element symbol (case-sensitive, so the word "in" is not indium),
the element name, the written formula (``PbI2``, ``CaCO3``), or a systematic
name built from element names and anion words (``sodium chloride``,
``lead(II) iodide``, ``silicon nitride (Si3N4)``) naming only elements the
structure contains. Anything else -- graphite, calcite, coesite, fused
silica, stainless steel, h-BN, saline -- names a form, a polymorph, a
mineral or a mixture, and the formula does not identify it.

verified_symbols.name: structure_identifies
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether a resolved structure may stand as *label*'s material identity.

THE SEAM THAT MERGED SEVEN CARBONS. Promotion keyed every material on
``structure_slug(smiles)``, so two names whose authority returned the same
structure became one vocabulary entry -- right for ``EtOH``/``ethanol``,
wrong for ``graphite``/``diamond``, which share a formula and nothing else.
A formula is an identity only for a molecule. So the structure identifies
*label* when:

* the label is a molecular name at all (`molecular_name_candidate` -- no
  form words such as foil, nanotube, black, glass), AND
* the structure is a molecule, or the label is the PLAIN name of the bare
  substance (`plain_inorganic_name`): "carbon", "C", "calcium carbonate",
  "CaCO3" -- never "graphite", "calcite", "fused silica".

Everything else keeps its own name as its identity and gets its own entry;
the structure is kept as a hint, never as the key.

verified_symbols.name: EmbeddingUnavailable
verified_symbols.doc: No embedding model is configured, or the endpoint refused.

verified_symbols.name: EmbeddingBatch
verified_symbols.doc:
Vectors plus the identity of the space they live in.

`model` and `dim` travel WITH the vectors rather than being assumed by the
caller, because the failure they prevent is silent: two quants of the same
model answer at the same dimension and cluster into confident nonsense.

verified_symbols.name: configured_model
verified_symbols.doc: The embedding model tag, or "" when none is configured.

verified_symbols.name: embed_texts
verified_symbols.doc:
Embed *texts*, in order, as one batch object.

Args:
    texts: The strings to embed. Empty strings are rejected rather than
        embedded: an embedding of "" is a well-formed vector pointing
        nowhere in particular, and it would join whatever cluster happened
        to be nearest.
    model: Tag override. Defaults to ``EMBEDDING_MODEL``.
    batch_size: Texts per request.
    timeout_sec: Per-request budget.

Raises:
    EmbeddingUnavailable: No model configured, the endpoint failed, or the
        reply's shape or dimension disagreed with itself.
    ValueError: *texts* contains an empty string.
verified_symbols.signature: texts: list[str], *, model: str | None=None, batch_size: int=DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE, timeout_sec: float=300.0

verified_symbols.name: EmbeddingCache
verified_symbols.doc:
Vectors keyed by (model tag, sha256 of the text), kept in a SQLite file.

WHY A CACHE AT ALL. Embedding costs ~31 ms/text on the local Ollama, so a
157k-term corpus is ~80 minutes, and the campaign embeds the same
`surface + snippets` text on every stage that touches a term. The text is the
key, so a re-run over an unchanged graph embeds nothing.

KEYED BY MODEL TAG, NEVER MIXED: see the module docstring. A different tag is
a different space, so it is a miss by construction.

float16 ON DISK. A 4096-d vector is 8 KB as float16 against 32 KB as float64;
at corpus scale that is ~1.3 GB against ~5 GB. The round-trip cosine error on
random 4096-d vectors is under 1e-3 (pinned in the tests).

NEVER FAILS AN EMBEDDING RUN. A cache that cannot be opened (a read-only home
directory, a path that is a directory, a corrupt file) or written degrades to
a per-process dict, with a WARNING: losing the cache costs time, and raising
would lose the run.

`hits` and `misses` count the texts `embed_texts_cached` took from the cache
and the texts it sent to the model, for the caller's report.

verified_symbols.name: EmbeddingCache.get_many
verified_symbols.doc:
``text_sha -> vector`` for every text that has one cached under *model*.

A row whose blob does not match its recorded `dim` is a miss, not an error.

verified_symbols.name: EmbeddingCache.put_many
verified_symbols.doc:
Store ``(text, vector)`` pairs under *model*, replacing any already there.

A vector whose length is not *dim*, or that float16 cannot hold faithfully,
is not stored.
verified_symbols.signature: self, model: str, dim: int, items: list[tuple[str, list[float]]]

verified_symbols.name: embed_texts_cached
verified_symbols.doc:
`embed_texts`, asking the model only for texts it has not already embedded.

Same contract as `embed_texts` (vectors in input order, one batch, `model` and
`dim` travelling with them, the same refusals), plus the cache.

THE RETURNED VECTORS ARE THE FLOAT16 ROUND TRIP whether they came from the
cache or from the model just now. Returning the model's full-precision vector
on a first run and the stored one on the second would make two runs over the
same graph disagree in the fourth decimal, which can move a pair across the
grouping threshold between runs. The cost is under 1e-3 in cosine.

A cached vector whose dimension differs from the others is a miss. When the
model now answers at a different dimension than the cached vectors it
returned, the same tag has changed underneath the cache, and those vectors are
re-embedded rather than blended into a second space.

Raises:
    EmbeddingUnavailable: As `embed_texts`.
    ValueError: *texts* contains an empty string.
verified_symbols.signature: texts: list[str], *, model: str | None=None, cache: EmbeddingCache | None=None, batch_size: int=DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE, timeout_sec: float=300.0

verified_symbols.name: TermGroup
verified_symbols.doc: Terms proposed as naming one thing.

verified_symbols.name: embedding_text
verified_symbols.doc:
The string actually embedded for one term.

Surface first so it dominates a short vector, then up to three snippets --
the same `limit=3` `vocab_cleanup._evidence_for` already uses, chosen there
because it is the cheapest thing that makes a row decidable by a human, and
the same reasoning applies to a model.

A term with NO snippets is embedded on its surface alone. That is not
equivalent, and callers are expected to route those to review rather than
trust a group they land in -- `group_terms` marks them.

verified_symbols.name: cosine
verified_symbols.doc: Cosine similarity. Returns 0.0 for a zero vector rather than dividing.

verified_symbols.name: _similarity_matrix
verified_symbols.doc:
All pairwise cosine similarities, as one normalised matrix product.

float32 rather than float64: the vectors come from a quantised model and
are compared against a threshold with two decimal places, so the extra
precision buys nothing and doubles a 180 MB working set.

Zero-norm rows are given a norm of 1 before dividing, which leaves their
similarities at 0.0 -- matching :func:`cosine`'s own contract rather than
producing NaNs that silently compare false against every threshold.

verified_symbols.name: group_terms
verified_symbols.doc:
Group *terms* by vector similarity, WITHIN each category.

Never across categories: a technique and the instrument that performs it
co-occur in every sentence about either, so their vectors are close for a
reason that is not sameness.

Greedy single-link from the most-connected term outward. Not k-means: the
number of real groups is unknown and most terms belong to no group at all,
which is the case k-means handles worst.

Args:
    terms: Rows carrying `surface`, `category`, and optionally `mentions`
        (used only to pick a representative) and `has_context`.
    vectors: One vector per term, positionally aligned.
    threshold: Cosine floor. See :data:`DEFAULT_THRESHOLD` for why this
        number is only meaningful on context-embedded vectors.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the lengths disagree -- vectors are matched to terms by
        POSITION, so a mismatch would relabel every term after the gap.
verified_symbols.signature: terms: list[dict[str, Any]], vectors: list[list[float]], *, threshold: float=DEFAULT_THRESHOLD

verified_symbols.name: snippet_around
verified_symbols.doc:
The window of *text* around where *surface* occurs.

NOT `text[:width]`, and the difference is the whole point. A section's
opening 280 characters are IDENTICAL for every term that section mentions,
so two techniques named in one Methods paragraph get the same context and
embed to nearly the same vector -- the surface form, a few words, is
drowned out by shared prose.

Measured on the live graph before this: `atomic force microscopy` and
`transmission electron microscopy` shared 2 of 3 snippets, `STXM` and
`Ptychography` shared 1 of 3, and the resulting clusters merged techniques
that are simply named together. At threshold 0.78 that was 3,607 terms
proposed for merging.

Returns "" when the surface does not occur, so the caller can record the
term as context-free rather than pretending a window is about it. That
matters: `group_terms` refuses to auto-apply any group holding a
context-free member.
verified_symbols.signature: text: str, surface: str, width: int=SNIPPET_WIDTH

verified_symbols.name: GraphRows
verified_symbols.doc:
Everything one pass over the graph yields; built once per campaign stage.

`candidates`: node id -> ``{"name", "surface_form", "category_guess",
"slug"}``. `surface_form` is the node's own surface, falling back to its
name; `category_guess` is "unknown" when the writer recorded none.

`sections`: section node id -> ``{"publication_id", "section_name",
"text"}``; a section with no recorded publication has "" there and counts
towards no publication's support.

`mentions`: candidate node id -> ``[(section id, edge id), ...]``, in edge
order. Only edges that point at a surviving candidate from a section that
exists are kept.

`skipped` counts what was dropped rather than raising: ``no_surface`` (a
candidate with neither `surface_form` nor `name`), ``dangling_section`` (a
mention edge whose subject is not a section), ``bad_properties``
(unparseable catalog JSON) and, after `fold_terms`, ``empty_fold`` (a
surface with nothing alphanumeric in it, which would fold onto every other
such surface).

verified_symbols.name: load_rows
verified_symbols.doc: Read the whole graph through a store. The complete read, never a prefix.

verified_symbols.name: load_rows_from_catalog
verified_symbols.doc:
The same rows, straight from the Tiled catalog's SQLite file. READ-ONLY.

Mirrors `scripts/cluster_candidate_terms.read_terms`: a whole-table scan for
an offline stage, where the store's per-node API would be thousands of round
trips. Measured there over this local file: every section's text is 51 ms for
22.6 MB, every link 12 ms for ~50k rows.

OPENED `mode=ro`, so a write is impossible at the driver level and not merely
by convention: on a WAL database a stray write handle contends with tiled's
own writers, and an offline stage is exactly what runs while an ingest is in
flight. A write attempt is a programming error and sqlite raises.

THE CATALOG'S SCHEMA, NOT `KGStore`'s. Nodes live in `entities(id,
entity_type, properties)` -- the name is inside `properties` -- and edges in
`links(id, subject_id, predicate, object_id)`; `KGStore`'s own file has
`nodes` and `edges` tables and is read through `load_rows`. Edge ids are the
link uuids, which is what `TiledKGStore.iter_edges` returns, so an id from
here is usable against the live store.

verified_symbols.name: repair_surface
verified_symbols.doc:
*surface* with PDF extraction damage undone.

NFKC, ligature code points to ASCII, whitespace collapsed, trailing `.,;:`
stripped -- always. The fixed damage table and the `(\w)based` hyphenation
run only when the vocabulary does not already know the surface as it stands:
a spelling the vocabulary matches is not damage, whatever it looks like.

Pass no vocabulary and the table always runs. `fold_terms` does exactly that
on purpose: its key is persisted across campaign stages, and a key that moved
whenever the vocabulary grew (it does, the tier-1 migration promotes terms)
would stop joining to its own earlier rows.

verified_symbols.name: fold_terms
verified_symbols.doc:
``term_key -> candidate node ids`` (sorted), one entry per distinct term.

A surface that folds to nothing is dropped and counted in
``rows.skipped["empty_fold"]``: all such surfaces would share one key.

verified_symbols.name: support
verified_symbols.doc: ``(distinct publications, distinct sections, edges)`` over *node_ids*' mentions.

verified_symbols.name: build_menu
verified_symbols.doc: The vocabulary entries a judge may map a *category* term onto, sorted by slug.

verified_symbols.name: assemble
verified_symbols.doc:
Everything a judge needs about the term the candidate nodes *node_ids* make up.

Raises:
    ValueError: *node_ids* is empty or names a node that is not a candidate.
verified_symbols.signature: rows: GraphRows, node_ids: list[str], vocab: Vocabulary, *, k: int=5

entries.integration_instructions: Decouple graph reads, retain source contexts, incomplete-read errors and evidence-constrained canonical choices. F2W B14 currently prompts over all existing names on its extraction tool path; bounded candidate search is an upgrade, not a claimed preserved ANN implementation.

verified_symbols.name: classify_surface
verified_symbols.doc:
The quarantine class of *surface*, or None when it should go on to a judge.

Args:
    surface: The term as extracted. Whitespace is collapsed first.
    vocab: The vocabulary; a surface it already matches is never quarantined.
    software_extra: Further program names, added to :data:`SOFTWARE_SEED`.
    generic_stoplist: Single words that name nothing (seeded empty; a human
        fills it from the most frequent unmatched single tokens). Empty
        entries are ignored.

Returns:
    The first class that applies, evaluated in this order and no other:
    ``junk:fragment`` (a bracketed acronym the words before it do not spell),
    ``junk:sentence`` (more than six words, or a comma), ``software``,
    ``junk:property_or_result``, ``procedure``, ``junk:generic``. None when
    no rule fires, and None for an empty surface (callers skip those).

    THE ORDER IS THE CONTRACT: a surface that fits two classes gets the
    earlier, so ``"synthesis"`` is a ``procedure`` even when it is also in the
    stoplist -- the stoplist only reaches words no earlier rule has taken.

Never raises on any string.
verified_symbols.signature: surface: str, vocab: Vocabulary, *, software_extra: Iterable[str]=(), generic_stoplist: Iterable[str]=()

verified_symbols.name: reasoning_fields
verified_symbols.doc:
Request-body keys that put thinking *level* on a vLLM request for *model*.

Args:
    model: The served model id (no `vllm:` tag, no `@level` suffix).
    level: `None` for thinking OFF -- the measured-accurate mode for this
        task (0.90 with 0 wrong auto-applies; thinking on produced prose and
        empty JSON in `vocab_cleanup`). Otherwise one of `low|medium|high|max`.
    thinking_budget: Optional `thinking_token_budget` cap; ignored when
        thinking is off.

Returns:
    `chat_template_kwargs`, `max_tokens`, and for a level the model takes the
    `reasoning_effort` key. A level the model family does not take (`medium`
    on GLM: reasoning.py measured it as the server default under another
    name, not a level) is dropped with a logged warning by
    `vllm_request_fields`, so the server default applies rather than a key it
    would misread. `max_tokens` still follows the requested level, because
    the budget is a property of how much room the caller asked for.

Raises:
    ValueError: *level* is not one of `EFFORT_MIN_TOKENS`.
verified_symbols.signature: model: str, level: Level | None, *, thinking_budget: int | None=None

verified_symbols.name: menu_first_schema
verified_symbols.doc:
The strict verdict schema for the menu-first framing.

`menu_slug` is an enum over the slugs actually sent (plus null), so under
guided decoding the model cannot name a slug that was not offered.
`disposition`, `canonical_label`, `category`, `aliases`, `evidence_quote`,
`confidence` and `reason` exist so the answer can be passed to
`cborg_resolution.validate_resolution` unchanged.

verified_symbols.name: ResolverConfig
verified_symbols.doc: Which endpoint to ask. Empty strings fall back to the provider's env defaults.

verified_symbols.name: StructuredTermResolver
verified_symbols.doc: Ask one model for one term's verdict and judge the answer deterministically.

verified_symbols.name: StructuredTermResolver.resolve
verified_symbols.doc:
One verdict for one term.

Never raises on anything the endpoint or the model can do: every such
failure is an abstain verdict with `errors` naming it (`retry`, `length`,
`unparseable`, `http_<status>`; `retry` means "not a verdict, ask again").
The only exceptions are a caller contract violation -- an unknown
`framing` or `level`, or a negative `thinking_budget` -- raised before any
request is built, because a wrong argument would otherwise turn a whole
campaign stage into silent abstains.
verified_symbols.signature: self, evidence: TermEvidence, *, round_key: str, framing: Literal['menu_first', 'evidence_first'], level: Level | None=None, thinking_budget: int | None=None, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None

Do not import donor model defaults or add independent direct inference transports. F2W B14 currently prompts over all existing names on its extraction tool path; bounded candidate search is an upgrade, not a claimed preserved ANN implementation.

verified_symbols.name: CampaignRun
verified_symbols.doc: One command's settings, its policy, and its state connection.

verified_symbols.name: open_run
verified_symbols.doc:
Resolve a command's options into a `CampaignRun`; exit 2 when they do not hold.

The campaign id defaults to the one the work directory already belongs to, and
only a fresh directory gets ``c<YYYYMMDD>``: a campaign runs for days, and a
default that moved with the date would refuse every command after midnight. An
id the caller names explicitly that disagrees with the stored one is refused.
verified_symbols.signature: *, work: Path | None=None, campaign_id: str | None=None, catalog: Path | None=None, apply: bool=False, limit: int=0, level: str | None='none', sample: int=100, policy_path: Path | None=None, needs_catalog: bool=False

verified_symbols.name: campaign_status
verified_symbols.doc:
What the Ingest tab's status panel shows. READ-ONLY; never raises.

Returns exactly the keys the client's `CampaignStatus` type takes from this
module: ``campaign_id, terms, histogram, rounds, plans, review_pending, probe``
(the route adds the rest: policy, the running process, the approval, the
ledger), plus ``errors``. A section that cannot be read comes back empty and
its reason lands in ``errors[section]``; an empty or missing work directory is
a status of zeros, not an exception.

verified_symbols.name: run_collapse
verified_symbols.doc:
Fold candidates to distinct terms, then settle what needs no model.

A term that is new gets exactly one outcome: a material is routed away from
every model round; otherwise a deterministic vocabulary match writes a
`campaign_deterministic` decision per candidate node; otherwise a quarantine
class (`term_quarantine`); otherwise it stays `new` for `route`. A term already
past `new` is never reset -- only its support numbers are refreshed -- so a
rerun after the graph moved on does not undo a later stage.

Materials are checked BEFORE the vocabulary: an exact-matching material would
otherwise become a decision the migration must refuse (`campaign_*` methods may
not target a material), and nothing about a material is the campaign's to decide.
verified_symbols.signature: run: CampaignRun, *, rows: GraphRows | None=None, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None

verified_symbols.name: run_route
verified_symbols.doc:
Decide which new terms a model will ever see.

``local`` for a term in at least ``min_pubs_local`` publications, else ``park``:
a one-paper term can not be promoted whatever a model says (promotion needs
three), so no call is spent on it. A local term in at least ``min_pubs_paid``
publications is also flagged ``paid_eligible`` -- recomputed for every local
term on each run, so raising the threshold in the policy takes effect.

verified_symbols.name: run_measure
verified_symbols.doc:
Run a stratified sample twice at each thinking level and report what each costs.

Twice, at temperature 0, because run-to-run AGREEMENT is the number that shows
whether a level is a stable judge: `vocab_cleanup` measured the model's
confidence unstable on identical input, and thinking-on produced prose and
empty JSON where thinking-off with a schema did not. Nothing here changes a
term: the first run's verdict is stored under ``<campaign>:measure:<level>``
(`verdicts` only), and the report is the product.

Exits 2 when the model server is not reachable.
verified_symbols.signature: run: CampaignRun, *, resolver: StructuredTermResolver | None=None, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None, rows: GraphRows | None=None, levels: str='none,low,high', gold_path: Path | None=None

verified_symbols.name: run_round1
verified_symbols.doc:
Ask the local model once per routed term, with the vocabulary menu in the packet.

Acceptance is `StructuredTermResolver`'s deterministic gate; a model that says
``map_to`` onto a policy-forbidden pair (SAXS -> GISAXS) is overruled here. One
answer is ONE vote: a term moves to state `round1` and waits for round 2, where
two independent votes are needed before anything is applied.

A `retry` (transport failure, 429, 503) is retried with a back-off and, if it
persists, NOT stored: the term keeps its state and the next run asks again. If
the server stays unreachable for three terms in a row the run stops with exit 3.

A dry run looks at ``--limit`` (default 20) terms and persists nothing.
verified_symbols.signature: run: CampaignRun, *, resolver: StructuredTermResolver | None=None, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None, rows: GraphRows | None=None

verified_symbols.name: Vote
verified_symbols.doc: One signal about one term, reduced to what `decide` needs.

verified_symbols.name: decide
verified_symbols.doc:
The agreement matrix: ``(action, target_slug, quarantine_class)``.

action is ``auto_apply | review | park | escalate | quarantine``. The first
matching rule wins:

1. Only ACCEPTED `map_to` votes count as votes for a slug.
2. One slug, named by two or more different framings, and no accepted vote for
   any other slug: ``auto_apply``. This is the one door to the graph: two
   independent signals, not one model asked twice.
3. Accepted votes for two or more slugs: ``escalate`` while no escalation vote
   (GLM at max thinking, a second model family, CBORG) exists, else ``review``
   when the term is in ``min_pubs_review`` publications, else ``park``.
4. Exactly one accepted map vote and every other vote an abstain or a novel:
   ``auto_apply`` only when the term is in ``min_pubs_review`` publications, the
   vote is the menu-first one, and a cluster vote names the same slug (a cluster
   that said "same thing" but not confidently enough to be accepted); otherwise
   as rule 3.
5. Two or more votes reject the term as the same kind: ``quarantine``.
6. Every vote says novel: ``park`` as a ``novel_candidate`` (the caller opens a
   review row when the term is well supported).
7. Anything else (abstains): ``escalate`` while the term is in ``min_pubs_paid``
   publications and GLM max has not been tried, else ``park``.

``min_pubs_paid`` defaults to ``min_pubs_review`` (they are both 3 by default);
the matrix has no other use for it, so the signature the plan gives still works.
verified_symbols.signature: votes: list[Vote], *, pubs: int, min_pubs_review: int, min_pubs_paid: int | None=None

verified_symbols.name: run_round2
verified_symbols.doc:
Collect independent signals on every round-1 term, then apply the matrix.

2a an embedding cluster judged as a group; 2b an evidence-first prompt (the
model names the term from the snippets before it sees the menu); 2c a second
model family (Codex Sol) for disagreements, when it is installed; 2d GLM at max
thinking for disagreements still open in at least `min_pubs_paid` publications,
capped by `max_glm_max_terms`. `decide` turns the votes into an action;
an `escalate` that nothing can still act on becomes a review row (well
supported) or a park. A term whose signal could not be collected (the server
went away) is left in `round1` for the next run: deciding on a partial set of
votes would turn an outage into a verdict.
verified_symbols.signature: run: CampaignRun, *, resolver: Any=None, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None, rows: GraphRows | None=None, cluster_judge: Callable[[str], str] | None=None, embed: Callable[..., Any] | None=None, codex_request: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], httpx.Response] | None=None

verified_symbols.name: run_round3
verified_symbols.doc:
Ask CBorg's escalation model about the best-supported unresolved terms.

One term per request, straight to the escalation model, with the earlier
proposals shown as hypotheses; its answer is ONE vote that `decide` weighs with
the rest. A cborg vote alone never applies, and one that disagrees with the
local votes sends the term to review.

NOTHING IS SPENT UNLESS ALL OF THESE HOLD, or the run exits 2 before any
request: ``--apply``; the budget ledger has scopes; an API key; the CBorg switch
is on; and the approval artefact only the user can write (`cborg_approval`) is
valid, for this campaign, for a stage that fits ``--limit`` (probe: 1 to
``cborg_probe_terms`` terms; full: needs a finished probe).

PER TERM, in this order: estimate the cost; `check_approval("term_campaign",
estimate)`; reserve it against the campaign's scope cap (inside the global cap);
only then send. A refused approval or reservation, three missing cost headers in
a row, or three failed calls in a row (429, 5xx, transport) stops the run with
exit 4. A failed call's reservation is cancelled; a call that was answered is
settled on the provider's header, and on its reservation when there is none.
verified_symbols.signature: run: CampaignRun, *, resolver: _PriorAwareResolver | None=None, store: ScientificArtifactStore | None=None, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None, rows: GraphRows | None=None, control: Callable[[], dict[str, Any]] | None=None, http_post: Callable[..., httpx.Response] | None=None

verified_symbols.name: run_park
verified_symbols.doc:
Park every term still waiting that no stage decided; record what it knew.

Nothing is deleted: a parked term stays a `candidate_term` in the graph with its
support recorded here (`parked.json`), and a later campaign with a larger
vocabulary or a lower threshold can pick it up again.

verified_symbols.name: run_plan
verified_symbols.doc:
Write one migration plan file per round that has decisions.

``<work>/<date>/round<N>_migration_plan.json`` is a `vocab_migration` plan
(``kind: vocabulary_migration``) whose ``decisions`` are `Decision` rows and whose
``apply_methods`` is exactly the campaign methods present, so the apply runs ONLY
those re-links and not the exact-alias ones the current vocabulary also implies.
The operator hands it to ``POST /api/graph/vocab_cleanup/apply`` -- dry run
first, which reports the drift since the plan was made; this module never writes
the graph.

A person's decisions (`campaign_human_review`) are recorded without a plan; they
are filed under the round that queued the term, and take that round's plan id and
activity here, at plan time. Given a store (tests; the service), the file also
carries a fresh ``plan_migration`` count so a reader can see the drift.
verified_symbols.signature: run: CampaignRun, *, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None, store: KGStore | None=None

verified_symbols.name: record_review_decision
verified_symbols.doc:
Apply a person's verdict on one term and take it off the review queue.

``map_to`` is checked as strictly as a model's answer would be, and refused with
``ValueError("<code>,<code>")`` naming every failure: ``slug_not_in_vocabulary``,
``category_conflict`` (the entry's category is neither the term's nor a declared
neighbour), ``forbidden_pair`` (the policy's), ``material_refused`` (a material is
never decided here). A good mapping writes one `campaign_human_review` decision
per candidate node. ``quarantine`` takes a `RejectKind`; ``park`` leaves the term
a candidate. Returns ``{"term_key", "state"}``.

Raises:
    KeyError: no such term.
    ValueError: the codes above, ``unknown_action`` or ``unknown_quarantine_kind``.
verified_symbols.signature: work: Path, *, term_key: str, action: str, target_slug: str | None, quarantine: str | None, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None

Do not import donor model defaults or add independent direct inference transports. F2W B14 currently prompts over all existing names on its extraction tool path; bounded candidate search is an upgrade, not a claimed preserved ANN implementation.

verified_symbols.name: read_all_nodes
verified_symbols.doc: Every node of a type -- the complete read, never a store's default prefix.

verified_symbols.name: read_all_edges
verified_symbols.doc: Every edge -- the complete read, never a store's default prefix.

verified_symbols.name: classify_node
verified_symbols.doc:
Place one node against the vocabulary, deterministically.

Returns:
    ``(verdict, target_slug, target_category)`` where verdict is one of:

    ``canonical``
        The name resolves to a vocabulary entry in the node's own category.
        Nothing to do.
    ``category_mismatch``
        The name resolves, but to an entry in a DIFFERENT category. The
        vocabulary states the right answer, so this is repairable without a
        model: re-point the edges at the entry's canonical node.
    ``unmatched``
        The name resolves to nothing anywhere. Only these need judgement,
        and only these should ever reach a model.
verified_symbols.signature: node: dict[str, Any], entity_type: str, vocab: Vocabulary

verified_symbols.name: Adjudication
verified_symbols.doc: One term's verdict, and how it was reached.

verified_symbols.name: adjudicate_term
verified_symbols.doc:
Decide what to do with one free-form node.

DETERMINISTIC FIRST, ALWAYS. `classify_node` settles `canonical` and
`category_mismatch` from the vocabulary alone, and those are 143 of the 708
live nodes. Sending them to a model would pay for an answer already on disk
AND expose it to being contradicted -- a model that decides `gisaxs` filed
under analysis should map to `saxs` is worse than no model, and the
deterministic path cannot make that mistake.

Args:
    node: Node row; `name` and (for candidates) `category_guess` are read.
    entity_type: The node's entity type.
    vocab: Vocabulary to judge against.
    judge: Injected LLM adjudicator for `unmatched` terms. Omitted means no
        model is available, and the verdict is `keep`/`no_model` -- NOT
        `reject`, because "we could not decide" must never become a delete.

Returns:
    An :class:`Adjudication`.
verified_symbols.signature: node: dict[str, Any], entity_type: str, vocab: Vocabulary, *, judge: Callable[[dict[str, Any], str, Vocabulary], Adjudication] | None=None

verified_symbols.name: quality_report
verified_symbols.doc:
Measure the entity layer. Reads only; writes nothing.

Args:
    store: Open store. Only `iter_nodes` and `iter_edges` are used, so a
        fake store is enough to drive this in tests.
    vocab: Vocabulary to judge against; loaded from disk when omitted.
    edge_limit: Page at most this many edges. None (the default) reads
        ALL of them -- see `UNBOUNDED`. A bound is reported back under
        ``truncated`` so one that binds cannot be mistaken for a small
        graph -- the silent-clamp failure this repo has now hit five times.
    include_history: Attach the scheduled snapshots' latest and trend
        (`vocab_quality_snapshot.snapshot_history`), which is how the
        `/api/graph/vocab_quality` route surfaces them. Best-effort.

Returns:
    A JSON-serialisable report. See the module docstring for the shape and
    for the live "before" numbers. ``scan`` says how long the complete read
    took and how many rows it saw.
verified_symbols.signature: store: KGStore, *, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None, edge_limit: int | None=None, include_history: bool=True

verified_symbols.name: format_report
verified_symbols.doc: Render a report as the fixed-width table the module docstring shows.

verified_symbols.name: build_llm_judge
verified_symbols.doc:
A judge for `adjudicate_term`, backed by a model.

THE RETURNED VERDICT IS VALIDATED, NOT TRUSTED. A `map_to` naming a slug that
is not in the vocabulary is downgraded to `novel` with the invented slug
recorded in the reason. That guard is not hypothetical politeness: the whole
apply path keys on the target existing, and a hallucinated slug would either
crash the apply or -- worse -- mint a new canonical node named after
something no vocabulary entry ever declared, which is the exact failure this
two-tier design exists to stop.

Args:
    model: Model string, `vllm:`-prefixed to route to vLLM.
    chat: Pre-built chat model, for tests. Injected rather than patched so
        the harness needs no network.

verified_symbols.name: propose
verified_symbols.doc:
Adjudicate every free-form node and return a reviewable proposal.

ORDER IS THE DESIGN. The deterministic pass runs over everything first and
only `unmatched` rows reach the model, so a run costs one model call per
genuinely unknown term -- 565 of 708 nodes live -- rather than 708.

Concurrency is 6-way for the same reason `extract_paper` uses it: measured on
this vLLM deployment, 6 concurrent requests complete in 7.2s total against
35.8s for Ollama, and serialising 565 calls would turn a two-minute pass into
twenty.

NOTHING IS WRITTEN TO THE GRAPH. The output is data; `apply` is a separate
entry point that defaults to a dry run.

Args:
    store: Open store. Reads via `iter_nodes` / `iter_edges` only.
    model: Model string for the judge, `vllm:`-prefixed to route to vLLM.
        Ignored when *judge* is supplied.
    vocab: Vocabulary to judge against; loaded from disk when omitted.
    limit: Adjudicate at most this many nodes needing a model (0 = all).
        The deterministic pass always covers everything -- it is free, and a
        partial deterministic pass would make the counts meaningless.
    max_workers: Judge concurrency.
    judge: Injected adjudicator, for tests. When both this and *model* are
        omitted, unmatched rows come back `keep`/`no_model` rather than
        being guessed at.

Returns:
    A proposal dict: header, counts, and one row per node.
verified_symbols.signature: store: KGStore, *, model: str | None=None, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None, limit: int=0, max_workers: int=6, judge: Callable[[dict[str, Any], str, Vocabulary], Adjudication] | None=None

verified_symbols.name: write_review_file
verified_symbols.doc:
Write a proposal as reviewable YAML and return the path.

YAML rather than JSON because a human edits this: it takes comments, and the
reviewer's job is to change `verdict` on the rows they disagree with.
verified_symbols.signature: proposal: dict[str, Any], path: Path | None=None, *, stamp: str=''

verified_symbols.name: merge_novel
verified_symbols.doc:
Append a review file's approved `novel` entries to vocabulary.yaml.

ONLY FROM A REVIEWED FILE. A `novel` verdict means "add a term to the
controlled vocabulary", which is the one action here that changes what every
FUTURE extraction will canonicalise -- so it does not happen on a model's
say-so. Refuses unless the file carries `reviewed: true`.

Duplicate slugs are skipped rather than overwritten: the vocabulary loader
already refuses duplicates, and silently replacing a curated entry with a
generated one is how a tuned pattern gets lost.

verified_symbols.name: apply_cleanup
verified_symbols.doc:
Execute a proposal. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT.

`apply=False` computes exactly the plan `apply=True` would execute -- through
`repair.plan_edge_moves`, the same pure function the real merge calls -- and
writes nothing. A dry run computed by a second code path is a dry run of
something else.

WHAT IS GATED, AND ON WHAT:

* `map_to` rows in the AUTO tier (exact alias, category fix, or an LLM
  mapping at or above the confidence floor onto a slug that exists) apply
  from an unreviewed file. Their answer comes from the vocabulary or from a
  verdict that has already been validated against it.
* every `reject`, every `novel`, and every low-confidence `map_to` REQUIRES
  `reviewed: true` in the file. A reject deletes an entity and
  `deleteEntity` CASCADES to every link at either end; that does not happen
  because a model was confident.
* a `novel` row additionally requires its slug to be IN THE VOCABULARY
  already -- run `merge-novel` first. Applying a novel row before then would
  have nothing to point at.

Merges go through `repair.merge_shadow_duplicate`, unchanged: it writes every
edge onto the canonical entity FIRST and deletes the duplicate only once they
are durable, aborting the delete if any write fails. A duplicate left behind
is cosmetic and visible; a duplicate deleted with an edge un-copied is data
loss nobody can see.

Args:
    store: Open store, used to create canonical nodes and read them back.
    review_path: The proposal file, reviewed or not.
    apply: Execute. Default False -- report only.
    limit: Act on at most this many rows (0 = all). Reported, never silent.
    vocab: Vocabulary; loaded from disk when omitted.

Returns:
    A report of what was done or would be done, per verdict.
verified_symbols.signature: store: KGStore, review_path: Path, *, apply: bool=False, limit: int=0, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None

verified_symbols.name: triage_proposal
verified_symbols.doc:
Sort a proposal into what needs a human and what does not.

THE ONLY VERDICT THIS CHANGES IS `novel` -> `keep`, and `keep` is the
do-nothing verdict: the node stays exactly as it is, a `candidate_term`
holding a term the vocabulary has not accepted. So an unsupported novel is
not deleted, not merged, and not promoted -- it stays quarantined, which is
what `candidate_term` exists for. Nothing here approves anything; the
`reviewed: true` gate on `apply` is untouched.

Every other row keeps its verdict and gains a `review` label saying why it
does or does not need reading:

``auto``
    Deterministic, or a high-confidence mapping onto an existing entry.
    Applies without review, as before.
``read``
    A judgement with consequences: a recurring novel, or a reject that would
    destroy edges.
``bulk``
    A reject whose node is already an orphan. Still gated behind
    `reviewed: true`, but approvable en bloc -- there is nothing to weigh.
``none``
    Already correct, or demoted to `keep`.

Args:
    proposal: A `propose` result, or a loaded review file.
    min_novel_edges: Edge support a novel needs to stay novel.
    min_reject_edges: Edge support at which a reject must be read.

Returns:
    A new proposal dict, same shape so `apply` can consume it, plus a
    `triage` block counting each bucket.
verified_symbols.signature: proposal: dict[str, Any], *, min_novel_edges: int=MIN_NOVEL_EDGES, min_reject_edges: int=MIN_REJECT_EDGES

A 2,400-row YAML is not reviewable; this is the same decisions ordered by
what they cost. Rows are grouped so the reader is answering one kind of
question at a time rather than switching between "is this a real technique"
and "may I delete this".

verified_symbols.name: plan_migration
verified_symbols.doc:
Every re-link, creation and retirement the current vocabulary implies. PURE.

Reads the WHOLE graph (`read_all_nodes` / `read_all_edges`, never a capped
prefix -- a missed edge would be cascade-deleted with its node) and writes
nothing.

Args:
    store: The store to read.
    vocab: Vocabulary; the effective one is loaded when omitted.
    decisions: Campaign decisions keyed by (category, candidate slug),
        consulted before any vocabulary rule. DEFAULTS TO None, which keeps
        the other caller (`vocab_quality_snapshot.write_snapshot`) exactly
        as it was.

Returns:
    A JSON-serialisable plan: ``relinks`` (one row per edge), ``creates``
    (target nodes that do not exist yet), ``retires`` (nodes that end with
    zero edges), ``kept_orphans`` (orphans not retired, and why), counts,
    and the timing of the complete read.
verified_symbols.signature: store: KGStore, *, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None, decisions: dict[tuple[str, str], Decision] | None=None

verified_symbols.name: decisions_from_plan
verified_symbols.doc:
The campaign decisions a plan file carries, keyed by (category, candidate slug).

The category in the key is the one `plan_migration` reads off an edge: one of
`_RELATION`, else "" (no category recorded, or one the writer does not have a
relation for). The campaign names that case `unknown` -- or whatever odd category
the extractor wrote -- in `Decision.category`, so the key folds it the same way;
without that, a decision for such a candidate matches none of its edges
(`decisions_unmatched`) and nothing is applied.

Raises:
    ValueError: a decision's method is not in `CAMPAIGN_METHODS`. The method
        becomes the re-link method that `apply_methods` gates on, so a stray
        one (``exact_alias``) would slip a model's answer past that gate.
    TypeError: a row has a key `Decision` does not (`Decision.from_dict`).

verified_symbols.name: apply_migration
verified_symbols.doc:
Execute the migration. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT: returns the plan and writes nothing.

The plan is recomputed here, from the graph as it is NOW, by the same pure
`plan_migration` the dry run used -- never replayed from a file that may be
hours old. A reviewed plan file only contributes its counts, reported as
``drift`` so an operator sees whether the graph moved since review.

Order is load-bearing: (1) create missing target nodes, (2) write each new
edge, (3) delete the old edge only if (2) succeeded, (4) retire nodes,
each re-checked for zero links at the store immediately before the delete.
A failure at any step leaves the old edge -- and therefore the node -- in
place; re-running is safe and recognises what already moved.

Args:
    store: The service's store.
    apply: Execute. Default False.
    limit: Re-link at most this many edges (0 = all); retirement then only
        considers nodes the processed rows emptied, plus true orphans.
    vocab: Vocabulary; the effective one is loaded when omitted.
    reviewed_plan: The plan file the operator approved, for drift -- and
        its optional ``apply_methods`` list, which restricts the run to
        those re-link methods (e.g. leave ``category_fix`` for later: it
        overrides the extractor's own category guess). Its ``decisions``
        list (campaign decisions, see the module docstring) is read by
        `decisions_from_plan` and handed to `plan_migration`; set
        ``apply_methods`` to a subset of `CAMPAIGN_METHODS` with it.
    methods: The same restriction as an argument; wins over the file.
verified_symbols.signature: store: KGStore, *, apply: bool=False, limit: int=0, vocab: Vocabulary | None=None, reviewed_plan: dict[str, Any] | None=None, methods: list[str] | None=None

* A cost header: that cost, whatever the status -- an error response that

* An error response (status >= 400) with NO header: the reservation is
  CANCELLED. A 429 or a 5xx produced no completion, so nothing was billed;
  leaving it charged at the reservation burned the budget on every retry of

  charge may exist): the reservation is the charge (`settled_estimated`),
  never $0 -- see `ScientificArtifactStore.settle_budget`.

verified_symbols.name: plan_reextraction
verified_symbols.doc:
Which sections to re-extract, and which cases that closes. Writes nothing.

A case names a publication, a section NAME and a chunk id; the graph is
where the section's text lives, so each case is joined to its `paper_section`
node through the publication and the name. The join is never guessed:
two sections of one paper with the same name (`skipped_ambiguous_section_
name`) or none (`skipped_missing_section`) leave the case untouched, because
re-extracting the wrong text would close a case against a chunk of a different
section.

Args:
    artifacts: The artifact store holding the cases. Only `connect()` is used,
        so a read-only shim works.
    store: The graph; only `iter_nodes("paper_section")` is used.
    case_types: `incomplete_extraction` (the model call failed) and/or
        `low_confidence`.
    model: The extraction model. Must start with `vllm:` to carry a budget.
    thinking_budget: Thinking tokens per chunk; 0 is thinking off.
    max_tokens: Output tokens the SERVICE must allow
        (`ALS_EXTRACTION_MAX_TOKENS`); the apply refuses to run below it.
    limit: At most this many sections (0 = all), in publication order.
    reasons: Keep only cases whose `reason` contains one of these (e.g.
        `LengthFinishReasonError`), case-insensitively.
    probe: Mark the plan so a DRY RUN also calls the extractor (no writes).

Returns:
    The plan dict: `kind`, `planned_at`, `model`, `thinking_budget`,
    `max_tokens`, `case_types`, `reasons`, `code_version`, `plan_id`,
    `publications[].sections[]` (`section_id`, `section_name`, `case_ids`,
    `chunk_ids`) and `counts`.
verified_symbols.signature: artifacts: ScientificArtifactStore, store: KGStore, *, case_types: tuple[str, ...]=('incomplete_extraction',), model: str='vllm:glm-5.3-flash', thinking_budget: int=0, max_tokens: int=8192, limit: int=0, reasons: tuple[str, ...]=(), probe: bool=False

verified_symbols.name: apply_reextraction
verified_symbols.doc:
Execute a re-extraction plan. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT: writes nothing.

A dry run reads the graph and reports what an apply would do -- sections,
already-done sections, the old term edges that would go -- and calls no model,
unless the plan sets ``"probe": true``, in which case it also runs the
extractor over the planned sections (WITHOUT a publication id, so the extractor
registers no artifact and enqueues no case) and reports what each section
would yield, still writing nothing.

The apply order per publication is load-bearing: (1) extract every planned
section that is not already done -- a raise here ends the publication with
nothing written; (2) per section that answered, delete its old term edges and
only then link the new ones, chunk records stamped with the plan id; (3) close
the planned cases against the new chunks. A section whose every chunk failed
again is left exactly as it was.

Args:
    store: The service's store.
    apply: Execute. Default False.
    limit: Process at most this many sections (0 = all); the rest are counted
        as ``over_limit``, never dropped silently.
    reviewed_plan: The plan file (`plan_reextraction`'s output). Its own
        ``plan_id`` stamps the chunks, so a rerun of the file is a no-op.

Returns:
    ``{"kind", "applied", "plan_id", "done", "failures", "failure_count"}``,
    plus ``"plan"`` on a dry run, ``"probe"`` when probing, and ``"error"``
    (nothing written) when a precondition fails.
verified_symbols.signature: store: KGStore, *, apply: bool=False, limit: int=0, reviewed_plan: dict[str, Any]

verified_symbols.name: _record_provenance
verified_symbols.doc:
One plan node and one activity node for this apply; never fails the run.

The work is already in the graph, so a refused provenance edge is reported
(`provenance_error`) and logged, not raised -- failing here would throw away
the run's result report, not the writes.
verified_symbols.signature: store: KGStore, plan: dict[str, Any], report: dict[str, Any], *, run_started: float
