verified_symbols.name: ensure_namespaces
verified_symbols.doc:
Seed :data:`NAMESPACES` on the server. Idempotent.

``upsertNamespace`` is by name, so re-running is free. Call this before the
first write from a fresh catalog: the ``namespaces`` table is created by
the graph router at startup, not by the alembic migration, so a
just-migrated database has the table but no prefixes in it.

verified_symbols.name: resolve_node_id
verified_symbols.doc:
Resolve a catalog *path* to its Tiled node id, or None.

None is the normal answer for an entity that does not correspond to a
catalog node (a publication, a technique, an agent run). It is not an
error, and callers must not treat it as one.

verified_symbols.name: find_entity_id
verified_symbols.doc:
Find an existing entity for a catalog *path*, by its canonical uri.

The server has no uri filter, so this pages. ``entity_type`` narrows the
scan when known and is worth passing.

IT NOW INFERS THE TYPE FROM THE PATH when the caller does not pass one,
and that is a correctness fix rather than a speed one. The scan gave up
after 10,000 entities; the graph crossed that on 2026-08-25 (10,179), so
`upsert_edge` began refusing endpoints that EXIST -- "endpoint missing from
the graph" for `materials/pm6-y6`, which is right there. Every edge write
whose endpoint was not in the write-side memo was affected, silently, and
the symptom was a simulation that ran and then linked to nothing.

A narrowed scan is also bounded by a number that grows slowly: 47 materials
against 10,179 entities. The cap is raised as well, because narrowing helps
only the types that are small -- `paper_section` alone is 3,451 -- and a cap
that is merely larger will be crossed again.
verified_symbols.signature: path: str, entity_type: EntityType | None=None, client: GraphQLClient | None=None

verified_symbols.name: upsert_entity
verified_symbols.doc:
Insert or update an entity, reporting only whether it worked.

The boolean face of :func:`upsert_entity_id`, kept because most callers
only need to know that the write landed.

verified_symbols.name: upsert_entity_id
verified_symbols.doc:
Insert or update an entity and RETURN ITS ID.

The server has no upsert, so this is find-by-uri then create-or-update.
Best-effort: returns None if the endpoint is unreachable or the mutation
fails, logs a warning, and never raises. A KG outage is not a simulation
failure.

Returning the id is what lets a caller stop searching for what it just
wrote. ``createEntity`` has always answered with ``{ id nodeId }`` and this
function always discarded it, so every later reference to the entity paid a
fresh ``find_entity_id`` scan -- and the server cannot filter by uri, so
that scan pages the entire table.

Args:
    entity: The entity to write. Its ``path`` is the identity.
    client: GraphQL client. Defaults to the configured endpoint.
    assume_new: Skip the find and create directly. Only for paths the
        caller KNOWS are unique to it -- a run recorder's ``runs/<uuid>/...``
        entities cannot collide, and the find can only ever exhaust the
        scan and return nothing.
    resolve_node: Look up a Tiled node id to bind. False for paths that
        name no catalog node (runs, turns, tool calls), where the lookup is
        a guaranteed-None round trip.

Returns:
    The entity's id, or None if the write failed.
verified_symbols.signature: entity: Entity, client: GraphQLClient | None=None, *, assume_new: bool=False, resolve_node: bool=True

verified_symbols.name: delete_entity_by_id
verified_symbols.doc:
Delete one entity by its server-assigned id.

THE ID IS THE ONLY UNAMBIGUOUS HANDLE. :func:`delete_entity` finds its
target by re-deriving a canonical uri from a path, and that derivation runs
through :func:`_canonical_uri`, which spells the host from
``get_settings().tiled_uri``. A repair holds ids read out of a snapshot of
the graph itself, so going back through the path would re-introduce a
host-spelling mismatch (``localhost`` vs ``127.0.0.1`` vs the container
name) that no error would report: the lookup would simply find nothing and
the delete would return False as though the entity were already gone.

CASCADES TO LINKS: every edge with this entity at either end goes with it
(verified against the running server). Any edge worth keeping must be
rewritten onto its new owner BEFORE this call, never after.

Args:
    entity_id: The server's entity id, as read back from ``entities``.
    client: GraphQL client. Defaults to the configured endpoint.

Returns:
    True if the server reported the entity deleted.

verified_symbols.name: create_link
verified_symbols.doc:
Create a directed link (edge) between two entities, by catalog path.

Both endpoints must already exist as entities -- this does not invent them,
because an edge to an entity nobody described is a dangling reference that
reads as data. Best-effort: returns False and logs rather than raising.

Args:
    source_path: Catalog path of the subject entity.
    target_path: Catalog path of the object entity.
    relation_type: The relation; mapped to a CURIE by :func:`predicate_for`.
    metadata: Optional confidence/evidence, stored in the link properties.
    client: GraphQL client. Defaults to the configured endpoint.

Returns:
    True if the link was created.
verified_symbols.signature: source_path: str, target_path: str, relation_type: LinkType, metadata: LinkMetadata | None=None, client: GraphQLClient | None=None

verified_symbols.name: link_ids
verified_symbols.doc:
Write one edge between two entity ids, with a raw CURIE *predicate*.

The lower level under :func:`create_link`, for callers that already hold
entity ids and need a predicate outside :class:`~forge.kg.links.LinkType` --
the workflow vocabulary (``wf:executed``, ``prov:used``) is a fixed set of
strings in :mod:`forge.kg.ontology`, not a user-extensible relation table,
so routing it through the enum would mean growing the enum every time the
recorder learns a new edge.

Predicates are stored EXPANDED and compacted back to CURIEs on read, so the
prefix must be registered first -- see :func:`ensure_namespaces`.

Args:
    subject_id: Entity id of the subject.
    predicate: CURIE, e.g. ``"prov:used"``.
    object_id: Entity id of the object.
    properties: JSON-serialisable payload stored on the edge.
    client: GraphQL client. Defaults to the configured endpoint.
    label: Human-readable endpoint description, for log messages only.

Returns:
    True if the edge was written.
verified_symbols.signature: subject_id: str, predicate: str, object_id: str, *, properties: dict[str, Any] | None=None, client: GraphQLClient | None=None, label: str=''

verified_symbols.name: find_links
verified_symbols.doc:
Edges matching a triple pattern, filtered by the server.

ANY SUBSET OF THE THREE MAY BE GIVEN, and that is a change from the version
that required a subject positionally. `Query.links` declares `subjectId`,
`predicate` and `objectId` as INDEPENDENT Optionals
(`tiled/graph/schema.py:410`), so "who points at this node?" has always been
one server-side query -- and was unreachable from Python because this
helper, the only server-filtered link reader in the repo, would not express
it. Every reverse walk therefore paged the whole graph instead. Verified
live before the signature changed: `links(objectId:)` returns matching rows.

All three empty is REFUSED rather than silently paging 50k links. That is
`views.iter_links`, which exists for it and says so at the call site.

ONE QUERY PER SUBJECT, not a scan of the whole graph. The obvious
alternative -- :func:`forge.kg.views._load` and filter -- pages 19k links
to answer a question about one node. ``links(subjectId:)`` works, unlike
the nested ``Link.subject`` / ``Link.object`` resolvers, which return null
for every link in this tiled build.

**FILTERING IS DONE SERVER-SIDE AND THE RESULT IS PAGED. Both matter, and
the first version of this function did neither.** ``Query.links`` defaults
to ``limit: 100`` (``tiled/graph/schema.py:416``). Fetching one unfiltered
page and filtering predicates in Python therefore answered questions about
the first 100 edges only -- and a publication in this graph carries
hundreds of ``schema:author`` edges, so those 100 rows were ALL authors and
the paper's figures were invisible. Measured: papers reporting "0 of 33
edges landed" immediately after those 33 edges had been written
successfully. Same shape as the 200-row ``find_entities`` clamp that has
already cost this project a corpus sweep.

Args:
    subject_id: Entity id at the tail of the edge. Empty matches any.
    predicate: CURIE to match, e.g. ``"schema:image"``. Empty matches any.
        Sent to the server, which expands it against the namespace table.
    object_id: Entity id at the head. Empty matches any.
    client: GraphQL client. Defaults to the configured endpoint.

Raises:
    ValueError: If no filter is given at all.

Returns:
    Matching link rows (``id``, ``predicate``, ``objectId``,
    ``properties``, ``createdAt``), oldest first as the server returns
    them. Empty on any failure -- callers treat "cannot read" as "nothing
    known", never as "nothing there".
verified_symbols.signature: subject_id: str='', *, predicate: str='', object_id: str='', client: GraphQLClient | None=None

verified_symbols.name: delete_link
verified_symbols.doc:
Delete ONE edge by id, leaving both endpoints untouched.

THIS IS THE ONLY IN-PLACE REVISION THE GRAPH ALLOWS. Entity properties are
create-only (``UpdateEntityInput`` has no ``properties`` field), and
``updateLink`` -- which does exist in tiled 0.2.15, contrary to an earlier
note in the project notes -- carries only ``predicate`` and ``access_blob``, so link
properties are no more editable than entity ones. What IS cheap is
delete-and-recreate of an edge: unlike ``deleteEntity``, this cascades to
nothing.

Args:
    link_id: The server's link id, as read back from ``links``.
    client: GraphQL client. Defaults to the configured endpoint.

Returns:
    True if the server reported the link deleted. False if it was already
    gone, which is not an error -- the caller's intent is satisfied either
    way.

verified_symbols.name: record_provenance
verified_symbols.doc:
Record a wasDerivedFrom edge in the knowledge graph.

Callback for forge.bridge.handoff.run_simulation. Executes after the
simulation output is already durable in Tiled, so a KG failure does not
undo the run.

**MUST NOT RAISE.** Best-effort only: returns False and logs each failure.

Strategy:
    1. Upsert a SIMULATION_RESULT entity for the output path.
    2. Ensure the source frame has an entity to point at.
    3. Link result -``prov:wasDerivedFrom``-> source, confidence 1.0.

Args:
    result: The completed simulation result.
    request: The originating simulation request.
    client: GraphQL client. Defaults to the configured endpoint.

Returns:
    True if the entity write and the link both succeeded.

Raises:
    None. All exceptions are caught and logged.

verified_symbols.name: slug
verified_symbols.doc:
A stable, path-safe, lowercase token for *text*.

Deterministic and lossy on purpose -- two names that differ only in
punctuation or case are meant to collide, because "PS-b-PMMA", "PS-b-PMMA "
and "ps-b-pmma" are one material.

Greek letters are transliterated ("ε" -> "epsilon") and the rest is
NFKD-folded to ASCII, so accented Latin agrees with its bare form and
"poly(ε-caprolactone)" agrees with "poly(epsilon-caprolactone)" -- the two
spellings a paper and a metadata field will use for one material.

Args:
    text: Free-text name.
    max_length: Truncation bound, keeping paths readable in the UI.

Returns:
    The slug, or ``"unknown"`` when *text* has no usable characters --
    never an empty string, which would make the path a bare directory.

verified_symbols.name: publication_path
verified_symbols.doc:
The graph path for a publication.

OpenAlex id wins when present: it is a single opaque token, whereas a DOI
carries slashes and case that every producer normalises slightly
differently. A paper resolved twice by different routes must land on one
entity, so the precedence is fixed here rather than left to each caller.

Args:
    openalex_id: e.g. ``"W2741809807"`` or the full OpenAlex URL.
    doi: e.g. ``"10.1021/acs.macromol.6b02138"`` or a doi.org URL.

Returns:
    e.g. ``"literature/publications/w2741809807"`` or
    ``"literature/publications/doi/10-1021-acs-macromol-6b02138"``.

Raises:
    ValueError: If neither identifier is usable. A publication with no
        identifier cannot be deduplicated, and inventing a title-based key
        guarantees duplicates on the next ingest.

verified_symbols.name: author_path
verified_symbols.doc:
The graph path for an author.

Args:
    openalex_id: OpenAlex author id, preferred for the same reason as above.
    name: Display name, used only when there is no id.

Returns:
    e.g. ``"literature/authors/a1969205032"``.

Raises:
    ValueError: If neither is usable.

verified_symbols.name: material_path
verified_symbols.doc:
The graph path for a material, keyed on its name.

Name, not SMILES: the sample metadata, the paper text and the user's
question all say "PS-b-PMMA". A structural key would be more correct in
principle and would connect to none of them.

Args:
    name: Material or polymer-system name.

Returns:
    e.g. ``"materials/ps-b-pmma"``.

Raises:
    ValueError: If *name* has no usable characters.

verified_symbols.name: document_path
verified_symbols.doc:
The graph path of a project file: ``documents/<first 16 hex of its sha256>``.

Content-addressed, so one file attached to two projects is one node.

verified_symbols.name: compact_predicate
verified_symbols.doc:
``forge:similarConditions`` -> ``similar_conditions``.

An alias when one is declared, else: drop the namespace, split camelCase,
lowercase. Done HERE rather than in the viewer so the server and the client
cannot hold two different opinions about what an edge is called -- which is
exactly how ``cites`` and ``has_q_range`` came to be wrong on one side only.

verified_symbols.name: Publication
verified_symbols.doc:
A published scientific paper or article.

Attributes:
    doi: Digital Object Identifier.
    title: Publication title.
    authors: List of author names.
    year: Publication year.
    journal: Journal or venue name.
    volume: Journal volume.
    pages: Page range.
    url: Web URL of the publication.

verified_symbols.name: Author
verified_symbols.doc:
An author of a publication.

Attributes:
    first_name: Given name.
    last_name: Family name.
    email: Email address.
    orcid: ORCID identifier.

verified_symbols.name: PaperSection
verified_symbols.doc:
A section within a published paper.

Attributes:
    publication_path: Path to the publication entity.
    section_title: Section heading.
    section_type: Type of section (abstract, introduction, methods, etc.).
    page_number: Starting page number.
    text_summary: Summary of the section content.

verified_symbols.name: PaperFigure
verified_symbols.doc:
A figure or table within a published paper.

Attributes:
    publication_path: Path to the publication entity.
    figure_number: Figure or table number.
    caption: Figure caption text.
    data_uri: Tiled URI of the figure data, if available.

verified_symbols.name: Evidence
verified_symbols.doc:
A verbatim quotation from a paper, with where it was found.

THE POINT IS THAT IT IS NOT AN INTERPRETATION. An assertion ("the cylinder
spacing is 26 nm") is a claim someone or something made; this is the text
that claim was read out of. Keeping them apart is what makes a claim
checkable later without re-reading the paper -- and what stops an
uncertain inference being promoted into a definitive parameter, which the
research plan calls out by name.

IMMUTABLE, WHICH IS WHY IT MAY BE AN ENTITY AT ALL. Entity properties are
create-only in tiled 0.2.15, so anything that needs revising has to live on
a link. A quotation never needs revising: if the extraction changes, that
is a NEW reading of the same sentence, and it gets its own assertion edge
pointing at this same evidence.

Attributes:
    text: The quotation, verbatim.
    publication_id: The publication it was quoted from.
    section_name: Which section, where known.
    page: Page number, where the parser reported one.
    extracted_by: What produced this reading -- model name or tool.

verified_symbols.name: Quantity
verified_symbols.doc:
One number a paper reports, or one this pipeline assumed for it.

PROMOTED OUT OF A JSON BLOB. These values lived as a list of dicts in the
``properties`` of a ``prov:wasDerivedFrom`` edge, which made three ordinary
questions unanswerable: which simulations used a spacing of 26 nm, which
numbers in this graph were assumed rather than measured, and what sentence
supports THIS value (the evidence edge hung off the SIMULATION, one hop
away from the number it justified).

AN ENTITY DESPITE CREATE-ONLY PROPERTIES, for the same reason
:class:`Evidence` is: a reading is immutable. "26 nm from Fig 2b" does not
become something else later -- a different extraction produces a DIFFERENT
quantity node, and both readings stay visible with their prompt versions.
That is a feature in a provenance graph and a bug in a database.

BOTH UNITS ARE KEPT. ``value``/``unit`` are exactly as the paper wrote
them; ``value_nm`` is the normalised length where one applies. Storing only
the normalised number would erase whether the paper said "26 nm" or
"260 angstrom", and storing only the original would leave every consumer
re-implementing a conversion that is allowed to REFUSE (see
``forge.agents.literature.publication``, whose converters raise on an
unrecognised unit rather than guessing).

Attributes:
    quantity_name: Which quantity this is, from the extractor's closed set
        (``cylinder_center_spacing``, ``lamellar_period``, ...).
    value: The number as reported.
    unit: Its unit as reported ("nm", "angstrom", "nm^-1", "").
    value_nm: The same length in nanometres, where the quantity is a
        length and the unit was convertible. None otherwise -- an absent
        normalisation is not zero.
    epistemic_status: One of :data:`EPISTEMIC_STATUSES`.
    caveat: The extractor's own qualification, if any.
    confidence: The extraction's confidence. NOTE this is per-EXTRACTION,
        not per-value: every quantity from one paper shares it, because
        that is all the model reports. Recorded rather than fabricated.
    publication_id: The paper this came from.
    extracted_by: Model or tool that produced it.
    prompt_version: Which extraction prompt asked for it.

verified_symbols.name: Claim
verified_symbols.doc:
One assertion a publication makes about a structure.

NOT A RENAMED `Quantity`, and not a replacement for one. A `quantity` is a
NUMBER with a unit; a claim is what the paper ASSERTED, which may be a
number, a reported reflection, or a morphology with no number attached at
all. The two coexist on purpose: `sim_build_recipe_from_paper` and
`views.paper_simulation_recipe` must keep answering for every paper already
in the graph, so `quantity` stays universal while claims add a richer tier
that can be rolled out per paper.

DENORMALISED ON PURPOSE. A claim carries name, value, unit, location and
quote itself rather than pointing at them, so a recipe builder can rebuild
a `PaperStructureExtraction` from ONE
`links(subjectId: publication, predicate: forge:asserts)` page instead of a
fan-out per field. That duplicates data the evidence nodes also hold, and
the duplication is the point: this type exists to be read cheaply.

IMMUTABLE, LIKE `Evidence` AND `Quantity`. Entity properties are
create-only in this store, which suits a claim exactly -- what a paper said
does not change. A re-extraction that reads the paper differently produces
a DIFFERENT claim node, and both stay visible with their prompt versions.
Everything revisable rides on edges instead: a verdict is a
`forge:evaluates` edge appended by whatever tested the claim, superseded by
a newer edge rather than by an impossible property update.

THE ID IS CONTENT-ADDRESSED over (publication, kind, name, value, unit) and
deliberately EXCLUDES `prompt_version`: re-extracting the same reading at
the same values must converge on one node rather than minting a second that
says the same thing. First writer wins on the properties, which is why
`prompt_version` records who that was.

Attributes:
    kind: One of :data:`CLAIM_KINDS`. `reported_peak` and `morphology` are
        the two the quantity table cannot express, and they are exactly the
        two the extractor was silently dropping.
    quantity_name: For `kind="quantity"`, the name from the extractor's
        closed set. For a peak, its label ("(100)", "first order").
    value: The number as reported, when there is one.
    unit: Its unit exactly as printed -- never normalised, so "260
        angstrom" stays distinguishable from "26 nm".
    value_nm: The normalised length in nm, or None when the strict unit
        table refused. An absent normalisation is not zero.
    morphology: The raw morphology string as the extractor reported it.
        NOT remapped here; consumers that need `reported_peaks -> "other"`
        do that themselves, so the stored row keeps saying what the paper
        said.
    direction: In-plane / out-of-plane, where the paper distinguishes them.
    location: Where in the paper this was read (a section or figure).
    quote: The sentence it was read out of, verbatim.
    caveat: The extractor's own qualification.
    material_system: Which material the claim is about.
    epistemic_status: One of :data:`EPISTEMIC_STATUSES`.
    confidence: Per-EXTRACTION confidence, not per-claim -- that is all the
        model reports, and recording it honestly beats fabricating one.
    publication_id: The paper that made the claim.
    extracted_by: Model or tool that produced it.
    prompt_version: Which extraction prompt asked for it.
    run_id: The pipeline run that wrote it, when one was live.

verified_symbols.name: paper_subgraph
verified_symbols.doc:
Everything the graph knows about one paper, as a drawable subgraph.

Args:
    publication_id: The publication's TILED UUID. Not a DOI and not a
        catalog path: `resolve_fast` defers on an unknown path prefix and
        `literature/` holds two entity types, so a non-UUID ref falls back
        to the whole-graph load this exists to avoid.
    depth: 1 stops at the paper's own children; 2 adds panels, readings,
        quantities and quotations; 3 also links a quotation back to the
        section it was read out of.
    mentions: ``"typed"`` keeps the materials and techniques a section
        names; ``"none"`` skips that hop entirely -- it is the most
        expensive one and the least often wanted.
    text_chars: Section text to include, in characters. Zero ships none;
        the payload carries `text_chars` either way so a caller can say
        "12 k" without downloading it. Sections run to 59,000 characters
        and a paper has 28 of them.
    max_nodes: Draw no more than this, shedding the least structural first.
    client: Injectable; the default graph client otherwise.

Returns:
    A dict of `nodes`, `edges`, `groups`, `stats`, `glossary`, `predicates`,
    `entityColors`, and the honesty fields `truncated`, `truncated_at`,
    `dropped` and `requests`.

Raises:
    PublicationNotFound: No entity with that id, or it is not a publication.
    PaperSubgraphUnavailable: The graph could not be read. Deliberately not
        an empty graph -- see the module docstring.
verified_symbols.signature: publication_id: str, *, depth: int=2, mentions: str='typed', text_chars: int=0, max_nodes: int=DEFAULT_MAX_NODES, client: GraphQLClient | None=None

verified_symbols.name: KnowledgeGraphUnavailable
verified_symbols.doc: Raised when no knowledge-graph server can be reached or read.

verified_symbols.name: iter_entities
verified_symbols.doc:
Every entity of a type, PAGED. For batch work, not for the UI.

:func:`find_entities` clamps to 200 rows because it backs a search box,
where returning the whole graph would be useless. Batch consumers need the
opposite, and the clamp does not announce itself -- it returns 200 rows and
a caller that asked for 5,000 has no way to tell a truncation from a small
graph.

That silence has now cost twice on the same corpus:

* the figure classification sweep would have classified 200 of 1,754
  figures and reported success;
* ``paper_simulation`` read 200 of 1,684 ``paper_section`` rows, so 132 of
  149 papers had NO text and were declined with
  ``prefilter_no_scattering_keywords`` -- which reads as "this paper is not
  about scattering" when it means "we never saw the paper". A GISAXS review
  with 59 mentions of the technique was rejected that way.

Args:
    entity_type: Entity type to page through.
    limit: Stop after this many rows. The default is effectively "all".

Returns:
    Entity dicts as the GraphQL layer returns them, properties parsed.

verified_symbols.name: reduce_newest
verified_symbols.doc:
Newest edge properties per subject, from link rows already in hand.

The comparison half of :func:`newest_link_properties`, split out because
two callers need it on rows they fetched some other way -- a per-paper walk
should not page a whole predicate to find out which of one figure's two
verdicts is current.

`timestamp_key` exists because the writers do not agree: `hasScale`,
`hasQRange` and `hasExtraction` stamp `recorded_at` while `classifiedAs`
stamps `classified_at`. Reading the wrong key makes EVERY edge look equally
old, and then "newest" is whichever row the server happened to return last
-- a superseded verdict winning silently, which is the failure this whole
newest-wins convention exists to prevent.

Args:
    rows: Link rows carrying ``subjectId`` and ``properties``.
    timestamp_key: The property the writer stamps.

Returns:
    ``{subjectId: properties}``. ISO-8601 strings compare correctly as
    strings, so nothing is parsed; a row missing the key sorts oldest and
    wins only when it is the only one.

verified_symbols.name: newest_link_properties
verified_symbols.doc:
Newest edge properties per SUBJECT, for one predicate.

THE ONE IMPLEMENTATION OF NEWEST-WINS-BY-APPEND. Revisable values in this
graph live on links because entity properties are create-only, so "the
current value" always means "the newest edge on this predicate" -- for a
figure's class, its scale, its q range, and everything that follows the
pattern next. That question was being answered by four near-copies of this
loop, which is four chances for the tie-breaking, the pagination and the
JSON-string handling to drift apart.

ONE PAGED QUERY OVER THE PREDICATE, never one per subject -- the shape that
cost the classification skip-set 4,023 round trips before it was fixed.

Args:
    predicate: The CURIE, e.g. ``"forge:hasScale"``.
    limit: Stop once this many subjects are known.
    timestamp_key: Which property the writer stamps; see
        :func:`reduce_newest`.
    client: Injectable for tests; the default client otherwise.

Returns:
    ``{subjectId: properties}``, the properties of the newest edge by
    *timestamp_key*.
verified_symbols.signature: predicate: str, *, limit: int=100000, timestamp_key: str='recorded_at', client: GraphQLClient | None=None

verified_symbols.name: iter_links
verified_symbols.doc:
Every link in the graph, PAGED, with properties parsed.

The batch counterpart to :func:`iter_entities`, and it exists for the same
reason: ``_load`` caps links at ``_MAX_LINKS`` (40,000) because it backs the
graph VIEWER, where more rows than that cannot be drawn. A quality report
that inherited that cap would silently describe a prefix of the graph -- and
this corpus is at 33,145 links, close enough that the cap would start biting
without announcing it.

Returns the raw row shape (``subjectId`` / ``objectId``), not the viewer's,
because callers here join on ids rather than render them. Note that
``/api/graph/full`` renames these to ``source`` / ``target``; a probe written
against that spelling and pointed at this function silently sees every node
as an orphan. That happened while this was being written -- 287 of 287
technique nodes reported orphaned against 5,816 live technique edges.

Args:
    limit: Stop after this many rows. Callers wanting to detect truncation
        should compare the result length against the limit they passed.

Returns:
    Link dicts as the GraphQL layer returns them, properties parsed.

verified_symbols.name: walk
verified_symbols.doc:
Follow a predicate path from *start_ids*, one query batch per hop.

THE STORE IS A TRIPLE STORE AND MOST OF THIS REPO DOES NOT READ IT AS ONE.
`_load()` pages every entity and every link -- roughly 157 round trips at
28k/50k rows, with no cache -- and then filters in Python; it backs
`graph_lineage`, `graph_connections`, `sample_context` and `find_entities`,
and therefore `TiledKGStore.get_node`. Meanwhile the server filters links by
subject, predicate and object independently, and hydrates one entity by id.
This walks the edges instead of downloading the graph.

Cost is one batched request per `_ALIAS_BATCH` frontier nodes per hop, plus
hydration of what was reached -- never one request per node, and never the
whole table.

Args:
    start_ids: Entity ids to start from. Ids, not names or paths: name
        resolution is `_resolve`'s job and it has six tiers of ambiguity
        handling that do not belong in a traversal.
    steps: The path, one `WalkStep` per hop.
    max_frontier: Nodes a hop may reach before stopping. Exceeding it sets
        `truncated` rather than raising or silently returning a prefix.
    hydrate: Fetch entity rows for what was reached. False when the caller
        only needs ids, which halves the requests.
    client: GraphQL client. Defaults to the configured endpoint.

Returns:
    A `WalkResult`. On a transport failure it carries whatever was reached
    with `truncated` set -- a partial answer that says it is partial, never
    a short answer that looks complete.
verified_symbols.signature: start_ids: Sequence[str], steps: Sequence[WalkStep], *, max_frontier: int=_MAX_FRONTIER, hydrate: bool=True, client: GraphQLClient | None=None

verified_symbols.name: find_entities
verified_symbols.doc:
Search entities by name substring and/or type.

NAME filtering happens HERE because the server has no name predicate --
``entities`` takes only ``entityType``, ``limit`` and ``offset``. TYPE
filtering does NOT, any more, and that was the whole cost: an earlier
revision of this docstring argued a local scan "costs nothing extra", which
was true of the name half and false of the type half. A typed search paged
every entity in the graph and threw away all but one type.

Measured against the live graph, ``entity_type="publication"`` with
``name_contains="RSoXS"``: **40,756 rows read to return 583**, 4.0 s at the
route. The typed query reads the 583.

An UNTYPED search still pages the whole table, because there is nothing to
push down -- a name substring is not expressible in this schema. Reading
``catalog.db`` directly WOULD answer it in milliseconds and is deliberately
NOT taken here: `forge.kg` speaks to the served graph API, and reaching past
it as a side effect of a speed fix is the layering decision the project
records as one to take on purpose.

Args:
    name_contains: Case-insensitive substring matched against the entity
        name AND its uri, so a catalog path finds its entity.
    entity_type: Exact entity type, e.g. ``"publication"``. Empty matches
        all, and costs a whole-graph page.
    limit: Maximum rows returned (clamped to 1..200).

Returns:
    Matching entities, newest first where a creation time is known.

Raises:
    KnowledgeGraphUnavailable: If no graph server can be read.
verified_symbols.signature: name_contains: str='', entity_type: str='', limit: int=50

verified_symbols.name: graph_recent
verified_symbols.doc:
The slice of the graph created after *since*.

Args:
    since: ISO 8601 timestamp. Entities and links with a ``createdAt``
        strictly greater are returned. Empty returns everything, which is
        what a first poll wants.

Returns:
    ``{"entities", "links", "stats"}`` in the same shape as
    :func:`graph_snapshot`, so a live view can reuse one renderer.

Raises:
    KnowledgeGraphUnavailable: If no graph server can be read.

verified_symbols.name: graph_snapshot
verified_symbols.doc:
The whole knowledge graph plus derived summaries, for the Graph tab.

Concurrent callers share one load; see the note above `_SNAPSHOT_LOCK`.
The result is always freshly read -- this coalesces, it does not cache.

Returns:
    ``{"entities", "links", "stats", "runs", "ontology"}``. ``stats``
    carries totals plus ``byEntityType`` / ``byPredicate`` tallies; the
    ontology block is derived from what is actually present, so the legend
    can never list a type the graph does not hold.

Raises:
    KnowledgeGraphUnavailable: If no graph server can be read.

verified_symbols.name: graph_stats
verified_symbols.doc:
Totals and per-type tallies, WITHOUT loading the graph's contents.

`graph_snapshot` answers this today by reading every entity and link in
full and counting them -- correct, and it moves 89.5 MB to produce four
integers and two histograms. This asks for `entityType` and `predicate`
alone: 6.21 s -> 3.42 s against the live graph, for 4.2 MB.

COALESCES, DOES NOT CACHE, exactly like `graph_snapshot` and for the same
reason: a header that reports a count must never report an old one. It has
its OWN flight slot, because sharing one would make a cheap stats caller
wait on an expensive full load it does not need.

Returns:
    ``{"entities", "links", "byEntityType", "byPredicate", "truncated"}``,
    the same keys and the same meanings as ``graph_snapshot()["stats"]``
    minus ``runs`` -- which needs entity PROPERTIES and so cannot come from
    a tally. `tests/kg/test_graph_stats.py` pins the two against each other
    on one fixture; two implementations of "count by type" that drift are
    two different answers to the same question.

Raises:
    KnowledgeGraphUnavailable: If no graph server can be read.

verified_symbols.name: resolve_fast
verified_symbols.doc:
Resolve *ref* server-side, or None when only a full scan can answer.

WHY THIS EXISTS. `_resolve` walks seven tiers over a list `_load` had to
page in first -- and paging every entity is 2.6 s even at the raised page
size, for a question the server can often answer in ~20 ms. The two shapes
the frontend actually sends are exactly the two the server can resolve:
Browse's connections column passes a CATALOG PATH, and its drill-down passes
an ENTITY UUID.

A MISS IS NOT AN ANSWER. Returning None means "ask the full resolver", never
"no such entity", so nothing that resolved before can stop resolving.

Tier fidelity, which is the whole risk:

* A UUID is tier 1, and tier 1 is FIRST and cannot tie -- ids are unique. So
  a positive hit here is exactly what `_resolve` would have returned. No
  deviation.
* A path is tier 3, and tier 2 (exact NAME) precedes it. Taking the path
  first is a DELIBERATE, GUARDED deviation: proving no entity is *named*
  that string is the very scan this avoids. The guard is
  `tests/fitness/test_no_entity_name_shadows_a_path.py`, which asserts the
  collision set is empty on the live graph -- verified empty when this
  landed. If it ever fires, this function is what has to change.

verified_symbols.name: graph_lineage
verified_symbols.doc:
Trace one entity back through what it was derived from.

Walks outgoing :data:`LINEAGE_PREDICATES` breadth-first from the named
entity, so the chain reads target-first and each step records the predicate
it arrived by.

Args:
    name: An entity id, name, or catalog path.

Returns:
    ``{"target", "chain", "reachedRaw", ...}``. A ``name`` that matches
    nothing returns an empty chain plus a ``note`` saying so and
    ``availableNames`` -- never an unrelated chain presented as this one's.

Raises:
    KnowledgeGraphUnavailable: If no graph server can be read.

verified_symbols.name: graph_connections
verified_symbols.doc:
Everything directly linked to one entity, grouped by relationship.

Args:
    ref: An entity id, an entity name, or a Tiled catalog path such as
        ``browse/generated_data/TF001214`` -- the last being what a Browse
        row holds for a sample.

Returns:
    ``{"resolved", "ref", "groups", ...}``. A ref that is not in the graph
    resolves to ``{"resolved": false, "note": ...}`` rather than an error:
    a measured sample legitimately has no provenance until some run reads
    it, and reporting that as a failure would train users to ignore it.

Raises:
    KnowledgeGraphUnavailable: If no graph server can be read.

entries.integration_instructions: Retain bounded traversal and freshness projections. Filter literature ownership; sample_context and simulation recipes stay FORGE.
entries.evidence: AST-verified source symbols; selected implementations statically reviewed; runtime behavior not certified

verified_symbols.name: kg_find_entities
verified_symbols.doc:
Find entities by name, catalog path, or type.

The way in to everything else: get an id or a path here, then ask
``kg_get_connections`` or ``kg_get_lineage`` about it.

The search covers the entity's URI as well as its name, so a Tiled catalog
path from the Browse tab (``beamlines/bl733/projects/10k/TF000433``) finds
the entity bound to that node.

Args:
    query: Case-insensitive substring of the name or catalog path. Empty
        lists everything of the given type.
    entity_type: Exact type filter, e.g. ``"dataset"``, ``"agent_run"``,
        ``"simulation_result"``, ``"fit_result"``, ``"publication"``,
        ``"material"``. Call ``kg_get_summary`` for the types that exist.
    limit: Maximum rows, capped at 50.

Returns:
    JSON ``{"count", "entities": [{id, name, entityType, path,
    hasCatalogNode}]}`` -- or ``{"error": ...}``.
verified_symbols.signature: query: str='', entity_type: str='', limit: int=20

verified_symbols.name: kg_get_summary
verified_symbols.doc:
Summarise the knowledge graph: how big it is and what is in it.

Start here when asked what the graph knows. Returns counts only -- no
entities, no links -- so it is cheap and safe on a large graph, and it tells
you which entity types and predicates exist so a follow-up query can name
them exactly.

THAT CLAIM USED TO BE FALSE. This called `graph_snapshot`, which loads every
entity and link IN FULL -- 89.5 MB of properties, captions and file paths --
and counted the rows. Measured live: 6.07 s against 4.14 s for
`graph_stats`, which asks only for `entityType` and `predicate`. A 200-
question agent benchmark made it the single most expensive tool in the run
(9 calls, 59.4 s, 6.6 s average), and its docstring was advertising the
opposite.

`runs` comes from `byEntityType["agent_run"]` rather than from
`_run_summaries`, which needs entity PROPERTIES and so cannot come from a
tally. Verified equal on the live graph (14 = 14), and a test pins the two
against each other so a divergence cannot pass silently.

Returns:
    JSON with ``entities`` and ``links`` totals, ``byEntityType`` and
    ``byPredicate`` tallies, ``runs`` (recorded agent runs), and the
    ontology's ``lineagePredicates`` -- or ``{"error": ...}``.

verified_symbols.name: kg_read_paper
verified_symbols.doc:
Read an ingested paper: its section list, or one section's text.

THE ONLY TOOL HERE THAT RETURNS DOCUMENT TEXT. The others deliberately do
not: :func:`_trim` drops ``properties`` so a search cannot dump a paper into
the context, and ``kg_get_connections`` returns names and ids. That left the
agent able to say a paper exists and has twelve sections while unable to
quote a single word of it -- so "what does this paper report?" was
unanswerable even for papers this system had ingested itself.

Call it twice: once with no ``section`` to see what the paper contains, then
with a name to read one. That two-step keeps a single call bounded, and lets
the model choose "Results" rather than being handed an introduction.

MEMBERSHIP COMES FROM THE EDGES, not from matching id strings. Sections
carry their publication as a string property, and the same paper is stored
under two keys in this graph (an OpenAlex id and a DOI) -- string matching
on that silently found nothing, which is how ``forge:extractedFrom`` read
zero for papers that plainly had sections. The ``schema:hasPart`` edges are
authoritative.

Args:
    ref: The paper -- an entity id, its exact title, or a catalog path.
        ``kg_find_entities(entity_type="publication")`` is how to get one.
    section: A section name, matched case-insensitively and by substring so
        "results" finds "3. Results & Discussion". Empty returns the list.

Returns:
    With no ``section``: JSON ``{"paper", "sections": [{name, chars}],
    "figures", "tables"}``. With one: ``{"paper", "section", "text",
    "chars", "truncated"}``. On failure, ``{"error": ...}`` -- and an
    unresolved ref lists what it could have meant.

verified_symbols.name: kg_get_lineage
verified_symbols.doc:
Trace where a dataset, fit or simulation came from.

Walks provenance edges backwards in time -- ``prov:used``,
``prov:wasGeneratedBy``, ``prov:wasDerivedFrom`` -- from the named thing
towards the measurement it ultimately rests on. Use it to answer "what was
this derived from?", "which raw frame is behind this fit?", "what did that
run read?".

Args:
    name: Entity id, entity name, or Tiled catalog path.

Returns:
    JSON with the resolved entity and its ancestry chain -- or
    ``{"error": ...}``. An entity with no provenance yet is a normal
    answer, not a failure: a measured frame nothing has analysed has none.

verified_symbols.name: kg_get_connections
verified_symbols.doc:
List everything directly linked to one entity, grouped by relationship.

One hop in every direction, with the edges labelled in plain language --
which runs read this sample, what was derived from it, which paper mentions
it. Broader than ``kg_get_lineage``, which follows provenance only.

Args:
    ref: Entity id, entity name, or Tiled catalog path (what the Browse tab
        holds for a sample).

Returns:
    JSON ``{"resolved", "ref", "entity", "groups": [...]}`` -- or
    ``{"error": ...}``. ``resolved: false`` means the ref is not in the
    graph, which for a never-analysed sample is expected.

entries.integration_instructions: Five verified donor entrypoints are eligible with literature scope. Omit dataset runs/sample contexts/prior simulations. Preserve aliases through FORGE wrappers.
entries.evidence: AST-verified source symbols; selected implementations statically reviewed; runtime behavior not certified

verified_symbols.name: provenance_writes_allowed
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether this process may record provenance into a real graph.

False while a pytest test is running, unless
:data:`_ALLOW_TEST_PROVENANCE_ENV` is "1".

A BUG CLASS, NOT A HYPOTHETICAL. Two separate commits taught pipelines to
record themselves, and both then wrote provenance about work that never
happened as soon as a catalog was reachable:

* fine-tune jobs, whose tests inject a stub trainer -- four
  `stage_execution` rows, two `model` rows, two `dataset` rows NAMED BY A
  PYTEST TMP PATH, and two `prov:wasGeneratedBy` edges;
* the enrichment generator, which a test drives and then ABANDONS -- two
  `agent_run` rows left marked "running" that nothing would ever close.

Neither was visible for weeks, because every suite run until then happened
with the catalog DOWN and the writes were skipped for the wrong reason. Both
were found by listing the live graph and not recognising rows in it.

WHY HERE AND NOT IN `forge.kg.mutations`. The first attempt guarded the
mutation entry points and broke 47 tests -- they patch the CLIENT and then
exercise the real `upsert_entity`, so refusing there refuses the very logic
under test. The bug class is narrower than "any write during a test": it is
provenance recorders, which is this class and `kg_bridge.record_finetune`.
Guarding each RECORD SITE individually is how the second instance got
written after the first was fixed, so it goes at the recorder's own two
choke points instead.

Tests that patch `_write`/`_link` are unaffected either way -- they never
reach a graph.

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder
verified_symbols.doc:
Writes one agent run's provenance into the graph.

Best-effort throughout, matching the rest of :mod:`forge.kg`: a graph
outage must never turn into a failed agent conversation. Every write is
guarded, and failures are logged and counted rather than raised -- but they
ARE counted, and :meth:`summary` reports them, because a recorder that
silently writes nothing is indistinguishable from an agent that did
nothing.

Typical use, from :mod:`forge.api.kg_bridge`::

    recorder = GraphRecorder(agent_name="supervisor")
    recorder.start(question="...")
    for message in stream:
        recorder.on_message(message)
    recorder.finish(status="completed")

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.start
verified_symbols.doc:
Open the run: seed namespaces, write the ``agent_run`` entity.

Namespaces are seeded HERE rather than at import: they are created by
the graph router at server startup, not by a migration, so a fresh
catalog has none -- and without them every ``prov:`` predicate is
stored expanded and compacted back to something no reader matches.

Args:
    question: The user's prompt for this run; stored as ``task``,
        which is the name the run picker reads.
    provider: LLM provider, for the run picker.
    model: Model name, for the run picker.
    source: What started this run (e.g. "chat", "api").
    **properties: Extra fields stored on the run entity.

Returns:
    The run id.
verified_symbols.signature: self, *, question: str='', provider: str | None=None, model: str | None=None, source: str | None=None, **properties: Any

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.finish
verified_symbols.doc:
Close the run: record its outcome and attach every step to it.

WHY THIS DELETES AND RECREATES. Entity properties are **create-only** in
tiled 0.2.15 -- ``UpdateEntityInput`` is
``{name, nodeId, uri, entityType, accessBlob}`` with no ``properties``
field, and sending one is a hard GraphQL error. So the placeholder
written by :meth:`start` cannot have its ``"running"`` status revised;
it has to be replaced.

That is also why the ``wf:executed`` edges are written HERE rather than
as each step happens: ``deleteEntity`` cascades to links, so edges
attached to the placeholder would be destroyed by the very write that
records the outcome. Steps are still written to the graph immediately,
so a crashed run leaves its turns and tool calls behind along with a
run still marked ``"running"`` -- which is exactly what happened.
verified_symbols.signature: self, *, status: str='completed', error: str | None=None

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.llm_turn
verified_symbols.doc: Record one model turn, linked from the run. Returns its path.
verified_symbols.signature: self, *, text: str='', model: str | None=None, **props: Any

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.tool_call
verified_symbols.doc:
Record one tool call, linked from the run.

``used_paths`` are catalog paths the tool read. Each becomes a
``prov:used`` edge, which is what makes lineage bottom out at real
data rather than at the conversation. Paths with no entity are written
as datasets first, because an edge to an entity nobody described is a
dangling reference that reads as data.
verified_symbols.signature: self, *, tool: str, arguments: dict[str, Any] | None=None, output: str='', failed: bool=False, used_paths: list[str] | None=None, **props: Any

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.decision
verified_symbols.doc:
Record what the supervisor chose to do next, and in whose terms.

THE ONLY DECISION THIS LOOP ACTUALLY MAKES. `EntityType.DECISION` and
`wf:madeDecision` were declared with the workflow vocabulary and nothing
ever wrote either -- 0 live entities, 0 live edges. The reason is worth
stating: the target ontology assumes a PLANNER, and this supervisor is a
ReAct loop with no plan object. What it does decide, every turn, is
which capability to invoke, so that is what gets recorded.

CAPABILITY, NOT JUST FUNCTION. `requested_capabilities` are SKILL names
-- the 15-skill catalog is the vocabulary the system already uses to
describe what it can do -- so a reader can ask "when did this agent try
to fit a measured pattern?" rather than reassembling that from tool
names.

NO CHAIN-OF-THOUGHT, deliberately and per the plan. `summary` is the
model's own visible text, which it published; its private reasoning is
not a durable fact about the system and storing it would make this graph
a transcript archive with a provenance schema on top.

Args:
    requested_capabilities: Skill names the chosen tools belong to.
    selected_tools: The tools the model asked for.
    selected_agents: The sub-agents that will serve them.
    summary: The model's visible text for this turn.
    after_step: The turn this decision was made in, linked
        ``wf:madeDecision``.

Returns:
    The decision node path.
verified_symbols.signature: self, *, requested_capabilities: list[str], selected_tools: list[str], selected_agents: list[str], summary: str='', after_step: str | None=None

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.stage
verified_symbols.doc:
Record one stage of a non-chat pipeline.

FOR THE PIPELINES THAT RECORDED NOTHING. Only the chat agent had a run
entity. The KG Builder's enrichment stages already measure their own
durations and emit `stage_started`/`stage_progress`/`stage_finished`
events -- into a module-global in-memory job dict that is lost on
process exit. So a build that ran for an hour left no trace of having
run, and "why does the graph look like this?" had no answer.

A STAGE IS NOT A TOOL CALL. Recording it as one would misreport what
ran, so it gets its own occurrence type rather than borrowing the
nearest available.

Args:
    name: Stage name, e.g. "catalog_sweeper".
    status: How it ended.
    duration_s: Seconds, where the caller measured it.
    **props: Stage-specific counts.

Returns:
    The stage node path.
verified_symbols.signature: self, *, name: str, status: str='completed', duration_s: float | None=None, **props: Any

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.record_plan
verified_symbols.doc:
Record that an activity followed a named, versioned plan.

WHAT THIS FIXES. `prompt_version: "3"` sits on 4,023 classification
edges and names a prompt whose TEXT lives only in git. The graph cannot
say what v3 said, so "re-run under the newer prompt" is unverifiable
after the fact, and two runs at the same version number are
indistinguishable if the text drifted between them. A plan node per
version, carrying `prompt_sha256`, is what pins it.

ADDITIVE ONLY, AND NEVER BACKFILLED. Historical runs have no recoverable
plan version -- that IS the 0-rows finding this came out of -- so
stamping one on them would be inventing provenance, which is worse than
having none. This records what a run followed at the time it runs.

Args:
    activity_path: The `stage_execution` / `agent_run` that followed it.
    name: The plan's stable name, e.g. ``"figure-class-prompt"``.
    version: Its version, e.g. ``"3"``.
    text: The plan's actual text, hashed into `prompt_sha256`. Omitted
        means the node records the version but cannot prove which text
        it was -- honest, and strictly weaker.
    **properties: Extra fields for the plan node.

Returns:
    Whether both the node and the edge landed.
verified_symbols.signature: self, activity_path: str, *, name: str, version: str, text: str='', **properties: Any

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.generated
verified_symbols.doc:
Record data this run produced, and where it came from.

Writes ``prov:wasGeneratedBy`` to the step that made it and
``prov:wasDerivedFrom`` to each source. Both point BACKWARDS in time,
which is the direction :func:`forge.api.kg_graph.graph_lineage` walks.
verified_symbols.signature: self, *, path: str, entity_type: EntityType=EntityType.DATASET, by_step: str | None=None, derived_from: list[str] | None=None, **properties: Any

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.summary
verified_symbols.doc:
What this recorder actually wrote.

Reports ``errors`` explicitly. A recorder that failed every write and
one that ran against a silent agent both leave an empty graph, and the
UI cannot tell them apart -- this is where the difference lives.

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.on_message
verified_symbols.doc:
Record one LangChain message, dispatching on its type.

Duck-typed rather than isinstance-checked: this module must not import
langchain (nothing below the agent layer may), and the attributes used
here -- ``type``, ``content``, ``tool_calls``, ``name`` -- are stable
across the message classes.

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.note_langfuse_trace
verified_symbols.doc:
Record the Langfuse trace this run corresponds to.

THE ONE STRING JOINING TWO STORES. The knowledge graph holds durable
provenance -- what was decided, what it rested on, what it produced --
and Langfuse holds the full trace with prompts and timings. Without an
id in common, a run in one is unfindable from the other, and the two
were keyed on DIFFERENT uuids for the same conversation.

Stored as a run property, so it must be set before :meth:`finish`
rewrites the entity -- properties are create-only and `finish` is the
write that persists.

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.note_tool_context
verified_symbols.doc:
Supply the static maps that let a step name its agent and capability.

Args:
    owners: tool-name PREFIX -> canonical sub-agent name, e.g.
        ``{"sim": "simulation", "vision": "simulation"}``.
    skills: tool NAME -> the skills that contain it.

Both are pure lookups over registries that live in the agent layer,
which this module may not import. Passing them in keeps the layering
intact and keeps the recorder testable without either registry.

Without them the recorder still works and simply records less: a
`tool_call` with no owner gets no `prov:wasAssociatedWith`, which is
correct -- attributing a step to a guessed agent would be worse than
leaving it unattributed.
verified_symbols.signature: self, *, owners: dict[str, str] | None=None, skills: dict[str, list[str]] | None=None

verified_symbols.name: GraphRecorder.note_tool_times
verified_symbols.doc:
Supply the durations the graph measured for this update.

THE NUMBERS ALREADY EXISTED AND WERE THROWN AWAY. `AgentState` carries
`tool_times`, the supervisor graph populates it on every tool call, and
`stream_agent_task` iterated only `messages` -- so the timing of every
tool call was computed and discarded on every run. A provenance graph
that cannot say how long a step took is missing the one number an
operator asks for first.

Called before the messages of the same graph update, because the
durations and the ToolMessages arrive together and the recorder must
stamp them at CREATION (properties are create-only, so a duration added
afterwards would not persist).

KEYED BY TOOL NAME, which is the shape `AgentState` uses, and that shape
loses a repeat: `tool_times` is merged with `{**old, **new}`, so two
calls to one tool in a run keep only the later duration. Recorded as a
limitation rather than papered over -- fixing it means changing the
state's reducer, which is a wider change than this.

verified_symbols.name: QueuedRecorder
verified_symbols.doc:
Hands every recorder call to one background worker, in order.

Presents the surface the API layer uses -- ``run_id``, ``run_path``,
``start``, ``on_message``, ``note_tool_times``, ``note_langfuse_trace``,
``finish``, ``summary`` -- so callers are unchanged.

LangChain messages cross a thread boundary here. That is safe because they
are effectively immutable pydantic models and the recorder only ever reads
attributes off them; nothing mutates a message.

verified_symbols.name: QueuedRecorder.finish
verified_symbols.doc: Close the run, then wait (bounded) for the backlog to drain.

entries.integration_instructions: Drain/flush and report failures; never silently drop critical mutation audit while reporting success.
entries.evidence: AST-verified source symbols; selected implementations statically reviewed; runtime behavior not certified

verified_symbols.name: TruncatedGraphRead
verified_symbols.doc:
The graph read stopped at a cap, so no repair here may proceed.

Raised only by the finders that have no report dict to put an error in
(:func:`find_duplicate_figures`); every other entry point returns
``{"error": ...}`` instead. See :func:`_truncation_refusal`.

verified_symbols.name: find_identifier_duplicates
verified_symbols.doc:
Pair publications that share an identifier but sit at different paths.

THE SURVIVOR IS CHOSEN BY :func:`forge.kg.views._rank`, the same ranking
:func:`forge.kg.views._resolve` already applies to same-named entities:
connection count, then newest, then id. That is not merely convenient --
it means the node that survives is the node every by-name lookup was
ALREADY returning, so no reader's answer changes as a result of the merge.
On the live pairs it also keeps the right one for an independent reason: the
OpenAlex-keyed rows carry 120, 10 and 210 author edges where the DOI-keyed
rows carry none.

Two guards, both of which SKIP rather than guess:

* More than two rows for one identifier. With three candidates there is no
  evidence which is canonical, and guessing moves provenance onto the wrong
  entity -- worse than leaving it where a human can still find it. This is
  the same rule `find_shadow_duplicates` applies for the same reason.
* Disagreeing titles. A shared DOI is strong identity evidence and a
  differing title is a surprise; a surprise is a thing to report, not to
  merge through.

Args:
    entities: Every entity in the graph, in :func:`views._load`'s shape.
    links: Every link, used only for the connection-count ranking.

Returns:
    ``(pairs, skipped)`` where each pair is ``(shadow, canonical)`` -- the
    argument order :func:`merge_shadow_duplicate` expects -- and *skipped*
    describes every group a guard refused, so a refusal is visible rather
    than silent.
verified_symbols.signature: entities: list[dict[str, Any]], links: list[dict[str, Any]]

verified_symbols.name: repair_identifier_duplicates
verified_symbols.doc:
Merge publications written twice under two key schemes.

DRY BY DEFAULT, like every destructive repair here: the second half is a
cascading delete, so the caller has to ask for it in words.

Reuses :func:`plan_edge_moves` and :func:`merge_shadow_duplicate` unchanged.
Those are generic over ``(shadow, canonical, links)`` -- only the FINDER was
specific to the shadow-path shape -- and reusing them keeps the
edges-before-delete ordering that makes this safe in ONE place rather than
two. That ordering is the whole design: ``deleteEntity`` cascades, so
deleting first destroys the edges the merge exists to save, and it does so
silently.

Args:
    apply: False (the default) reads only and reports what a real run would
        do. True executes the merges.

Returns:
    ``{"applied", "scanned", "duplicates", "skipped", "merges", "note"}``,
    or ``{"error": ...}``. Never raises.

verified_symbols.name: dedupe_figures
verified_symbols.doc:
Collapse duplicated figure entities to one per (publication, caption).

WHICH COPY SURVIVES IS NOT A COIN FLIP. `_cached_pdf_for` resolves a DOI to
the `_safe_stem` (underscore) filename, so the set living under
``<safe_stem>_images/`` is the one a future re-ingest will find and reuse.
Keeping that one makes re-ingestion idempotent; keeping the other guarantees
a third set the next time the paper is parsed.

THE IMAGE FILES ARE NOT TOUCHED HERE, and that ordering is the whole point.
Figure paths are create-only, so an entity whose file is deleted can never
be repaired -- only re-ingested. So this removes ENTITIES, and a caller
removes the now-unreferenced directory afterwards, having confirmed nothing
still points into it.

Args:
    keep_stem: Substring identifying the surviving copy's path (e.g.
        ``"_images/"`` fragment of the safe-stem directory). When empty,
        the NEWEST entity in each group survives, matching
        :func:`dedupe_links`' convention.
    apply: Perform the deletions. Defaults to a dry run.
    client: GraphQL client. Defaults to the configured endpoint.

Returns:
    ``{"groups", "surplus", "deleted", "failed", "kept", "note"}``, or the
    same with ``"error"`` in place of ``"note"`` when the graph could not
    be read.
verified_symbols.signature: *, keep_stem: str='', apply: bool=False, client: GraphQLClient | None=None

verified_symbols.name: dedupe_links
verified_symbols.doc:
Collapse duplicate edges to one per triple.

KEEPS THE NEWEST, deletes the rest. Which survivor is right depends on why
the duplicates exist, and for the case this was built for it does not
matter -- re-ingesting a paper writes byte-identical structural edges. Where
the properties DO differ, newest matches the convention every other reader
in this graph already follows (the figure classifier writes a new edge per
run and reads the latest), so a repair that kept the oldest would quietly
revert to a stale verdict.

NOT FOR APPEND-ONLY EDGES. ``prov:wasDerivedFrom`` deliberately carries one
edge per simulation run, each with its own quantities and rod metrics.
Passing that predicate here would discard real history, which is why this
takes an explicit predicate rather than sweeping the whole graph by default.

Args:
    predicate: CURIE to restrict to. Empty examines every predicate, which
        is a REPORTING mode -- combine with ``apply=False``.
    apply: Perform the deletions. Defaults to a dry run.
    client: GraphQL client. Defaults to the configured endpoint.

Returns:
    ``{"predicate", "tripleCount", "surplus", "deleted", "failed",
    "groups", "note"}``. ``surplus`` is how many edges are redundant;
    ``deleted`` is how many were actually removed (0 on a dry run).
verified_symbols.signature: predicate: str='', *, apply: bool=False, client: GraphQLClient | None=None

verified_symbols.name: graph_summary
verified_symbols.doc:
Knowledge graph statistics.

OFF THE EVENT LOOP, like `vocab_quality` below and for a sharper reason.
`get_stats` reaches `views.graph_snapshot`, which pages the WHOLE graph --
4.8 s warm, 14 s cold -- and every KG page polls this on mount and every
30 s. Inline, that jams the entire service: measured 2026-09-09, four
concurrent `/api/graph/entities` calls returned at 3, 6, 9 and 12 s
(perfectly serial), and a summary poll issued 0.2 s after one waited 8.5 s
behind it. React StrictMode double-invokes the mount effect, so two of
these held the loop for ~9.6 s while the Inspect page's entity search sat
unscheduled and hit the browser's 10 s abort -- which `EntityList` draws as
`No entities found.`, indistinguishable from an empty graph.

THIS IS ONLY SAFE BECAUSE `graph_snapshot` NOW COALESCES. Off the loop with
nothing coalescing, retries pile up, the threadpool's slots fill with
whole-graph loads, and every request needing one hangs for ever while
`/health` still answers 200. That was measured too, by doing it. See
`views._SNAPSHOT_LOCK`.

verified_symbols.name: vocab_quality
verified_symbols.doc:
Measure the free-form entity layer against the controlled vocabulary.

UNGATED, because it is a pure read: no writes, no LLM, no network beyond the
graph the caller can already read through `/api/graph/full`. The admin gate
exists for the four routes a page reload cannot undo, and this is not one.

Runs in a threadpool because the store client is synchronous and this pages
the whole link table -- 33k rows on this corpus, seconds rather than
milliseconds. Blocking the event loop for that would stall every other
request on the service.

The before/after pair of this report is the deliverable for the cleanup
work, so it deliberately returns raw counts rather than a score: a single
quality number would hide that 49 of the 614 non-canonical nodes are
deterministic category errors and 565 need judgement.

verified_symbols.doc:
Add a single publication by DOI / OpenAlex ID / arXiv ID.

Runs synchronously from the caller's perspective (but wraps blocking I/O
in a thread).

Steps:
  1. Resolve identifier → OpenAlex work dict.
  2. Upsert publication + authors into KG.
  3. If ``parse_pdf`` and paper is open-access: download PDF, parse
     sections + figures, write ``paper_section`` / ``paper_figure`` nodes.
  4. If ``extract_entities``: run hybrid extractor, write
     technique / analysis / instrument nodes + edges.
  5. Return a summary dict.

Args:
    body: Request payload.

Returns:

verified_symbols.name: UploadPaperResponse
verified_symbols.doc:
What happened to one uploaded PDF.

``status`` is either an intake status from
:data:`~als_knowledge_agent.graph.paper_intake.STATUSES` (the file was
refused, and the reason is machine-readable) or ``"ingested"`` /
``"failed:ingest"`` for a file that got as far as the graph.

verified_symbols.name: upload_paper
verified_symbols.doc:
Ingest ONE uploaded PDF, by recovering and verifying its DOI.

The browser cannot hand a server a folder path, so the UI uploads files one
at a time and this route does per file what
``scripts/ingest_paper_folder.py`` does per file locally: vet the PDF with
:func:`~als_knowledge_agent.graph.paper_intake.prepare_local_pdf`, seed the
paper cache, then run the ordinary ``add_publication`` flow -- which finds
the seeded file rather than downloading, and does the parsing, figures,
captions, licence terms and entity extraction that already live there.

ADMIN-GATED, unlike ``add_publication`` itself. That route is a metadata
lookup a user can reasonably trigger; this one accepts a file and can spend
~20 s of docling plus an LLM extraction per call, which is the same cost
class as ``enrich``/``topic_sweep``/``pdf_parse``.

``doi`` LETS THE CALLER ASSERT THE IDENTITY, for the files DOI recovery
structurally cannot handle. Supporting Information is the motivating case:
an SI is not a registered work, so it carries no DOI of its own in its
text, metadata or filename, and the SI for ``10.1021/nl2020526``
additionally misspells its parent's title ("Nanostrucutred"), so the title
check cannot corroborate it either. With ``doi`` set, recovery and the
title check are skipped, OpenAlex still has to know the DOI, and the
response carries ``identity_asserted: true``.

A REFUSED FILE IS A SUCCESSFUL REPORT. Anything the intake declines -- not a
PDF, no DOI, a title that does not match -- comes back **HTTP 200** carrying
the closed-set reason, because the panel uploads a batch and needs a verdict
per file. Only auth, the body-size cap and a genuinely broken request are
non-2xx.

Args:
    file: The PDF.
    parse_pdf: Parse it into sections/figures (the point, usually).
    extract_entities: Also link techniques/materials found in the text.
    model: Override the extraction model. The ``str | None`` annotation is
        load-bearing: FastAPI turns a blank form field into ``None`` for it,
        so the panel's empty text input means "the default model" rather
        than a model literally named ``""``.

Returns:
    An :class:`UploadPaperResponse`.

  3. Upsert a ``note`` node and an ``annotates`` edge.

  5. If ``extract_entities=True``, run keyword extraction and link entities.

Returns ``{ok, note_id, dataset_node_id, mentions_count}``.

Whether the admin gate is configured, and whether it is being bypassed.

Ungated on purpose: it exposes no key material, and a caller can already
learn both facts by making one request and reading the 401 vs 503 vs 200.
The Builder needs it so it can stop disabling buttons that would now work --
without it, a bypassed gate still looks locked, which is a confusing way to
ship an escape hatch.

verified_symbols.name: vocab_cleanup_propose
verified_symbols.doc:
Propose a cleanup of the entity layer. WRITES NOTHING TO THE GRAPH.

ADMIN-GATED because it is an unbounded LLM spend -- the same reason `enrich`,
`topic_sweep` and `pdf_parse` are. It is NOT gated for being dangerous to the
graph: it cannot touch it. `apply` is the route that can, and it defaults to
a dry run.

Runs IN THE SERVICE rather than as a script, for the reason
`backfill_extractions` does: `TiledKGStore.upsert_edge` is a write-side memo
that only resolves ids this process has written, so anything that will later
write must run where the store lives. Propose only reads, but `apply` shares
its row shape and that is where it matters.

The response is the proposal plus, unless `write_file` is false, the path of
a reviewable YAML file. The FILE is the durable decision record and belongs
in git -- deliberately not per-node decision entities in the graph, which
would be create-only, unrevisable, and would themselves become nodes needing
curation.

Read `counts.auto_tier_edges` first: that is the blast radius of everything
the apply step would move without a human reading it.

verified_symbols.name: vocab_cleanup_apply
verified_symbols.doc:
Apply a cleanup proposal. Reports by default, changes nothing.

THE ONE ROUTE HERE THAT CAN DESTROY DATA, so it is the one with a harmless
default. `apply=false` runs the SAME pure planner (`repair.plan_edge_moves`)
the real merge uses and returns what would happen -- a dry run computed by a
second code path would be a dry run of something else.

Auto-tier merges apply from an unreviewed file; every reject, every novel and
every low-confidence mapping requires `reviewed: true`. A novel row also
requires its slug to be in the vocabulary already, so `merge-novel` runs
first.

Runs in the service, not as a script: `TiledKGStore.upsert_edge` resolves
only ids THIS process has written, and a merge writes edges onto a canonical
node it may have just created. Doing this from outside would have every
rescued edge silently refused -- which is the failure that once left 11 of 13
`decision` entities with no `schema:about` link.

verified_symbols.name: backfill_extractions
verified_symbols.doc:
Extract entities for papers whose sections are stored but unlinked.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Entity extraction is Step 4 *inside* `add_publication`,
operating on sections held in memory from the parse. So a paper whose
extraction failed is stuck: the sections are in the graph, the entities are
not, and there is no way to try again short of re-ingesting -- which the
duplicate check refuses (it tests whether the BYTES ARE CACHED, not whether
the paper has entities) and which `--force` would answer by duplicating every
figure and section child.

That state is not hypothetical. A model-name bug routed extraction at a
provider that 404'd, the failure was logged at DEBUG and swallowed into an
empty result, and papers landed with sections, figures and NO ENTITIES while
the ingest reported success. The entities are what make a paper answerable,
so the graph grew without becoming more useful.

IT RUNS IN THE SERVICE, and that is the whole reason it is a route rather
than a script. `TiledKGStore.upsert_edge` is a WRITE-SIDE memo: it only
resolves ids this process has written, so a separate process that writes
edges against nodes it did not create gets them silently refused. That cost
real edges in this graph before -- 11 of 13 `decision` entities had no
`schema:about` link. Doing the work in the process that owns the store avoids
the whole class.

Sections come from `store.iter_nodes`, NOT `query_nodes`: the latter goes
through `views.find_entities`, which clamps to 200 rows because it backs a
search box, and the clamp is silent. Measured on this corpus, that once cost
the simulation stage 1,484 of 1,684 sections.

Args:
    body: `model` names the extraction model, optionally `provider:`-prefixed
        (`vllm:qwen3.8-27b` routes to vLLM -- measured 5x faster per request
        than local Ollama at 6-way concurrency, because it batches).
        `limit` bounds one call so the request does not run for hours;
        call it again to continue. `only_missing` skips papers that already
        have `describes_*` edges. `dois` restricts to named papers.

Returns:
    Counts, plus a per-paper list of what was written.
