verified_symbols.name: may_parse_pdf
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether to parse a paper's PDF.

**DOWNLOADING and PARSING are different acts and were sharing one gate.**
Requiring open access before FETCHING a PDF is right -- this should not pull
a paywalled file on a user's behalf. Requiring it before parsing a file
already on disk is not: that is the operator's own copy, and reading it is
not redistribution.

The distinction only showed up against a real corpus. Ingesting a folder of
ALS papers, ``10.1021/ma900497j`` reported ``oa=False`` and contributed zero
figures while its PDF sat in the cache; with the gate split it parses and
yields 8. Across a collection that difference is every closed-access paper,
which is a large share of the literature this program is about.

Redistribution stays gated where it belongs: ``_redistribution_terms``
stamps a licence on every figure and defaults to NOT redistributable, so
nothing here grants permission to re-publish anything.

Args:
    parse_requested: The caller asked for PDF parsing.
    is_oa: OpenAlex reports the work as open access.
    have_local_pdf: A PDF for this DOI is already in the cache.

Returns:
    True when the PDF should be parsed.
verified_symbols.signature: *, parse_requested: bool, is_oa: bool, have_local_pdf: bool

verified_symbols.name: _cache_contained_path
verified_symbols.doc:
Resolve *raw* and require it to sit inside the paper cache.

ONE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE CONTAINMENT RULE. The path comes from a graph
property, so serving it verbatim would let anything that can write an entity
read any file the server can. Two routes need this check now; a second copy
is a second chance to get it subtly wrong.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 for missing, unreadable OR out-of-cache paths. All
        the same status deliberately -- "that file exists but you may not
        have it" is itself a disclosure.

verified_symbols.name: table_csv
verified_symbols.doc:
Serve one extracted table as CSV, by entity id.

Same shape and the same containment rule as `figure_image`: docling writes
the CSV beside the figures, the graph holds a pointer, and the file is only
served if it resolves inside the paper cache.

`text/csv` rather than a download: the point is that a table extracted from
a paper can be LOOKED AT, and a browser tab is the cheapest way to do that.

verified_symbols.name: publication_figures
verified_symbols.doc:
The figures of one publication, each with its newest verdict.

One call because the UI needs all three things together and none of them
can be derived from the others: the figures come from an EDGE traversal,
the verdicts from a different edge, and the image from a third route.

verified_symbols.name: figure_image
verified_symbols.doc:
Serve one extracted figure image by entity id.

**WHY A ROUTE AT ALL.** The figure's location is an absolute FILESYSTEM
path, stored on the entity by ``pdf_parse``. A browser cannot open one --
``FigureThumbnail`` has been calling ``window.open(figPath)`` on it since
the port, which does nothing, and lately did nothing with a CATALOG path
because of the property shadowing. So the tab listed figures it could never
show.

**PATH CONTAINMENT IS THE SECURITY BOUNDARY, and it is not optional.** The
path comes from a graph property, so serving it verbatim would let anything
that can write an entity read any file the server can. Every request is
resolved and checked to be inside the paper cache; anything else is a 404
rather than a 403, because "that file exists but you may not have it" is
itself a disclosure.

verified_symbols.name: figure_classifications
verified_symbols.doc: Newest classification verdict per figure.

verified_symbols.name: parse_status
verified_symbols.doc:
Which publications' content came from *parser*, and which have none.

THE HONEST VERSION OF `extraction_status`. That field was computed per
ingest and written onto the publication with an `upsert_node` that could not
persist -- entity properties are create-only, and the publication already
existed by then -- so the graph never held it despite the write reporting
success.

The answer does not need a stored flag: it is a property of the CHILDREN.
A paper is parsed by a parser when its sections and figures all carry that
parser's name, which is exactly what the corpus refresh's
`already_parsed_by` already asks in order to skip work. This exposes the
same question over HTTP rather than storing a second, staler copy of it.

Args:
    parser: Parser name to test for ("docling", "pymupdf4llm").
    limit: Cap on publications examined.

Returns:
    ``{parser, parsed, unparsed, no_children, counts}`` -- publication ids
    in each state, so a caller can act on the difference rather than a
    total.

verified_symbols.name: review_resolve
verified_symbols.doc:
Record a human verdict on a figure, overriding the model's.

NO NEW MACHINERY, WHICH IS THE POINT. Classifications are append-only edges
and readers already take the NEWEST by ``classified_at``, so a human verdict
written the same way as a model verdict simply wins -- no mutable "resolved"
flag, no second store of corrections to reconcile, and the model's original
call stays in the graph as the record of what it believed. That is the
revisable-value shape this graph supports: entity properties are
create-only, links are not.

It reuses `record_classification` rather than writing its own edge, so a
human row and a model row cannot drift in shape. `model` is set to the
reviewer (or "human") because that field answers "who said so", and
`needs_review` goes False because the review has happened.

NOT ADMIN-GATED, deliberately and consistently with the four routes that
are: those guard a graph reset and three unbounded LLM/network spends --
things a page reload cannot undo. This is one small append that another
append can supersede.

Returns:
    ``{ok, figure_id, figure_class}`` or ``{error}``.

verified_symbols.name: review_resolve_bulk
verified_symbols.doc:
Record many human verdicts at once, one append each.

WHY A ROUTE RATHER THAN A CLIENT LOOP. `review_resolve` calls
`ensure_class_anchors` per request, and that is 12 `find_entity_id` lookups
-- 85 ms measured. A 555-row bucket resolved one request at a time spends
**47 seconds on anchor lookup alone**, plus 555 round trips, to write 555
edges. Resolving the anchors once makes the batch the cost of its writes.

EVERY ROW CARRIES ITS OWN CLASS, and nothing is inferred here. "Accept the
model's verdict" is the CLIENT sending that verdict back explicitly, so the
stored assertion always says what a person agreed to rather than what the
server assumed they meant.

VALIDATION IS ALL-OR-NOTHING, WRITES ARE PER-ROW, and the split is
deliberate. An unknown class or a missing id is a caller mistake: refusing
the whole batch leaves nothing half-applied and the caller can fix it. A
write that fails partway is an infrastructure fault, and there refusing
retroactively is not possible -- so those are reported per row and the rest
still land. A caller must read `failed`.

Not admin-gated, consistent with `review_resolve`: these are appends another
append can supersede, not an unbounded spend.

Returns:
    ``{ok, written, failed: [{figure_id, error}], total}`` or ``{error}``
    when the batch was refused before anything was written.

verified_symbols.name: figure_scale_record
verified_symbols.doc:
Record what a human read off a figure, and report what it unblocked.

THIS IS THE ONLY THING STANDING BETWEEN A BUILT DUAL FIT AND A RUN. The fit
compares a scan extent in nm against a q grid in nm^-1; a figure lifted from
a PDF carries neither, captions were MEASURED not to supply them (of 127
micrograph captions: 28 have none, 26 put the scale in the image, and the 33
with a length are dominated by film thicknesses), and so all 198 candidate
pairs are blocked on two numbers a person can read in seconds.

Append-only, like a classification: readings are newest-wins edges, so a
correction supersedes a mistake without deleting the record of it. Entity
properties in tiled 0.2.15 are create-only, which is why a revisable value
lives on an edge at all.

The reply carries the pair counts AFTER the write, because the number a
reviewer wants is not "saved" but "how much did that unblock" -- and it is
the only feedback that distinguishes a useful reading from one on a figure
whose partner is still missing.

NOT ADMIN-GATED, consistent with ``review_resolve``: one small append that
another append can supersede, not an unbounded spend.

verified_symbols.name: review_queue
verified_symbols.doc:
Figures whose current verdict asks for a human look.

THE FLAG EXISTED AND HAD NO ROUTE. `_review_verdict` computes
``needs_review`` plus ``review_reasons`` on every classification and stores
them on the edge; the only consumers were a warning badge in the figure list
and a training-set exclusion. So "the 84-figure review queue" was a number
someone had derived once, not a thing anyone could open -- and a reviewer had
no way to see the queue, let alone work through it.

Ordered worst-first: `simulated_scattering` verdicts lead, because that is
the class this repo has MEASURED itself confidently wrong on (three verdicts
at 0.85-0.90 that captions corrected to experimental), and then by ascending
confidence.

Args:
    publication_id: Restrict to one paper's figures.
    limit: Cap on verdicts scanned.

Returns:
    ``{queue: [...], count, reasons: {reason: n}}`` -- the reason histogram
    is what says whether a queue is one systematic problem or many
    unrelated ones.

verified_symbols.name: paper_extraction
verified_symbols.doc:
What the extractor actually read out of one paper's figures.

THE COUNTS PANEL CANNOT ANSWER THIS. Ingest telemetry walks one hop off the
publication, and a panel hangs off a FIGURE -- so "12 figures" is the end of
what it can say, and after a backfill that wrote 9,365 panels the honest
per-paper view was still a figure count. This walks the second hop
deliberately, and it is not on a polling path.

ONE PAGED QUERY EACH for the scale and q-range readings, never one per
subject -- the shape that cost the classification skip-set 4,023 round
trips before it was fixed. The panel edges are read per figure, which is
bounded by the figures in ONE paper rather than by the corpus.

Args:
    publication_id: The publication's Tiled entity id.

Returns:
    One row per figure: its panels, and for each panel-or-figure the scale
    and q range attached to it. ``extraction`` says whether the figure has
    been read at all and what the pass concluded -- a figure with no panels
    and no readings has usually been read and found to have none, and that
    is a different fact from never having been looked at.

verified_symbols.name: classify_figures
verified_symbols.doc:
Triage paper figures into experimental / simulated / other.

Writes one ``forge:classifiedAs`` edge per figure, carrying the model,
prompt version, confidence and a ``needs_review`` flag. Storage is
append-only, so re-running under a newer prompt adds a verdict rather than
overwriting the old one -- the disagreement between prompt versions is the
signal that a prompt regressed, and destroying it would hide that.

NOT gated behind the admin key. It spends vision-model time, but bounded by
``limit`` and by the corpus itself, and it writes only edges that a re-run
replaces rather than anything a page reload cannot undo -- which is the line
the four gated routes sit on.

Returns:
    Counts and a per-figure list. ``skipped_missing_image`` is separate from
    ``failed`` on purpose: the first needs the paper re-ingested, the second
    needs the model looked at.

verified_symbols.name: paper_subgraph_route
verified_symbols.doc:
One paper's neighbourhood, as a drawable subgraph.

THE COUNTS CANNOT ANSWER THIS AND NEITHER CAN THE GRAPH VIEW. Ingest
telemetry walks one hop and a panel hangs off a FIGURE; `/api/graph/full` is
the WHOLE graph, ~21 MB and a minute, before anything can be focused. This
walks the paper's own edges: `_edges_touching` for the hub, batched `walk`
for the fans, `newest_link_properties` for the two reading predicates small
enough to fetch whole. Never `views._load()`.

Args:
    publication_id: The publication's TILED UUID -- not a DOI and not a
        catalog path. `resolve_fast` defers on an unknown path prefix and
        `literature/` holds two entity types, so a non-UUID ref would fall
        back to the whole-graph load this exists to avoid.
    depth: 1 the paper's own children; 2 adds panels, readings, quantities
        and quotations; 3 also links a quotation to the section it came from.
    mentions: ``"typed"`` keeps materials and techniques; ``"none"`` skips
        that hop -- the most expensive one and the least often wanted.
    text_chars: Section prose to include. Zero ships none.
    max_nodes: Draw no more than this, shedding the least structural first.

Returns:
    `nodes`, `edges`, `groups`, `stats`, `glossary`, `entityColors`, and the
    honesty fields `truncated`, `truncated_at`, `dropped`, `requests`.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 for an unknown or non-publication id; 503 when the
        graph could not be read. NOT a 200 carrying an empty graph -- the
        graph IS the answer here, so there is no degraded version of it,
        and a paper drawn with no figures because the service blinked is a
        claim about the corpus.
verified_symbols.signature: publication_id: str, depth: int=2, mentions: str='typed', text_chars: int=0, max_nodes: int=600

verified_symbols.name: extract_figures
verified_symbols.doc:
Read panels, scale bars and q axes out of paper figures.

Writes, per figure: `forge:hasPanel` to each panel it finds, `forge:hasScale`
and `forge:hasQRange` on whichever subject the reading belongs to, and
ALWAYS one `forge:hasExtraction` recording that this version looked --
including when it found nothing, because otherwise "already read, found no
scale" and "never read" are the same absence and a re-run cannot tell them
apart.

GATED BEHIND THE ADMIN KEY, where `classify_figures` beside it is not. The
difference is what a re-run undoes. A classification appends an edge that a
later verdict supersedes; this MINTS ENTITIES -- roughly two panels per
figure across 4,028 of them -- and a page reload does not undo an entity.

Returns:
    Counts and a per-figure list. ``skipped_missing_image`` is separate from
    ``failed`` on purpose: the first needs the paper re-ingested, the second
    needs the code looked at.

verified_symbols.name: analyze_figure
verified_symbols.doc: Analyze a single paper figure using the vision model. On-demand only.

verified_symbols.name: read_upload_limited
verified_symbols.doc:
Read an entire upload, refusing once it exceeds a byte cap.

Checks the multipart-reported size first for a cheap early refusal, then
enforces the same cap on the actual chunked read -- the reported
``file.size`` is client-controlled and cannot be trusted alone (some
clients omit it, and a lying Content-Length shouldn't be relied on).

Args:
    file: The incoming upload.
    max_bytes: Override for the cap; defaults to the current value of
        :data:`MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (looked up at call time, not import
        time, so tests can monkeypatch the module constant).

Returns:
    The full upload body.

Raises:
    fastapi.HTTPException: 413 if the upload exceeds the cap.

verified_symbols.name: MaxBodySizeMiddleware
verified_symbols.doc:
Pure-ASGI middleware capping the size of any incoming HTTP request body.

Wraps ``receive`` to count bytes as ``http.request`` messages arrive; once
the running total exceeds the cap, the wrapped callable raises an
``HTTPException(413, ...)`` instead of returning another chunk. That
propagates up through whatever the framework was doing with the body
(e.g. mid-parse inside Starlette's multipart parser or FastAPI's own
``request.form()``/``request.body()`` wrapper) -- deliberately an
``HTTPException``, not a plain exception: FastAPI's body-parsing wrapper
re-raises an ``HTTPException`` unchanged but converts any OTHER exception
into a generic "There was an error parsing the body" 400, which would
otherwise mask this as the wrong status code. Starlette's own
``ExceptionMiddleware`` (present in every Starlette/FastAPI app) then
renders it as the 413 response -- the downstream route never sees the
oversized request. The ``try/except`` here is a defense-in-depth fallback
for the (normally unreachable) case of a bare ASGI app with no such
exception handling: if the HTTPException somehow escapes all the way
back up to us, render it directly rather than letting it become a 500.

entries.integration_instructions: Enforce total body bound before multipart parsing and bounded stream reads afterward; validate PDF type and safe storage path.
entries.evidence: AST-verified source symbols; selected implementations statically reviewed; runtime behavior not certified

verified_symbols.name: require_admin_key
verified_symbols.doc:
FastAPI dependency admitting only a caller holding the admin key.

Use as ``dependencies=[Depends(require_admin_key)]`` on any route whose
effect cannot be undone by retrying, or that spends money.

Args:
    x_api_key: The ``X-API-Key`` request header, injected by FastAPI.
        ``None`` when the header is absent.

Raises:
    fastapi.HTTPException: 503 if no admin key is configured (fail closed
        -- see the module docstring); 401 if the header is missing or does
        not match. Neither response body, and neither log line, contains
        the expected key or any prefix of it: a 401 that echoed even a few
        characters back would turn this into an oracle.

verified_symbols.name: require_admin_key_strict
verified_symbols.doc:
Admits only a caller holding the admin key, even when the dev bypass is on.

Use ONLY on routes that approve paid spend. The development bypass exists so
a loopback dev box need not re-paste the key into the browser; that is a fair
trade for ``/api/graph/reset`` on a scratch graph and the wrong one for a
route that lets the next request spend money, where a stray
``ADMIN_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=1`` left in a shell must not be enough. This calls
:func:`_check_admin_key` and nothing else -- it never consults
:func:`dev_bypass_active`, so no setting of that switch changes its answer.

Args:
    x_api_key: The ``X-API-Key`` request header, injected by FastAPI.

Raises:
    fastapi.HTTPException: exactly as :func:`require_admin_key` without the
        bypass: 503 when no admin key is configured, 401 on a missing or
        mismatched key, and no response or log line carries key material.

verified_symbols.name: admin_gate_status
verified_symbols.doc:
What the gate will do right now, for a UI that has to decide whether to
offer a button. Deliberately reveals no key material -- only whether a key
is configured and whether the bypass is on, both of which a 401/503 already
tells any caller.

entries.integration_instructions: No inherited development bypass for write routes. Inject host principal/capabilities; public Python client and worker enforce the same authorization boundary.

verified_symbols.name: OriginGateMiddleware
verified_symbols.doc:
Reject a present-but-not-allowlisted ``Origin`` on state-changing ``/api/*`` routes.

Scope: only ``scope["type"] == "http"``, ``method`` in
:data:`_STATE_CHANGING_METHODS`, and ``path`` starting with
*path_prefix* -- GETs and out-of-prefix paths are untouched. Within that
scope: no ``Origin`` header -> pass through; an allowlisted ``Origin`` ->
pass through; anything else -> a 403 JSON response, never reaching route
code.

Deliberately reads the header directly from ``scope["headers"]`` rather
than wrapping ``receive`` (contrast ``upload_limits.MaxBodySizeMiddleware``,
which must inspect the BODY as it streams in) -- the ``Origin`` header is
already fully available before any body is read, so the decision is made
up front with no streaming needed.

Args:
    app: The ASGI app being wrapped.
    allowed_origins: Origins permitted to make a state-changing request.
    allowed_origin_regex: An additional pattern of permitted origins,
        matched in full. Mirrors Starlette's ``CORSMiddleware``
        ``allow_origin_regex`` deliberately, so a service can hand this gate
        EXACTLY what its CORS layer already admits rather than a hand-copied
        approximation. Two lists that are meant to agree and are maintained
        separately do not stay agreeing, and the failure is silent in the
        direction that matters: the gate refusing a legitimate client.
    path_prefix: Route surface to guard. Defaults to ``"/api/"``, which is
        where every mutating route on the browse and assistant apps lives.
        It stays a PARAMETER rather than a constant because a gate whose
        prefix does not match its app is a no-op that looks like
        protection. The app that motivated it was the MCP server, which
        mounted under ``/mcp/``; that app is retired (ADR-3), so today
        every caller passes the default -- the hazard it guards against is
        what justifies keeping it, not the number of current callers.

entries.integration_instructions: Origin checks supplement authentication; they are not a replacement for authorization or CSRF protections.

annotated it, or when the adjudicator is one of its annotators -- the
section-8.4 protocol has a THIRD person adjudicate. The adjudicator's own
edits are the adjudication; they do not make them an annotator.

verified_symbols.name: heading_prf
verified_symbols.doc:
Section-heading P/R/F1 plus reading-order distance over the matched ones.

A predicted heading matches an unused gold heading when the folded text
similarity is >= ``sim`` AND the levels differ by at most ``level_tol``;
the best-similarity candidate wins. ``order_distance`` is the normalised
edit distance between the matched gold indices in PREDICTED order and the
same indices sorted: 0 when the parser read the headings in order.
verified_symbols.signature: pred: Sequence[dict], gold: Sequence[dict], *, sim: float=0.85, level_tol: int=1

verified_symbols.name: box_match
verified_symbols.doc:
One-to-one matching at IoU >= ``iou_min``: recall, precision, mean IoU, pairs.

Gold boxes are taken in order and each claims its best unused prediction.
``None`` entries (a box nobody could place) can never match but still count
in their denominator -- a figure with no box is a figure not found.
verified_symbols.signature: pred: Sequence[PBox | None], gold: Sequence[PBox | None], *, iou_min: float=0.5

verified_symbols.name: caption_accuracy
verified_symbols.doc:
Fraction of gold captions reproduced exactly, and after :func:`fold`.

Multiset matching, so two identical gold captions need two predictions.

verified_symbols.name: table_cell_f1
verified_symbols.doc:
Cell F1 on ``(row, col, folded text)`` -- the cheap proxy for TEDS.

Position-aware on purpose: a dropped row shifts every cell after it, which
is exactly the docling-2.118+ TableFormer regression (dropped rows at the
OTSL max-steps cap) this metric exists to catch.

verified_symbols.name: table_teds
verified_symbols.doc:
Tree-Edit-Distance-based Similarity (Zhong et al. 2020), or -1.0 without ``apted``.

TEDS = 1 - TED(pred, gold) / max(|pred|, |gold|), node rename cost 1 for a
tag/span change and the normalised text distance for a cell whose text
differs. Returns -1.0 -- not 0, not a guess -- when ``apted`` is not
installed, so a missing dependency can never read as a bad parser.

verified_symbols.name: citation_scores
verified_symbols.doc: DOI recall/precision, and title-match recall for the gold refs with no DOI.
verified_symbols.signature: pred: Sequence[dict], gold: Sequence[dict], *, title_sim: float=0.9

verified_symbols.name: mention_prf
verified_symbols.doc:
Mention P/R/F1, overall and per category.

``exact``: same section, same char offsets, same category (multiset).
``normalized``: same category and canonical slug (or folded surface when
the slug is null) -- a SET per paper, since "the paper uses GIWAXS" is one
fact however many times it is written. ``role_aware`` also requires the
role to agree (used_in_this_work vs cited_or_background ...).
verified_symbols.signature: pred: Sequence[dict], gold: Sequence[dict], *, mode: str='exact', role_aware: bool=False

verified_symbols.name: role_kappa
verified_symbols.doc: Cohen's kappa of ``role`` over mentions matched by exact span + category.

verified_symbols.name: relation_prf
verified_symbols.doc: Relation P/R/F1: both endpoints match NORMALIZED and the predicate is equal.
verified_symbols.signature: pred: Sequence[dict], gold: Sequence[dict], *, pred_mentions: Sequence[dict], gold_mentions: Sequence[dict], texts: dict[str, str]

verified_symbols.name: quote_grounding
verified_symbols.doc:
Tally of exact / normalized / not_found, fabrication rate, offset accuracy.

``fabrication_rate`` is not_found / all quotes. It is an UPPER bound on
fabrication: a not_found quote is either a paraphrase or an invention, and
the overlap subset is hand-triaged into the two (section 8.5).
``offset_accuracy`` is over the located quotes that overlap a gold quote
span in the same section: the fraction whose start AND end are within
``offset_tol`` characters of that gold span.
verified_symbols.signature: pred_quotes: Sequence[str], texts: dict[str, str], gold_spans: Sequence[dict]=(), *, offset_tol: int=5

verified_symbols.name: quantity_scores
verified_symbols.doc:
Quantity accuracy: value within tolerance AND unit dimension AND sample equal.

One-to-one; a gold quantity is "correct" when an unused prediction matches
all three. Gold quotes with no value (qualitative claims) are not counted.
verified_symbols.signature: pred: Sequence[dict], gold: Sequence[dict], *, rel_tol: float=0.02

verified_symbols.name: figure_reading_scores
verified_symbols.doc:

* ``panel_kind_accuracy`` -- over every gold panel (an unread panel is wrong).
* ``axis_role/unit/scale_accuracy`` -- over gold axes, matched by ``which``.
* ``qrange_coverage`` -- gold q axes with a range for which the prediction
  gives a range in a convertible unit.

  Å^-1-vs-nm^-1 error the text layer exists to prevent. Target 0.
* ``qrange_endpoint_rel_error_median`` -- over covered, non-unit-error axes.
* ``peak_recall`` -- gold peaks recovered within ``peak_tol`` in a common unit.
* ``orientation_accuracy`` -- over gold panels whose orientation is not

* ``panel_sample_precision/recall`` -- panel->sample links.

verified_symbols.name: krippendorff_alpha_interval
verified_symbols.doc:
Krippendorff's alpha, interval metric, two coders, no missing values.

``rel_tol`` implements the "2 % tolerance" of the agreement table: a pair
within ``rel_tol`` of each other contributes zero observed disagreement.

yardstick. Pass values of ONE quantity kind (or their logs): an interval

verified_symbols.name: slugify
verified_symbols.doc:
The slug for a new entry -- delegated, never reimplemented.

THIS WAS A LOCAL REGEX AND IT BROKE THE SLUG INVARIANT.
`entity_slug` is THE slug function for entity identity in this tree; a
hand-rolled equivalent here agreed with it on short names and diverged on
long ones, because `entity_slug` (via `forge.kg.paths.slug`) caps length
while the regex did not. `tests/kg/test_vocabulary.py::TestTheOneSlugFunction`
asserts `entity_slug(slug) == slug` for EVERY entry, and a
generated entry like the Enlitech solar-cell system produced
`..._enli_technology_co_ltd_taiwan` where the canonical form stops at
`..._enli_technology_co_ltd` -- so the registry became unloadable-by-invariant
the moment v3 was written.

Delegating also means a future change to slug rules reaches generated
entries automatically, which is the whole reason that function is "THE" one.

MEASURED, AND THE PLANNED REWRITE WAS DROPPED. This was slated to reach

verified_symbols.name: check_server
verified_symbols.doc:
"" if the knowledge agent answers at *url*, else why not.

Checked UPFRONT rather than on the first POST: discovering the service is
down after twenty papers have been parsed and seeded is a worse experience
than being told before anything starts.

PROBES `/health`, NOT `/api/graph/summary`, and the difference is not
cosmetic. `summary` aggregates the whole graph, so it gets slower as the
graph grows -- measured at 8.4 s on 6301 nodes, against the 5 s timeout this
used to impose. A healthy service therefore failed its own liveness check and
the run aborted with "the knowledge agent is not answering (timed out)",
which reads as "the service is down" and sent me looking at the wrong thing.
A liveness probe must not scale with the data it is checking liveness for.

600 s IS NOT ALWAYS ENOUGH, measured: three Optics Express papers of 3.7-6 MB
timed out at the default on a real folder while eleven smaller ones finished.
A timeout here is not a failed ingest -- the server keeps working and may
finish after the client has given up -- so it is worth raising rather than
retrying blind, which is why `--timeout` exists.

verified_symbols.doc:
What each publication actually has, read back from the catalog.

MEASURED BEFORE OPTIMISING, AND THE OPTIMISATION WAS NOT WORTH DOING. The
three scans below were slated to become scoped JOINs on the strength of a
1,059 ms / 22.6 MB figure. That figure is real but belongs to the GRAPHQL
path: over this local SQLite file the same reads cost **53 ms for 28,081
entities and 49,919 links**, and loading every section's text -- the biggest
single read in this family -- costs 51 ms for 22.6 MB. There is nothing here
to win, and a JOIN rewrite would trade a plain, checkable loop for a query
nobody can eyeball against the graph.

What DID need fixing is the connection: this opened `catalog.db` READ-WRITE
to run an audit that never writes. On a WAL database a stray write handle
contends with tiled's own writers, and an audit is exactly the thing likely
to be run while an ingest is in flight. `mode=ro` makes that impossible at
the driver level rather than by convention, and `connect` carries the
busy_timeout the fitness gate requires.

verified_symbols.name: load_candidates
verified_symbols.doc:
Every `candidate_term` node, with its id, name and surface.

Args:
    db: The catalog SQLite file, read read-only.
    limit: Stop after this many rows; 0 means all.

Returns:
    ``[{"id", "name", "surface"}]``. Read straight from SQLite rather than
    through the graph API because this is an operator tool over a local
    file and the API's own pager would take minutes for 16,728 rows -- the
    same reason `cluster_candidate_terms.py` reads the catalog directly.

verified_symbols.name: propose
verified_symbols.doc:
Which candidates the widened resolver can now place, and where.

Args:
    candidates: Rows from :func:`load_candidates`.

Returns:
    ``[{"id", "surface", "slug", "name", "category"}]`` for the candidates
    that resolve. A candidate that does not resolve is simply absent.

THE RULE IS NARROWER THAN `_resolve`'S, deliberately -- see the module
docstring. A surface that IS a vocabulary term is skipped, because the
category it was claimed under was never stored and that is exactly the case
where the category decides.

verified_symbols.name: summarize
verified_symbols.doc: Counts an operator needs before applying anything.
verified_symbols.signature: candidates: list[dict[str, Any]], proposed: list[dict[str, Any]]

verified_symbols.name: _canonical_index
verified_symbols.doc:
Every canonical node of *entity_type*, keyed by its `slug` property.

ONE BULK READ PER CATEGORY. `_ensure_canonical` locates a node by scanning
`store.iter_nodes(entity_type)`, which pages the whole typed table
(`tiled_store.py:861` -> `views.iter_entities`, 500 rows a page). That is
cheap once and wasteful 172 times, which is what calling it per row would
do. The index answers the common case -- the node already exists -- without
any read at all after the first.

The `path` basename is indexed alongside the slug because `_ensure_canonical`
accepts either, and a node written before the `slug` property existed has
only the path.

verified_symbols.name: apply_proposal
verified_symbols.doc:
Promote each proposed candidate onto its canonical entity.

Args:
    proposed: Rows from :func:`propose`.
    store: Graph store. Defaults to the configured one; injected by tests.

Returns:
    A report with `migrated`, `failed`, `skipped_not_found` and `errors`.

THE CANONICAL NODE IS FOUND BY ITS `slug` PROPERTY, NEVER BY A CONSTRUCTED
PATH. The first version of this function called
`find_entity_id(row["slug"])`, which takes a catalog PATH and matches on
URI: a bare slug like `rsoxs` derives `metadata/rsoxs` where the node
actually sits at `technique/rsoxs`, and materials are at `materials/<slug>`
-- PLURAL, while technique, analysis and instrument are singular. Every row
would have landed in `skipped_not_found` and the run would have reported
success having promoted nothing.

`vocab_cleanup._ensure_canonical` is the authoritative lookup and is
IMPORTED rather than re-derived, for the reason the corpus ingester gives
for importing the clustering: two copies of a rule drift the first time
either is tuned, and this one already encodes the plural-`materials/` trap.

A slug with no node yet is MINTED, and that is correct: `propose` only emits
a slug that `vocab.match_within` returned, so the target is always a
vocabulary entry. The thing that must never be minted is a slug the
vocabulary does not hold, and that is refused one layer up, in `propose`.

Reuses `forge.kg.repair.merge_shadow_duplicate`, whose ordering is the whole
safety property: every edge is written onto the canonical entity FIRST and
the candidate is deleted only once they are durable, because `deleteEntity`
cascades. A failed edge write aborts that candidate's delete and the run
continues -- one unmigrated candidate is visible and re-runnable, where a
candidate deleted with an edge un-copied is silent data loss.

verified_symbols.name: _content_words
verified_symbols.doc: Lowercased words of *text*, minus stopwords and one-character tokens.

verified_symbols.name: title_agrees
verified_symbols.doc:
Whether *title* is plausibly the title of the document *head* came from.

Args:
    title: Title OpenAlex returned for a candidate DOI.
    head: The PDF's first-page text, as `scan_corpus` kept it.
    needed: Content words that must be present. A short title is accepted on
        all of its words.

Returns:
    True when enough of the title's content words appear on page one.

This is a VERIFICATION, not a similarity score, and it is deliberately
lopsided: a false accept writes this paper's figures under another paper's
DOI, while a false reject costs one paper out of 28,504 an abstract. So it
errs toward rejecting.

Example:
    >>> title_agrees("Nanoimaging Cells Using Soft X-Ray Tomography",
    ...              "NANOIMAGING CELLS USING SOFT X-RAY TOMOGRAPHY  G. McDermott")
    True
    >>> title_agrees("An Entirely Different Paper About Magnetism",
    ...              "NANOIMAGING CELLS USING SOFT X-RAY TOMOGRAPHY")
    False
verified_symbols.signature: title: str, head: str, needed: int=_TITLE_WORDS_NEEDED

verified_symbols.name: plan_lookups
verified_symbols.doc:
Which DOIs to ask OpenAlex about, and which paper each belongs to.

Args:
    papers: Rows from the corpus scan.

Returns:
    ``(dois, by_path)``. *dois* is the de-duplicated ask list, in a stable
    order. *by_path* maps a paper's path to the candidates asked for it --
    one entry for a text-verified DOI, up to six for a filename-derived one.

verified_symbols.name: _record
verified_symbols.doc:
One output row: identity, subject, and the technique profile carried through.

A paper with no OpenAlex record still gets a row. It keeps its technique
profile and its first-page text, which between them are enough to assign a
domain and to ingest -- `add_publication` has an `allow_without_openalex`
path. Dropping it here would silently shrink the corpus by whatever fraction
OpenAlex happens not to cover.
verified_symbols.signature: paper: dict[str, Any], work: dict[str, Any] | None, status: str

verified_symbols.name: resolve_papers
verified_symbols.doc:
Attach OpenAlex metadata to every scanned paper.

Args:
    papers: Rows from the corpus scan.
    batch: DOIs per OpenAlex request.

Returns:
    One row per paper, in input order, each carrying a ``doi_status`` of
    ``text_verified`` (the document printed its DOI and the scan checked it),
    ``title_verified`` (a filename reading that OpenAlex knows AND whose
    title is on page one), ``unverified`` (OpenAlex knows a reading but its
    title does not match the page -- NOT accepted), ``unresolved``, or
    ``quota_paused`` (never asked: the OpenAlex allowance ran out first).

verified_symbols.name: summarize
verified_symbols.doc: Counts a caller needs before deciding whether the resolve was good enough.

verified_symbols.name: _load_scattering_scanner
verified_symbols.doc:
The existing scanner, loaded as a module.

`scripts/` is not a package, so this is how the repo's other script tests
reach a script (see `tests/scripts/test_audit_geometry_parallel.py`). The DOI
recovery here is that scanner's, not a second implementation of it: `fold`
and `recover_doi` encode a rule -- the filename says WHICH characters, the
document says WHERE the slashes go -- that must not exist twice and drift.

verified_symbols.name: _build_pattern
verified_symbols.doc:
Compile the whole term table into one regex, with a group per surface.

One pass over the text rather than 75. Each surface gets its own named group
(`slug__index`) so the matching slug comes back from `Match.lastgroup` with no
second lookup by matched text -- which is what makes prefix terms workable at
all, since the text a prefix matched ("voltammetry") is not the key it was
written under ("cyclic voltamm*").

Returns:
    ``(pattern, group_to_slug)``.

Raises:
    ValueError: If a surface spelling appears under two slugs, or does not
        begin and end with an alphanumeric. Both are silent-wrong-answer
        bugs rather than crashes, so they are refused here.

verified_symbols.name: doi_candidates_from_stem
verified_symbols.doc:
Every DOI the filename could mean, when the text did not say.

These filenames ate every slash, and the registrant prefix is 4-9 digits, so
`10.10021873-3468.12505` reads as registrant `10.1002` with suffix
`1873-3468.12505`, or as `10.10021` with suffix `873-3468.12505`, and so on.
At most six readings exist. Rather than guess one -- which
`scan_scattering_papers` rightly refuses to do -- enumerate them all and let
the stage-1 OpenAlex batch say which is a real work; 50 DOIs ride in one
request, so six candidates cost no extra requests worth counting.

Args:
    stem: Filename without its suffix.

Returns:
    Candidate DOIs, shortest registrant first, which is the common case.
    Empty when the stem is not DOI-shaped at all -- the 42 title-named files.

Example:
    >>> doi_candidates_from_stem("10.10631.4973996")[0]
    '10.1063/1.4973996'
    >>> doi_candidates_from_stem("10.10021873-3468.12505")[0]
    '10.1002/1873-3468.12505'
    >>> doi_candidates_from_stem("Nanoimaging Cells Using Soft X-Ray Tomography")
    []

verified_symbols.name: profile_text
verified_symbols.doc:
Per-technique hit counts for one document's text.

Args:
    text: Extracted text, any case.

Returns:
    ``{slug: count}`` for the techniques that appear at least once, most
    frequent first. Sparse: a typical paper names three to eight.

Example:
    >>> profile_text("Cyclic voltammetry was performed; the CV curves show ...")
    {'cyclic_voltammetry': 2}

verified_symbols.name: scan_pdf
verified_symbols.doc:
Read one PDF and report its identity, technique profile and families.

Args:
    path: The PDF to read.
    max_pages: Stop after this many pages; the last page is read regardless,
        because journals print the DOI in the footer.

Returns:
    A record carrying ``path, stem, sha1, doi, doi_source, doi_candidates,
    pages, head, profile, families, hits, distinct_techniques``. An
    unreadable file returns ``doi_source: "unreadable"`` and an empty profile
    rather than raising: one corrupt document in 28,504 must not end the scan.

verified_symbols.name: _scan_one
verified_symbols.doc: Process-pool entry point. Module level because a closure does not pickle.

verified_symbols.name: dedupe
verified_symbols.doc:
Collapse byte-identical documents, keeping the first path seen.

Args:
    records: Scan records, in a stable order.

Returns:
    One record per distinct content hash, each carrying a ``duplicates`` list
    naming the other paths with the same bytes. Unreadable records (no hash)
    are all kept, since "unreadable" is not an identity.

verified_symbols.name: scan_directory
verified_symbols.doc:
Scan every PDF under *root*, in path order, deduplicated by content.

Args:
    root: Directory to walk recursively.
    max_pages: Pages read per document.
    limit: Stop after this many documents, for smoke-testing.
    workers: Processes. PDF text extraction is CPU-bound, which is the case
        `forge.core.parallel.map_parallel` explicitly says to use a process
        pool for; `scan_pdf` takes a path and returns a dict, so it pickles.

Returns:
    One record per distinct document, in path order -- never completion
    order, so two runs over the same tree produce the same file.
verified_symbols.signature: root: Path, max_pages: int=DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES, limit: int | None=None, workers: int=8

verified_symbols.doc: Counts a caller needs before deciding what to resolve and ingest.

verified_symbols.name: fold
verified_symbols.doc:
Reduce an identifier to alphanumerics, lowercased.

The repo-wide rule for comparing identifiers whose spelling is not stable.
Applied to BOTH sides of every comparison here, never one.

verified_symbols.name: recover_doi
verified_symbols.doc:
The paper's DOI, recovered from its own text and checked against *stem*.

Args:
    text: Text extracted from the document.
    stem: The filename without its suffix, which holds the DOI with every
        separator removed.

Returns:
    ``(doi, status)``. *status* is ``"recovered"`` when exactly one candidate
    in the text folds to the filename, ``"ambiguous"`` when several distinct
    ones do (which should not happen and is reported rather than resolved),
    and ``"not_found"`` when none does -- in which case *doi* is ``""``.

    A candidate is accepted ONLY on a fold match. An unverified DOI is worse
    than none: it names a real paper that is not this one, and every
    downstream write would attach this document's figures to it.

verified_symbols.name: scan_pdf
verified_symbols.doc:
Read one PDF and report its DOI and scattering-term density.

Args:
    path: The PDF to read.
    max_pages: Stop after this many pages.

Returns:
    A record with ``path``, ``stem``, ``doi``, ``doi_status``, ``pages``,
    ``hits`` (total term occurrences), ``distinct_terms``, and ``terms``
    (the per-term counts). An unreadable file returns ``hits: 0`` and
    ``doi_status: "unreadable"`` rather than raising -- one corrupt document
    in seven thousand must not end the scan.

verified_symbols.name: scan_directory
verified_symbols.doc:
Scan every PDF under *root*, most scattering-relevant first.

Args:
    root: Directory to walk recursively.
    max_pages: Pages read per document.
    limit: Stop after this many documents. For smoke-testing the scan.

Returns:
    Records sorted by distinct term count then total hits, both descending.
    Ranking on DISTINCT terms first is deliberate: one paper saying "XRD"
    forty times is a diffraction study, while a paper naming GIWAXS, SAXS,
    reciprocal space and structure factor once each is doing the multi-
    technique work this corpus wants, and a raw count buries the second.
verified_symbols.signature: root: Path, max_pages: int=DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES, limit: int | None=None

verified_symbols.name: summarize
verified_symbols.doc: Counts a caller needs before deciding how deep to ingest.
